*{and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err*} Or, *and* to be *a bridle*, or *a snaffle*; that it may run in the same tenor, with the branch next before it; or, as some, with reference to the former words, *as a flood*, or *a stream overflowing to the neck; and as a bridle, causing to err*, or *wander in the jaws of the people*, to wit, before-mentioned, turning the remainder of them this way, and that way, as he pleases, Jam. 3.3. or forcing them out of the way, that they desired, and intended to go, (their purpose being to Jerusalem) and enforcing them in a scattered manner, wandering some one way, some another, to make what haste they could home to their own country again, ch. 37.7,29,33,34,37. See 2 King. 6.19. Job 12.19,24. Psal. 107.40.

*{a bridle,}* Or *a snaffle*, as some: there are two words used, Psal. 32.9. this here, and that other, chap. 37.29. where our translators render this, *bridle*: as also, Job 30.11. & 41.13. that *bit*, which seems most probable: because said to be put, between the lips, into the mouth: see there; so that this seems to signify properly, *a bridle*, or *rein*: that is *a snaffle*, or *bit*: but this used here, as that there, to comprehend both.

**V. 29.** *{Ye shall have a song, as in the night, when an holy solemnity is kept, and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe, to come into the mountain of the Lord, to the mighty one of Israel*} In the midst of the relation, of the destruction of Sennacherib and his forces, is this passage inserted, foretelling the great joy, that God's people, thereby, delivered from their former fears and afflictions, should conceive, and express thereupon, to wit, such as they used to have at their solemn festivals, when with much mirth and music, they repaired to the Temple, and spent the night also, in singing and chanting there.

*{ye shall have a song*} Heb. *the song shall be to you*. That is, as some, Then *shall ye have a song*: supplied for the better connection; as Job 9.35. Or, as other, *This shall be a song unto you*: conceiving the article to be put for the pronoun. But I suppose it is never so used, with reference to any other thing, save that which the word, whereunto it is joined, imports. I should therefore thus render it, *Such songs*, or, *singing*, then *shall ye have*. *Songs*, for *song*: as 1 Kings 4.32. or, *singing*: as 1 Chr. 6.31.

*{as in the night, when an holy solemnity is kept*} Heb. *as a night*, or, *according to a night of sanctifying a festival*. That is, according to the singing that is wont, in such a night, to be used. For the word of *singing*, is to be supplied, here, from the former branch: as chap. 10.5. (see the note there) and in the next member the like. By *night*; some understand here the night, before the festival day, because their festivals began at even, Exod. 12.18,42. Lev. 23.32. Others, the night following the festival day: in which they made merry, with junkets after supper, and passed the night with all manner of mirth. Of some solemn night-wakes that they used to have in their festivals, see on chap. 12.3. The Jewish doctors hence gather, that it was a Paschal night, wherein Sennacherib's forces were defeated and destroyed. Which that it was done *in the nighttime*, is certain, 2 Kings 19.35. but that it was the Paschal night, is their groundless assertion. Nor is it likely that that night, wherein the deed was done, was so merry a night with them, being not as yet informed of it.

*{gladness of heart*} That is, *hearty gladness*; as Cant. 3.11. Jer. 15.16. When a man is *glad*, as we say, *at the heart*, *Our heart shall rejoice*, Psal. 33.21. & 105.3. Such joy does God require of us in his service, Deut. 16.12,14. & 28.47. Neh. 8.10–12. chap. 58.13. See Psal. 81.1,2.

*{as when one goeth with a pipe*} Heb. *as*, or, *according to one going*, or, *traveling*, as ver. 2. Judg. 5.10. or, *journeying, with a pipe*. That is, like the gladness of one that is going with music to God's house which they used to cheer up themselves with by the way, the journey, sometime, being long, 1 Sam. 10.3,5. Psal. 41.4. & 122.1.

*{a pipe*} The word signifies any sort of *wind instrument, pierced*, or, *bored*, through, whereof it has its name: as these made of wood, or metal, or *hollow*, so as it may be blown through, as those of canes, and the like. Put here for any sort of musical instruments; because such they used in the way, as being lightest for carriage, and readiest at hand, for use. See ch. 5.12.

*{to come into the mountain of the Lord*} Or, *to go unto the mountain of the Lord*, as the particle, (for change the rather here made use of) is used, Gen. 11.4. ch. 9.8. so ch. 2.3. *unto*, not, *into*, to mount Zion, Ps. 84.7.

*{the mighty one of Israel*} Heb. *to the rock of Israel*. So is God frequently styled, Deut. 32.3,31. 2 Sam. 23.3. Ps. 78.38. Howbeit, *by the rock of Israel*, some understand *Zion*, the rock, on which the Temple stood: and it should then be, as oft the same thing, in other terms. But the former may well stand; for they went to meet with God there, Exod. 23.14,17. Ps. 41.1,2. & 63.1,2.

**V. 30.** *{And the Lord shall cause his glorious voice to be heard*} The prophet returns to prosecute the relation of the overthrow of the Assyrians, in a rhetorical description of the manner, how it was done.

*{his glorious voice*} Heb. *his voice of might*, or *magnificence*, or *majesticalness*. That is, *his mighty*, or *his magnificent*, and *majestical voice*. For the word seems to be used in either of those notions, Job 37.22. Psal. 21.5. & 96.6. & 104.1. And by it is the *thunder* signified, called *the Lord's voice*, Psal. 29.3,5,7–9. and *his mighty*, Psal. 29.4. and 68.33. & *powerful*, Job 26.14. and *stately voice*, Job 36.4. From hence also, as also from the passages ensuing, it may be deemed, that though the judgment inflicted upon the Assyrian camp, was put in execution by the ministry of an Angel, Chap. 37.36. Yet it was not executed in a secret and silent way, as that destruction of many thousands, in David's time, by the pestilence, 1 Chr. 21.14–16. or, as that slaughter made of the firstborn, throughout all Egypt, Exod. 12.12,23,29. Heb. 11.28. but by raising a mighty storm and tempest, accompanied with dreadful thunder and lightning, wherein so many thousands of Sennacherib's soldiers miscarried. See the like, Ps. 18.12–14. & 77.17,18. ch. 29.6. Zach. 9.14,15. This seems rather to be here intended, than as some, an allusion to the voice of a commander, inciting, and encouraging his forces to fight, Joel 2.11.

*{and shall show the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a devouring fire; with scattering, and tempest, and hailstones*} A further description of that horrible and hideous tempest, wherewith the Assyrians were surprised.

*{and shall show the lighting down of his arm*} The word rendered, *lighting down*, is supposed to signify, sometime, *descension*, though there be no clear place produced for it: sometime, *rest*, and so it is oft used, Job 17.16. Prov. 29.9. Eccl. 4.6. & 6.5. Nor do I see, why it may not well be so taken here; as Damascus is said to be the *rest*, or *resting* place of God's wrath, Zach. 9.1. God will in a most conspicuous manner, cause his revenging power (that is, his *arm*, here; as chap. 48.14. & 52.10.) to light on, and to rest upon them. See ver. 32.

*{with the indignation of his anger*} Heb. *in indignation of anger*. Two words, much of the same notion, joined together, as before, ver. 26. Ch. 7.4. & 13.13. Lam. 2.3,6. to express an excess of wrath, manifested in this their destruction. God will do it, as in a most conspicuous, so in a most fierce, and wrathful manner; that it may be seen, both who does it, and in what manner it is done. See chap. 26.11.

*{and with the flame of devouring fire*} As chap. 29.6.

*{scattering*} Or, as some, *lightning*: so termed, because it pierces into, and violently rends, and breaks asunder. For the word seems to have in it a notion, not so much of *dispersion*, as of *dissipation*, or breaking to pieces; as chap. 27.9. And hence comes the word, for an *hammer*, that breaks things to pieces, Jer. 51.20.

*{hailstones*} Heb. *stone of hail*; *stone*, for, *stones*; as Hab. 2.11. See Josh. 10.11. chap. 28.2. Psal. 18.12. Thus also it is, by some, deemed, that God disturbed the Egyptian at the Red Sea, with a storm of the like condition, with that here described, Exod. 14.24.

**V. 31.** *{For by the voice of the Lord shall the Assyrian be beaten down, which smote with a rod*} Or, *By the voice of the Lord shall the Assyrian be terrified*; or, *affrighted*, ch. 20.5. & 31.4,9. Mal. 2.5. spoken of Sennacherib, especially, who though not slain, at present, yet was so affrighted, with what he heard and saw, that he durst not stay by it, ch. 31.8. & 37.37. Or, if of his army, rather, *broken in pieces*, and dissolved; as Ch. 7.8. which at length, also, befell himself, ch. 37.38. See ch. 31.8. & 33.3.

*{which smote with the rod*} Whom God used as a rod, to chastise his children, chap. 10.5,6,20. a defect of the relative; as ver. 14.28. Or, as others, *with the rod will he smite him*: that is, *God will smite* him; or, *he shall be smitten*: as ver. 14.23. See chap. 10.24. with *the rod of iron*, that shall break him to pieces like a potter's vessel, Psal. 2.9. The text will bear either: and this latter fits well with what follows, ver. 32.

**V. 32.** *{And in every place where the grounded staff shall pass, which the Lord shall lay upon him, it shall be with tabrets, and harps*} Heb. *Every passage of the founded staff, which God shall make to rest on him, shall be with tabrets*, or, *drums, and harps*.

*{grounded staff*} The *rod* spoken of, vers. 31. which shall not pass, slightly over them, giving of them a wipe only by the way; but shall be fixed and founded; as chap. 28.16. it shall stick surely by them, as a rod, or scourge, that enters into the flesh, and makes therein a deep impression.

*{shall lay upon him*} Or, *make to rest on them*. The word being collective, ver. 31. It shall not be, as with God's own people, on whom *the rod* does *not rest*, Psal. 125.3. but it shall stick by them, and rest on them, till it make an end of them, Zach. 9.1. ver. 31. Yet there want not, that expound this of the rod, wherewith, by God's appointment, the Assyrian had smitten them, that in all such places, there should now be much joy, ver. 29. See more on the next clause.

*{with tabrets, and harps*} This passage is exceedingly pestered with variety of expositions: some by the *tabrets and harps*, understand those sacrifices, which were offered with some kind of solemn music, Numb. 10.10. Psal. 81.1,2. to that purpose, drawing in hither from the next branch, the word of *shaking*, which they apply to the *shake-offerings*, Levit. 8.30,34. or to the lifting up of the hand in prayer, Psal. 141.2. and so the sense should be, that the Assyrian should be fought with, and prevailed against, by sacrifice and prayer, 2 Chr. 32.20,21. Others, that the Angels shall exceedingly rejoice, and make melody, that they were sent upon such an employment; and hither they strain the *shakings*, after mentioned, as implying the agitation of the hand, in the use of hand instruments. Others, of God's coming to battle against the Assyrian, in a triumphant way, as being sure of victory beforehand, and going forth to fight in such manner, as conquerors use to be entertained, when they come home from fight, as conquerors Judg. 11.34. 1 Sam. 18.6. Others, of the public joy and triumph, that should be in all places, where this miraculous overthrow had been wrought, as was after the overthrow of the Egyptians in the Red Sea, Exod. 15.1,20. Psal. 66.6. so 2 Chr. 20.28. Psal. 59.10. & 68.25. Jer. 31.4. And this should I incline to, but that this whole verse seems to run still upon the defeat, and the overthrow itself. Others, therefore, of those, that by music and merriments should seek to avert the rod of God, and either the dread, or the smart of it, as kings assay oft to do, that God will set, in a furious manner, upon such. Others, lastly, suppose that as we now use *drum* and *fife*, so the Jews, and other Eastern people, in those days, used *tabor*, and *harp*, in battle: and that thereunto the prophet should here allude, as intimating that with *tabrets* and *harps*, indeed; but other, than such as they used, to wit, thunder and lightning, and storm and tempest, and hailstones, instead of such, would God come to war against them, ver. 30. and the very noise of his warlike drums, and military music alone, should be sufficient, both to daunt and to destroy them, v. 31.

*{and in battles of shaking will he fight with it*} Or, *against them: battles of shaking*. That is, say some, by a kind of inversion, *agitation of war*: thereby understanding the enemy, who had destroyed God's people, and whom God would now destroy. Or, as others, rather, *battles*, wherein God will show his power, by *shaking* them to nothing *in the sieve of vanity*, before spoken of, ver. 28. which some of the Jewish doctors suppose here alluded to. Or, with the *lifting* up, and *shaking* of his hand over them, ch. 11.15. & 19.16. (in another manner against the Assyrian, than he formerly shook his hand, at Jerusalem, chap. 10.31. which may here be glanced at, as another of them intimates) *will he fight with it*; that is, as some, with the *rod*, before spoken of, ver. 31. Or, as one of the Rabbis, with the Assyrian *camp*. Or, *with her*, that is, with *Assur*, or, *Assyria*: for the names of countries, are commonly feminine in Hebrew: see ch. 15.1. Some render it, *with them*, or *against them*; as Exod. 14.25. Psal. 55.18. & 66.2. that is, with the Assyrians, supposing the word collectively taken, ver. 31. and the country put for the people. See ch. 31.8,9. The whole verse may well be rendered, as one of the Jewish commenters well observes; *And it shall be*, that in *every passage of the staff*, (that is, in every place, whereby it passes) *which God shall cause to rest on them, with tabrets and harps, and warlike shakings, will he fight against them*.

**V. 33.** *{For Tophet is ordained of old, yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep, and large*} The prophet closes up this prediction of the Assyrians' overthrow, with a rhetorical relation of what manner of place God had prepared for the execution of them, and in what manner, therein, they were to be dealt with. That which some understand, only of their destruction, here: others, of their torment, only, hereafter, in hell. A middle sort of the former, but not without reference also, to the latter; with whom I concur.

*{Tophet*} Heb. *Tophte*: With addition of a letter; which is not therefore always, a note of honor, or respect, as some have said. But it is, ordinarily, elsewhere termed, *Tophet*. And it is the name of a place, in the valley, lying on the south side of Jerusalem, Josh. 18.16. sometime belonging to one *Hinnom*, then owner of it, and after him to a son of his, and his posterity; in regard whereof, it is called sometime, *the valley of Hinnom*, Hebrew, *Gehinnom*: whence the Greek, Γέεννα, and the Latin, *Gehenna*. Sometime, *the valley of the son of Hinnom*, 2 Chr. 33.6. & Jer. 7.31. both Josh. 15.8. & 18.16. And sometime, *the valley of his sons*, 2 Kings 23.10. In this vale, stood *Tophet*, wherein the idolatrous Jews used to burn their children, in sacrifice to an idol, called *Moloc*, Levit. 20.2. 2 Chr. 28.3. & 33.6. And it had that name from the *drums*, or, *tabrets*, that their idolatrous priests used to beat upon, at the time of their detestable services, to drown the shrieks and cries of the poor sacrificed children. For it seems but a fancy, which one of the Rabbis here has, that it should be termed *Tophte*, from a word signifying *to entice*, or *seduce*; because everyone that is misled by his own concupiscence, (Jam. 1.14.) goes down thither. But this place, was by Josias, in detestation of the horrid acts therein committed, not destroyed only, but defiled, 2 Kings 23.10. Made a common laystall for the city, where dung and filth lay continually reeking; and it became afterward, a common place of burial, for the meaner sort, especially, of the people; and persons (as some say) executed by the hand of justice, which were not, ordinarily, suffered to lie unburied, Deut. 21.22,23. Also it is, by some, affirmed, that there such were burnt, who by the law, were to suffer that kind of death, Levit. 21.9. And further, that in some notorious crimes, the bodies of the persons executed, were thither thrown out; as to the *Scalæ, Gemoniae*, at Rome; and there lay without burial; as to Jehojakim was threatened, Jer. 22.9. until the flesh being rotted and wasted, the bones remaining of them, were there burnt: alluded unto, as they suppose, in the *Gehenna of fire*, (for so the words are) as a higher degree of *judgment* or penalty, in capital crimes, Mat. 5.21,22. And it is used, as in the writings of the Rabbis, so in the Scripture of the New Testament, for *Hell*; whereof it is a type, not unfit, Mat. 18.8,9. & 23.15. Mark 9.43,44. But what is specially meant by, *Tophet*, here, is questionable; among those especially, that understand it of some place, wherein this execution was done here upon earth. Of these some are of opinion, that in the vale of *Benhinnom*, this execution was done; the Assyrian camp, a great part of it, lying thereabout; or that there the Jews buried, or burnt the carcasses of them, as Ezek. 39.11,15. But this is of no certainty, nor great probability. See on ch. 37.36. Others therefore understand it of a tropical *Tophet*, a place that should be as a Tophet to them; that wheresoever they should lie encamped, when God's executioner should come to do his office with them, and to execute his master's doom upon them, that place should prove such a Tophet to them, as the prophet here describes. See ch. 66.25. and see of *Ariel*, somewhat the like, ch. 29.2.

*{ordained*} Fitted and furnished, as ch. 21.5.

*{of old*} Heb. *from yesterday*: which phrase is used, sometime, for some short space of time past, as *we are, but of yesterday*, Job 8.9. *thou camest but yesterday*, 2 Sam. 15.20. sometime, without any such restriction, as 1 Sam. 10.11. *those that knew him by yesterday*: that is, in time past, or beforetime: and so here. Howbeit, that fancy of the Jewish Doctor is too nice, who because the phrase, in Hebrew, of a thing past, runs commonly in those words, *yesterday, and the third day*, past, Gen. 31.2,15. Exod. 4.10. & 5.7,14. Josh. 4.18. would have here by *yesterday*, meant the second day of the creation, on which they hold that *hell* was made, which had an yesterday, indeed before it, but no third day. But to let pass the groundlessness of the conceit, he might have found the phrase used single, as here, so elsewhere, in the places above recited, and Mic. 2.8. So also, Heb. 13.8.

*{it is prepared*} So of hellfire, Mat. 25.41.

*{for the king*} For the King: which being understood of hellfire, there is no scruple of it; or, if of some place of destruction here on earth, in general, then his Temple proved his Tophet, chap. 37.38. But he escaping that tempest, that swept away so many thousands of his army, the question is, how it is said, to have been prepared for him. To evade, rather than to assoil this, some would have the words read, not *prepared for the King*; but *prepared by the King*: and the old Latin so renders it: some, by the King, understanding *God*, that *great King*, Mal. 1.14. *the King of the whole world*, Psal. 47.7. Others, King Ezekiah, who, say they, had purged that place, and voided it of those superstitious and idolatrous instruments and monuments, that it was packed and pestered with before, among those other trash and abominations of the like kind, which he is said to have taken away, 2 King. 18.4. and so made it a fit place to receive the Assyrian carcasses: not that he intended any such thing, in so doing; but that, by that work of his, it was made as fit for such an use, as if it had been of purpose thereunto designed. See the like, Mat. 26.12. But of such use of the particle, there is no example. Others therefore, retaining the received, and right reading, understand it, *for the King*, that is, for the forces he brings with him, and in whom he sustains loss, being thereby, both disappointed of his purpose, and much weakened in his power; as David suffered deeply in the diminution of his people; and it is said, therefore, to be done to him, 2 Samuel 24.12–15. or, as others, understanding the word collectively, *King*, for *Kings*, as Proverbs 25.3,4,5. for those *Kings* that serve under him, and those his commanders, whom he counts as kings, Chap. 10.3.33. see Chap. 31.8,9.

*{he hath made it deep and large*} Heb. *he hath deeped, he hath broaded*: that is, *made it deep*, and *broad*; capacious enough to receive as many as are designed to it: a defect of the person agent herein. Ezekiah, say some; others, God. It may be understood indefinitely, *it is made deep* and *broad* enough, as vers. 14. a defect of the pronoun, as Chap. 28.20,28. of the copulative, as chap. 27.4.

*{the pile thereof is fire and much wood*} Heb. *the pile thereof, fire and wood abundance*. See the like, Ezek. 24.9–10. he seems to allude to those piles of wood, that were used and spent there, in their cruel and inhumane sacrifices, or in the burning of bodies, and other abominable things there, when it came to be for either purposes employed.

*{the breath of the Lord, as a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it*} See v. 28. He seems to allude to that shower of *brimstone*, wherewith Sodom was destroyed, Gen. 19.24. so Ps. 11.6. beside, that all lightning is of a sulfury savor; any sudden destruction is compared to a great fire, that in an instant consumes any combustible matter. In somewhat the like manner is the destruction of Sennacherib's army, described, ch. 10.16–18.

*{kindle it*} Heb. *burneth*, or *fireth it*: see of the Leviathan, Job 41.18–21.

### CHAPTER 31

**V. 1.** *{Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help*} This chapter contains another sermon, or prophecy, of the same subject with the former; and consists, partly, of a severe denunciation of destruction to those that were still obstinately bent to seek succor from abroad, from Egypt especially, and relied upon human helps, ver. 1–3. and partly, of a gracious promise of protection from God, unto all those, for their comfort and encouragement, that should constantly rest on him, or sincerely return to him, v. 4–7. together with a prediction of the Assyrians' overthrow, vers. 8,9.

*{Woe*} As ch. 30.1.

*{go down to Egypt*} Whither God had forbidden them to return, Deut. 17.16. & 28.68. Hos. 11.5. partly, that they might not seem to slight, or forget the benefit of their deliverance thence; and partly, also, yea, principally, that they might keep free from the superstitions, and idolatries, of that place and people, Jer. 2.17,18. See chap. 30.1,2.

*{for help*} Against the Assyrians, 2 King. 18.21. Chap. 30.6,7. and 36.8. as after, also, in process of time, for succor, Jer. 37.5. and for shelter against the Chaldeans, Jeremiah 43.5–7.

*{and shall stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong.}* See Chap. 30.16. Ps. 20.7.

*{stay*} See ch. 30.12.

*{they are many*} Heb. *a multitude*, as ch. 1.11. to wit, there; in Egypt where was both store and choice of them, Deut. 17.16. 1 King. 10.28,29. Ezek. 17.15.

*{they are very strong*} Or, rather, *very many*, as before: so the word is most commonly used in the Hebrew, though the other way, in the Syriac: see Ps. 40.5,13. & 69.5. & 139.17. Jer. 5.7. & 15.8. & 30.14,15.

*{but they look not to the holy one of Israel, nor seek the Lord*} Without whom, all help of man, or horse, is vain and helpless, Psalm 33.16,17. & 60.11,12. & 108.12. Prov. 21.31. See chap. 30.1,2.

*{look not*} Up to God, as ch. 17.7. See ch. 22.11.

*{seek the Lord*} Either by asking advice of him, 1 Chr. 15.13,14. ch. 38.2. Or by craving help and assistance, by prayer and supplication, from him, chap. 55.6.

**V. 2.** *{Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words;}* God is too wise, for them to go beyond with their projects; wherewith they shall not be able to prevent, or avoid that evil, which he is peremptorily purposed and resolved to bring upon them, as has already been foretold: see ch. 28.15,17,18. & 29.15,16.

*{Yet*} Heb. *And*: as ch. 8.10. & 29.2.

*{he*} The Lord, v. 1.

*{also wise*} Yea, *only wise*: 1 Tim. 1.17. Jude 25. and all their wisdom is folly to his, 1 Cor. 1.25. & 3.19. Job 5.19. and 12.13,16.

*{bring evil*} Affliction and destruction upon the obstinate wicked, for the evil of their ways, chap. 45.7. Jer. 11.11. and 18.11.

*{call back his words*} Heb. *remove*, as chap. 48.9. or *withhold*, or *withdraw*, Prov. 4.26. or *revoke*, and frustrate, leave undone, as Josh. 11.15. *his words*, what he has spoken, as Esth. 5.5. Psal. 103.20.

*{but will arise against the house of evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity*} He will raise up himself though he now seems not to look after them, and destroy the wicked, for all their helps and supports; yea, both them, and their aids together, v. 3.

*{but*} Heb. *And*: as ch. 30.20.

*{arise*} In hostile manner will I raise up myself, Psal. 9.19. & 12.5. See ch. 28.21.

*{against the house of evildoers*} That is, against Egypt, say some; but that is the help, in the next branch: against Israel, the ten tribes, say others: but this prophecy concerns not them. Rather, therefore, that family, if there be meant, some one special family, that had a principal hand in this project: or those families that had: or that malignant and rebellious people, considered as a body, or a family: of whom, chap. 30.1,9. So Ezek. 2.5,8. See v. 6.

*{the help*} Egypt, from whom they sought help, and that should assay to succor them, ch. 30.7.

*{workers of iniquity*} Or, *wrongdoers*, the common description of the wicked ones in Scripture, Job 34.5,22. Psalm 5.5. and 6.8. and 14.4. and 18.2. and 36.12. & 64.2. and 92.7,9. & 94.4,16. ch. 59.4.

**V. 3.** *{Now the Egyptians are men, and not God*} And unable therefore to help, or prevail against God, Ps. 9.20. & 60.11. see Ps. 52.9,7. Ezek. 28.9.

*{Now*} Heb. *And*.

*{and their horses flesh, and not spirit*} *Flesh*, in Scripture, is used, as a note of infirmity and frailty, Psal. 79.39. 2 Chr. 32.8. Jer. 17.5. Heb. 5.7.

*{not spirit*} Nothing like, in regard of power, to *a spirit*; one of whom, is able to do more, than many millions of horse, or men, can do: how many thousands did one Angel destroy suddenly in the Assyrian camp? Ch. 37.36. how many millions did one in an instant of time dispatch in the land of Egypt? Exod. 11.29,30.

*{when the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down: and they all shall fail together*} Or, *And when the Lord shall stretch out*, or *put out his hand, the helper shall stumble, and the holpen shall fall, and they shall all fail together*. Heb. *And the Lord shall stretch out his hand, and the helper shall stumble*, &c. That is, by a common Hebraism, when the one is done, the other shall be. So 1 Sam. 17.34.

*{stretch out his hand*} The bare putting out of God's hand, shall be sufficient to overthrow, both all your own forces, and theirs also, that offer to assist you: so Jer. 15.6. Zeph. 2. v. 13.

*{both*} Heb. *And*. So 17.26. but here rather (if it be needful to express it) *then*: as ch. 6.1.

*{he that helpeth shall fall*} Heb. *stumble*. Psal. 27.2. See Chapter 3.8.

*{fail*} Or, *perish*, Job 4.9. Ps. 37.18. & 71.13.

**V. 4.** *{For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me*} Or, *Howbeit*, or *Notwithstanding*: as ch. 9.1. Job 5.7. because here begins the comfortable part of this prophecy; the gracious promise of protection. Albeit, that God intends thus to destroy both the Egyptian aids, and those that seek to them, for succor, against the Assyrian: yet will he not suffer the Assyrian to surprise Jerusalem: but he will protect it, against him, and destroy him. The like introduction, see chapter 21.16.

*{Like as the lion, and the young lion, roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof*} God will protect Jerusalem, no more regarding the multitude of the Assyrian forces, than some fierce lion, in the prime of his strength, will regard a company of shepherds, that shall assay to rescue his prey from him. See Mic. 5.8.

*{Like as*} Or, *Like as when:* for the one is frequently included in the other: see Est. 2.20. ch. 64.2. Jer. 5.26.

*{a lion, and a young lion*} Or, *a lion, even a young lion:* as chap. 1.6. or *a lion, or a young lion:* as Exod. 21.15. 1 Sam. 17.34. See ch. 30.6.

*{roaring over his prey*} Heb. *shall roar;* or rather *murmur, mutter, grumble,* or *gruntle.* The lion roars not, when he has his prey; as of the ox, and the wild ass, Job 6.5. but when pinched with hunger, for want of it, he is ranging after it, Ps. 104.21. or has it now, hasting to seize on it, in his eye, Amos 3.4. Chap. 5.29. but being possessed of it, he is in another, a new note, in a grumbling, or gruntling tone, over it; especially upon the approach of any that attempt to get it away from him: for such a kind of voice does the word, here used, imply, ch. 38.14. & 59.11. See ch. 8.20. Jer. 2.15. & 25.30.

*{on his prey*} Or, *over it:* as 1 Chr. 21.16.

*{when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him*} Or, *against whom a full company of shepherds is called out.* Heb. *whom a fulness of shepherds is called against him: a fulness,* for *a multitude:* as Gen. 48.19. or, *a full company:* all that the town or village is able to make out: as *the fulness of the world,* for all that is in it, Psal. 24.1. *whom against him,* for *against whom:* a common redundancy, Gen. 1.21. Ps. 1.4. Jer. 1.2.

*{is called forth against him*} Or, as some read it, and so the old Latin, *shall meet with him:* and so the word is used, Deuter. 22.6. and it may well stand here; which if we admit, the text would be rendered, *with whom a multitude,* or *full company of shepherds, shall meet.*

*{not be afraid*} Or, *daunted:* as Ahaz was, at the rumor of the Syrians' confederacy with Ephraim, ch. 7.7. and as the Assyrians shall be with God's voice, chapter 30.31. where the same word is used.

*{nor abase himself*} As those of Jerusalem, even the king himself, did to the Assyrians, 2 King. 18.14,26. chapter 10.4. & 36.11. Heb. *be humbled,* Psal. 116.10. & 119.67. Eccl. 1.13. Zach. 10.2.

*{for that noise*} Or, *the multitude:* so called, of the noise, that multitudes are wont to make, Chapter 13.4. See Chapter 33. ver. 3.

*{the Lord of hosts*} So ver. 5. able without any foreign aids, sufficiently to defend his, and to discomfit any forces, that shall come against them. See ch. 1.9.

*{come down*} From heaven, as Psal. 18.9. & 144.5. ch. 64.1. by his angel, ch. 37.36. or *go forth* to war; as the word is used, 1 Sam. 23.11. & 29.4. because fights were most in the plain, Exod. 17.9,10. Judg. 4.11.14.

*{to fight for mount Zion*} That is, for Jerusalem, ver. 5. Zion, the principal part of it, the place of God's special residence in his temple, and the king’s in his palace, both there situate, put for the whole city, ch. 1.8. & 37.35. Some read the words, *against Zion:* as ch. 29.3. Hos. 8.1. and the initial particle so taken, as our English renders it, would carry it that way, as rendering a reason of what was said, v. 3. of the Egyptians helping, and the Jews helped by them, both falling together: but the verse next following, shows evidently, that the meaning is not against, but *for,* or in the behalf of it; as the preposition is oft used also, v. 5. and elsewhere, 1 Chr. 6.49. & 29.21. Lam. 5.17,18. Ezek. 27.30. where, *against the,* is against the sense and drift of the place.

*{for the hill thereof*} The *hill,* or *knoll* on which that city then stood: the words here used, rendered *mountain,* and *hill,* are of the same signification, says a Jewish critic: differing only in quantity; the latter, the less. For *mountain,* and *hill,* with us, though in common use, it may seem also so to be: yet if we regard the original, they differ, but as a Latin term, and a Saxon only, both importing the same thing: and that therefore, which is rendered *a mountain* here, is, elsewhere, rendered *an hill,* Ps. 1.6. & 15.1. & 68.15,16. but what is here termed *an hill,* may well be rendered, *a knoll.* For though Sion be termed *a mountain,* or *an hill;* in regard, either of the lower part of the city, standing on the side of it, Ps. 48.2. or in regard of the valley that lay beneath it, yet the rising, or higher ground, on which both the rest of the city, and Sion itself stood, may well be termed, rather, *a knoll* than *an hill,* in regard of those far higher hills that encircled it, Ps. 125.2. See Jer. 17.3.

**V. 5.** *{As birds flying; so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem*} Another similitude, whereby the prophet illustrates God's working for the protection of his people: the former intimated his power and ability to do it: this, as some: his speed and alacrity, to the doing; or, as others, rather, his affection and sedulity in the doing of it.

*{As birds flying*} As fowl are wont to fly, either to their nests with all speed, when they perceive their young ones to be in some danger, or descry any making towards them, so will God come swiftly and suddenly to rescue and deliver his, Psalm 18.10. (the flight of fowl being an emblem of swiftness, Deut. 28.49. Hos. 8.1.) or, about their nests, fluttering over their young ones, to succor and shelter them, when any offer to seize on them; and flying to and fro on every side, to keep those off, what they can, that come to annoy them: so will God hover over those of his, that trust in him, and depend upon, to save and secure them: and over Jerusalem, in particular, to protect it: in such manner bestirring himself, that the enemy shall, on no side, find opportunity to assault it, Deu. 32.12. Ps. 91.1,2. and it may well be deemed, that the prophet herein alludes, to what the Assyrian had boasted; that he had seized upon the kingdoms of the earth, *as a birds nest,* and none durst *wag the wing* at him, ch. 10.14. but he should find it otherwise there, when he came to Jerusalem, ch. 37.33.

*{will defend Jerusalem*} The word properly signifies, *to fence,* and so to *defend,* by fencing a place round about, as a vineyard, ch. 5.2,5. or *a garden,* Cant. 4.12. which, from thence, has its name: so Psalm 34.7. & 125.2. Zach. 2.5. See chap. 37.35. Zach. 9.15. & 12.8.

*{defending, also he will deliver it*} Heb. *defending, and he will deliver:* a defective speech; for in *defending,* he will defend *and deliver:* of which form of speech, see further, on ch. 59.13. he will assuredly defend, and by defending, deliver it: a defect of the pronoun, as ch. 2. & 28. & 30.33.

*{and passing over, he will preserve it*} Or, rather, (transplacing the copulative, thrust out of his right place, and supplied needlessly, in a wrong one) *passing over,* he will pass over, *and deliver it,* or *cause it to escape.* For the word is of the very same notion with the former; that is, he will assuredly so pass over, as to save, and deliver the city; and withal, to defeat and destroy those that encamp against it, or intend evil to it, as he did sometime in Egypt, when he slew their firstborn, Exod. 12.12. for thereunto, the word used here, seems to allude; though some would have it import no more, than suddenly, as in a passage. But the former, is the rather justly deemed here to be intimated, because the word is nowhere else found in Scripture, used in that notion; but concerning that act of the angel, in Egypt, of which it is thrice used there, ver. 12,23,26. it is used, also, but once only of an *assault,* 1 Kings 18.26. which not unfitly, also, may be applied to God's dealing with the Assyrian camp; by *assault* whereof, he saved the city, ch. 37.36,37.

**V. 6.** *{Turn ye unto him, from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted*} The prophet having propounded to them, God's gracious promise of preservation and protection, does now show them, what course those that had revolted from God, and failed in their loyal carriage to him, must now take, if they desire to have a share in the promised protection; to wit, by returning to him, from whom they had withdrawn themselves; which he, therefore, here exhorts them to.

*{Turn ye*} Or, *Return:* as Jer. 3.1. & 4.1. that it may answer to *Revolt;* some read it, *They shall return:* to wit, moved by the miraculous, both overthrow, and delivery: and so vers. 7. but the form of the verb will hardly bear it.

*{unto him from whom*} Heb. *unto whom,* or *unto which:* which some expound with such supply, as our text has; as designing the person, whom they were to return to: a defect of the antecedent: as Ruth. 2.9. 2 Chr. 1.4. and of the preposition: as ch. 18.7. & 32.2. & 52.2. Others, rendering it, *according* to that *which,* or *according as,* understand it, of the manner, or measure of their return: as your revolt has been deep and great; so let your return be proportionable thereunto: and indeed, so is the particle oft times used, Est. 3.15. Psal. 119.98.154.

*{the children of Israel*} Not the ten tribes; though true of them, Hos. 9.9. as if they were, by their example, warned, and admonished to do better, Hos. 4.15,16. but the people of the Jews, as v. 5.11,16. many, if not the main of them, and too many of the chief among them, had herein been faulty, see v. 1,2. ch. 30.1. and some, therefore, read this, as in the vocative, *Return, according as you have deeply revolted, O ye children of Israel:* which term, he gives them, not to grace them, but to mind them, what they boasted to be, and to tax, and shame them, for not answering the honor and worth of that title, but disgracing the stock they came of, by degenerating from him, whose name they bare. So Chap. 7.13. & 48.1.

*{have deeply revolted*} Heb. *have deepened revolt;* and there is the like phrase, ch. 7.11. as also, not unlike, used in the same argument, Hos. 5.2. & 9.9. This they had done, as by other enormities, so by their seeking to Egypt, and relying on an arm of flesh, v. 1,2. which is a revolting from God, 2 Chr. 16.7. Jer. 17.5. In the word of *depth,* some think there is an allusion to the *depth* of their plots and projects; and digging *deep,* as imagining to conceal them, even from God, ch. 29.15. It may well have some glance that way; but withal, it is not unlikely, that the prophet had a purpose to mind them, both of the grievousness of their defection and delinquency, and of the greatness, also, of the danger, that thereby they had plunged themselves into; as being sunk so deep in revolt, that unless they did rise, and get up again the sooner, by speedy and hearty repentance, returning unto God, from whom they had revolted, they were like suddenly to perish, without hope of recovery. See Pro. 9.18. & 22.14. & 23.27. of the change of the person, *they have revolted,* for *ye have revolted,* See ch. 29.15. & 30.19. v. 7.

**V. 7.** *{For in that day, every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you, for a sin*} Many interpreters understand this of the serious, and sincere repentance, and return of idolatrous persons unto God, testified by the breaking and abandoning of their idols, as chap. 27.9. & 30.22. Some, upon the Assyrian invasion, and before his overthrow, and of them, some conceive a reason to be here rendered, of what was formerly said, *they shall return,* v. 6. Others of them, reading the words, *when in that day;* or *For in that day.* Wherein men shall do thus, then will God stay his hand from proceeding further in judgment against his people, and turn it against the Assyrian, v. 8. chap. 10.12. and so it should come in, as an argument, to induce to repentance, in hope of such an issue. Others after his overthrow, being by that strange work of God, convinced; as of his power and providence; so of their own former sin and folly, and returning now from their idols, to their only true and living God, ch. 10.20. & 17.7. But others, rather, whom I herein concur with, expound it, as foretelling, what would befall all those, that persisted in their idol-worship, and resting on any other helps, save God, and his alone; that then they would cast away their idols, when by woeful experience, they should find, to their cost and smart, that neither their idols, nor their human helps, were able to stand them in any stead. So understood, it is the same, with what he had before, ch. 2.20. produced here, as there also, to persuade to return speedily to God, and to give over resting on such sorry shores, as are not able to support them, ch. 1.31. & 2.20,22.

*{every man*} Heb. *a man;* but so, chap. 9.20. here, the rather, because the verb is plural: whereas, chap. 2.20. it is singular: but there is another word for *man,* and that, also, there collective.

*{shall cast away*} So ch. 2.20. but the same thing, here intimated, by a word, that signifies properly, *to despise,* or *set light by:* so it is rendered, ch. 33.8. Amos 5.21. and because things of no account, are usually refused, rejected, thrown away and the like; hence it comes, that it is rendered sometime, *refuse,* chap. 8.6. sometime, *reject,* 1 Sam. 15.23. sometime, *cast off:* as ch. 5.24. so here, & so *spernere* in Latin, *a se spernit procul.*

*{his idols*} See chap. 2.20.

*{which your own hands made for you*} See ch. 2.8. and of the change of the person, v. 6.

*{for a sin*} Or, *for sin.* To commit that most heinous sin of idolatry. For so it is, chap. 2.20. *to worship,* instead of the true God. So of the golden calf, Moses, *I took your sin,* that is, the idol, wherein you had so grievously transgressed, Deut. 9.21. Or, as a learned writer of ours, and the rather, because there is no preposition in the text, *of sin,* with reference to the word *hands; which your hands of sin;* that is, your most sinful hands, *had made for you.* Of which manner of syntax, that author produces divers examples, Exod. 26.21. Levit. 6.10. 2 Sam. 22.32. Psalm. 35.19. & 71.9. Lam. 4.17. Ezek. 16.27.

**V. 8.** *{Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man, and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him*} As God will deliver Jerusalem, so will he destroy the Assyrians, by the ministry of an angel, that intend, and attempt to destroy that city, having overrun the whole country, round about it, already; and cause their king, for fear, to retire to his own country, with such scattered ones as are left him, ch. 36.1,2. & 37.36,37.

*{the Assyrian*} Heb. *Ashur,* as ch. 10.5. the name, both of the country and people; here put for the king of Assyria, who is said *to fall,* and yet *to flee; to fall* in his forces; to *flee* in his own person. See ch. 30.31,32. & 37.36,37.

*{fall*} Be slain; as 1 Kings 22.20. Psalm 63.10. Luke 21.24.

*{with the sword*} Or, *by the sword;* as Ps. 63.10. *not of a mighty man,* or *a mean man.* (See of the terms, chap. 29.) Not of any man, one or other; (which of Sennacherib himself cannot be said, who was slain by his own sons, chap. 37.38.) but by an angel, to whom *a sword* is here given; as 1 Chr. 21.16,30. Not that he used any such material weapon, but to express his commission, and power to do execution; as the magistrate is said *to bear the sword,* Rom. 13.4. And God's power put in practice, by taking vengeance on his enemies, is called *his sword,* Chapter 34.4,5. and *a mouth to devour* with, is given to this sword, as to the material one, Deut. 32.42. ch. 1.20. Jer. 21.7.

*{but he shall flee from the sword*} Or *for fear of the sword.* Heb. *from before,* or *from the face of the sword* as chap. 21.15. Jer. 35.11. Seeing his forces defeated and destroyed, he shall, for fear of the like, likely to befall him, if he stay by it, betake himself to flight or, as some render it, supplying the note of similitude, which they suppose to be wanting, both here, and ver. 9. *he shall flee, as from the sword:* as if men with swords drawn, were pursuing him. There is a redundancy in the Hebrew: that has some emphasis in it, which our English cannot well express: *He shall flee himself,* or *for himself.* Which though in some other like forms, it may seem to have no such weight; as Exod. 18.27. Yet here seems to be, as if it had been said, *He shall flee for his life;* as of Elias it is said, 1 Kings 19.3.

*{but*} Heb. *and;* as ch. 29.13.

*{and his young men shall be discomfited*} Those of his forces that remain, and escape that hideous storm, wherein so many were slaughtered. For of those, that fell in it, before.

*{his young men*} *His choice young men;* properly; as Chap. 40.38.

*{shall be discomfited*} The Hebrew word, here used, is ambiguous. It may signify, *they shall be unto tribute:* or *they shall become tributary.* And so some here, according therein with the old Latin, expound it; because so it is most commonly used, Gen. 49.15. Deut. 20.11. Josh. 16.10. & 17.13. Lam. 1.1. And this exposition to make good, some say, that some of them pursued, and seized on, were made captives. Others, supposing that to be too much forced; and for that the Assyrians were never tributary, in those times, to the Jews, they deny this to be spoken of Sennacherib and the Assyrians, in Ezekiahs reign, and would turn it, wholly, to the kingdom of Christ. But the prophecy is too clear to be so shifted off. And as for those, that would have it understood of the Assyrians becoming *tributary,* sometime after, first, to the Chaldeans, and then to the Medes and Persians, they stray too far from the story, here intended. Others, therefore, render it. *They shall be unto melting;* for that is the proper notion, and common use of the root, and the signification of another word springing from it, Ps. 58.8. So the meaning is, either their multitude *shall melt* away; as 1 Sam. 14.16. or their hearts *shall melt* within them; as Josh. 2.11. & 5.1. & 7.5. and they shall faint for fear; as chap. 10.18.

**V. 9.** *{And he shall pass over to his strong hold, for fear*} The word, here used, signifies, properly *a rock,* c. 32.2. and in the next places any *strong hold,* or *fort:* because such were usually built upon rocks, and from their such situation, receive much strength. See on chap. 16.1. And for that to such places, in time of trouble and danger, men are wont to retire, and therein much to confide: (Prov. 18.10,11.) Hence by a metaphor, that is called a man's *rock;* wherein his strength consists, and whereunto he trusts, Psalm. 18.2. & 31.3. and 42.9. Some therefore, here, render the words, *his rock,* that is, his strength, says one; his forces which he confided in, says another, shall pass away, that is, shall fail, *for fear shall perish;* as Job 34.20. & 36.12. But others, taking the words in a sense nearer to the native use of it, read the text, some, *His rock for fear he shall pass by,* understanding by *rock,* a stronghold, situate in the frontiers of his country; or as some, *his strong holds,* collectively, and indefinitely; which for fear he should not dare to stay in, but pass by, to arrive at some surer place of retreat, as to Niniveh. Of which others understand the words, and read them, as our English has them, *To his strong hold, for fear he shall pass over:* that is, to Niniveh, his chief city, and of greatest strength; never thinking himself in safety, until he got thither, ch. 37.37. Thus *the wicked fleeth, where none pursueth,* Prov. 28.1.

*{and his Princes shall be afraid of the Ensign*} Some read the words, *his Princes shall be afraid of flight:* That is, as some with the old Latin, *Shall flee with fear;* or, as others, *shall be terrified with the flight* of their king. And it is true, that the word here used, has in sound, some affinity with that of *flight;* whence some ambiguity, ch. 59.19. but never so signifies, voweled, as here. Our version, therefore, is by most sound interpreters, and by the Jewish, generally, here maintained and approved. Howbeit, by *being afraid of the ensign,* some understand here, that they should be so affrighted, that if they espied but an ensign on some watchtower, by the way, (as ch. 30.17.) though within their own country, they should be afraid, as if some troops of soldiers were pursuing them: or, that they should be afraid, as men are wont to be, when they do indeed see an *ensign,* with some hostile forces making towards them. Supposing the note of similitude to be here wanting, as before, ver. 8. Others, that they should be stricken with fear, at the sight of those wondrous *signs,* and miraculous works, that God had wrought for his people. Or rather, (for I find not this word anywhere so used) of the *ensign,* or *standard,* that God, by his angel, had lifted up, in the slaughter of their fellows: for this is spoken of such of them, as had escaped, and survived the bitter brunt of that battle, in which the angel came down, as with *God's standard,* against them. See Exod. 17.15,16. & ch. 59.19.

*{saith the Lord, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem*} Whose residence is at Jerusalem; where his house is, and fire continually kept burning on his altar, in it, Levit. 6.13. which he also therefore will protect, ch. 37.35. or, who there has his furnace and his fire, to burn up his enemies, and the enemies of it, Lev. 10.2. Num. 16.25. Psal. 21.9. Zach. 2.5.

*{fire*} Or, *hearth;* as some render it, Ezek. 5.2. Or, *flame;* as others, ch. 50.11.

*{furnace*} Or, *oven;* as it is rendered, Lev. 2.4. Hos. 7.6,7. or *chimney,* as some render it Lam. 5.10. and so may not unfitly be here expressed, if the allusion be to housekeeping.

### CHAPTER 32

**V. 1.** *{Behold a King shall reign in righteousness, and Princes shall rule in judgment*} Whether this chapter be a new sermon, or prophecy, distinct from the next before, or belong to it, and have dependence upon it, as well it may, yet is not so clear. That the former part of it, contains a description of the righteous and religious government of God's people, under Ezekiah, most concur. In the latter part of it, is a denunciation of judgments to be inflicted on God's people, for some space of time, v. 9,14. with a promise of a removal thereof, after that time expired, and restitution of them to their wonted estate, ver. 14.19. Some suppose, the prophecy to have been delivered in Ahaz his days; foretelling the happy entrance of Ezekiah, his pious son, after the decease of his ungodly father. Others, in the time of Ezekiahs reign, foretelling what manner of government should be in the state, now better purged, and settled than ever before, after the overthrow given to Sennacherib, and the deliverance of them from that distress, that his invasion had put them to, with reparation of the damage, that had thereby accrued unto them. See v. 10.

*{a King*} That is, Christ, say some, the King of his church, Psalm 2.6. Or, Ezekiah; as the Jews generally, and most of ours so Chap. 33.17. Yet a type of Christ, as before him, David, Ezek. 34.24.

*{in righteousness*} As Hos. 10.12. or *according to justice:* that is, justly, righteously; as the like, Lev. 19.15. Ps. 9.8. see Joel 2.23. where the same is: yet some render it, *to justice:* that is, *to do justice:* and after *to judgment,* or *to right:* that is, *to execute judgment,* or *to do right:* but the former seems the plainer.

*{Princes shall rule*} There is a particle in the text, which the Jewish critics deem redundant here; as it is, questionless, in some places elsewhere, 2 Sam. 3.30. 1 Chr. 3.2. & 26.17. Psalm 9.17. & 12.6. Yet some interpreters thus express it, *as for Princes, they shall rule,* as Eccl. 9.4. chap. 59.11. See verse 2.

*{Princes*} Those under Ezekiah, the inferior magistracy being now purged, and well ordered; and such as Shebna was, ch. 22.15. being either removed, or reformed. See ch. 1.26.

*{in judgment*} Or, *according to judgment,* or *right.* See ch. 1.27. not unjustly, by oppression, extortion, bribery, and iniquity, as formerly, ch. 1.23. & 60.18.

**V. 2.** *{And a man shall be, &c.*} The great benefit that shall hereby redound to the people, to wit, the righting and relieving of all those that have been wronged or oppressed, set forth by divers elegant and pregnant similitudes.

*{a man*} This some restrain to Christ: Others, to Ezekiah, the king before mentioned, v. 1. and the like is said of Solomon, Psalm 72.2,4,12–14. a type, also, of Christ: and they read the words, *And that man,* as conceiving a defect of the article, according to the like, Acts 17.31. 1 Tim. 2.5. But that seems, both a groundless, and a needless supply in this place. The word *man,* being here put indefinitely, or distributively: as Chap. 13.14. & 31.7. and has reference to the *Princes* before spoken of, as the Jewish writers well observe: and so the particle in the former verse, if the course of the context be well weighed, is not wholly without weight, the text being thus rendered, *as for Princes* (to wit, governing under the king, 1 Pet. 2.13,14.) *they shall rule according to right;* and (not the king alone himself, but) *each one* of them (also under him) *shall be,* such as is here described; *a man,* for *each one,* or *any one,* is most frequent in Scripture, ch. 2.20. & 3.5,6. & 9.20. & 19.2.

*{as an hiding place from the wind*} Heb. *of the wind:* that is, such a place of covert, as may protect man, or beast, from, or against the violence and injury of wind and weather. See the next branch: the word is nowhere else found, save here, in the singular form, and in the plural, 1 Sam. 23.23. where it is rendered, *lurking places.*

*{and a covert from the tempest*} Heb. *a covert of a tempest:* a defect of the preposition, either *from,* as Chap. 18.7. & 52.2. or *against,* as Psalm 53.5. Chap. 25.4. *tempest* of wind, or water, extraordinary, either in showers, or deluges, ch. 4.6. & 25.4. See Ps. 32.7. & 119.114. ch. 28.17.

*{as rivers of water in a dry place*} Or, *as streams.* (Heb. *divisions,* as ch. 30.25.) *of water in a place of drought.* Heb. *in drought,* or *dryness:* a defect of the noun regent, as chap. 25.5. Ps. 63.1. as streams of water in such a place, which not only moisten the parched ground, & make the place more pleasant and fertile, ch. 44.3,4. but are a mean, also, of much refreshing to the thirsty passenger, ch. 41.17–19. & 43.19,20. See Joh. 4.10.14. & 7.37–39.

*{as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land*} *Shadow,* for *relief, succor,* or *shelter,* Chap. 4.6. & 25.4. because, against the scorching heat of the sun, the shade affords much refreshing, whether from trees, and plants, where such are, 1 Kings 13.14. Jon. 4.6. or where they want, from some high hill, or rock, overlooking the plain.

*{a great rock*} Heb. *heavy,* as ch. 36.2.

*{in a weary land*} As Ps. 143.6. Prov. 25.25. where it is rendered, *thirsty:* see ch. 20.18. & 29.8. where men are weary of traveling through heat and drought, John 4.6. Mat. 11.28.

**V. 3.** *{And the eyes of them that see, shall not be dim*} Or, *closed,* as chap. 29.10. *he hath closed their eyes.* Which some understand, of spiritual light restored by the pure, and clear preaching of the gospel, in the kingdom of Christ, chap. 29.18. and 35.5. Acts 26.18. 2 Cor. 4.6. Eph. 1.18. opposed to the judgment threatened, Chap. 6.9. & 29.10. and that complaint of the condition of his people, chap. 42.19,20. or, as some rather render it, *shall not look* another way; as, *look away from me,* Job 7.19. chap. 22.4. and *look away from him,* Job 14.6. they shall not look another way, when holy things are tendered to them, and wholesome admonitions, are pressed upon them, as their manner formerly had been; and as those are wont to do, who have that presented to their view, which they list not to look upon. See Psalm 18.22. & 119.37,117. or, they shall not now *look aside* after their idols, and other frivolous stays, which they then relied and rested on, refusing to look after their only true stay, Chapter 31.1. but they shall now look unto God, and rely upon him, Chapter 10.20. & 17.7,8. and this latter reading, seems to suit, very fitly, with what follows in the next branch. But whether way we take it, it is not to be doubted, but that in Ezekiah's days, it was fulfilled in those, who by the judgments of God, then inflicted on the land, and sanctified to them, were refined and reformed, Chap. 48.10. See chap. 30.20. & 35.5. The meaning is, that his people (for those, here, are they, that *See,* or, as the word is, the *Seers:* as ch. 42.20. not the *Prophets,* as ch. 30.10.) who had the light of God's word shining brightly among them, and his judgments conspicuously manifested to them, should not now willfully turn their eyes aside from them, or shut them willfully against either, as those, Chap. 26. ver. 11.

*{and the ears of them that hear, shall hearken*} Heb. *attend:* as ch. 21.7. & 28.13. & 48.18: they that before refused to hear any word of God, or message from God, or to hearken to any advice given them by his prophets, from him, ch. 28.9–12. shall then attentively hearken to what is, from God, spoken to them, and readily yield obedience thereunto, ch. 29.18. See ch. 30.21. & 35.5. They seem to carry it too far, and to narrow it no less that restrain it to the people's attentive hearing of Christ, Mat. 7.28. Luke 4.22.

*{those that hear*} As before, God's people, that had God's word among them, and continually sounding in their ears, ch. 42.20.

**V. 4.** *{The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge*} Heb. *hasty:* so also, ch. 35.4. such as were heady and inconsiderate, as fond and foolish persons usually are, shall then be better advised, and by attending to the word of God, come to understand aright the will of God. See Prov. 1.2–7. & 2.2–5. Heb. *understand to know,* or *unto knowledge:* When men so hear, that they understand what is spoken; and by understanding, attain to sound knowledge, Neh. 8.3,8,12. not like those, ch. 6.9. Mat. 13.19. 2 Tim. 3.7.

*{and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly*} Men, by their religious speech, and communication, at which they did but stammer, when they assayed aught before, shall now manifest the inward alteration and change of their hearts, Mat. 12.34,35. or their language, that was before rude, harsh, savage, barbarous, unsavory, unpleasant, shall now be pure, pious, like the language of God's people, seasoned with grace, and pleasing in God's ear, Prov. 15.26. ch. 19.18. Zeph. 3.9. Eph. 4.29. Col. 4.6. See ch. 3.5,6.

*{stammerers*} See chap. 28.11. for this word, nowhere else found: and that there used, differing but in a letter, have near affinity in notion, also, the one with the other: and there is in the word, here, an allusion, either unto those, that out of a natural defect, cannot speak without stammering; or to those, that speaking in some barbarous language, seem so to do, unto those that understand them not, 1 Cor. 14.11.

*{be ready*} Heb. *hasten; make haste:* as ch. 51.14. a good *haste,* or *speed,* far differing from the hastiness, or headiness, of inconsiderate persons, taxed in the branch before going; and implying an inward readiness of heart to vent itself, in such sanctified communication, as is here imported.

*{to speak plainly*} Heb. *to speak neat, elegant,* or *clear* words, or things: a metaphor taken from the clearness of the air, in dry and fair weather, ch. 18.4. and a defect of the subject, as Gen. 42.30. *hard,* Psalm. 12.4. *great,* Prov. 5.16. *right,* for *hard, great, right,* words or things.

**V. 5.** *{The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful*} The prophet, in these words, further describes the happy and well-settled condition of the Jewish state in those times. Some understand the words, as if the meaning were, that men having, in those days, the spirit of discerning, should be able to distinguish between good and evil; yea, between good and bad men, Rom. 2.18. Phil. 1.10. 1 Cor. 12.10. 1 John 4.1. Acts 8.23. Others, of the sincerity and ingenuity of the times, that neither the false prophets should soothe men up, any more in their sins; nor others, for fear or favor, flatter those that were in power and authority, the richer sort, and the great ones, Psalm 49.18. chap. 5.20. Ezek. 13.22. But the most, and best, that in the state reformed, and established, by Ezekiah, after his delivery from the Assyrian invasion, and the recovery of his health, from that deadly disease that soon after surprised him, chap. 38.5,6. having assurance given him from God, both of the continuance of his life, and of his reign in peace; base minded, and evil affected persons should not be now raised, and advanced unto places of honor and dignity, as in his father Ahaz his time, too many had been; whereof, also, some had continued their places, in the former part of his reign, the state being, as yet, unsettled; nor he able, by reason of wars with his neighboring adversaries, to do as otherwise he would: see Psalm 12.8. Prov. 28.22,28. & 29.2.

*{vile person*} The word is, in Scripture, commonly used for *a fool:* as Deut. 32.6. where *wise,* and it, are opposed: as also, in that speech of Abigail, excusing her husband's uncivil and churlish behavior towards David's messengers; *Nabal is his name, and folly is with him,* 1 Sam. 25.25. his name shows what he is, and so some render it here. Howbeit, in the native signification of it, it may seem to import, as our English well renders it, *a vile* person, a man of no worth: like *a withered flower,* or *leaf,* or *branch,* or *plant,* of no reckoning or esteem, ch. 18.1,4. & 64.6. See ch. 14.19. & 27.11. and both *foolish* and *wicked* ones (of whom, also, it is in the Proverbs of Solomon, especially used, and they may well go for the same) are persons of no worth, Prov. 10.20. But in this place, being opposed to a word, that has a notion of *liberality* in it, it seems rather to import *tenacity* and niggardliness; and our ancienter versions therefore render it, one of them, *a niggard;* another, *a foolish niggard:* and it may well be, that the prophet had a glance at the story of Nabal, 1 Sam. 25. and that the very name of *Nabal,* was among them, in those days, as with us, to this day, used as a byword, or a nickname, for *a niggard:* and that the prophet, the rather, made choice of it here; because this, and the other its opposite here, sound somewhat alike, as they lie together in the text; as if he had said, alluding to the names of men, in use formerly; *Nabal shall not be Nadab,* or *Nadib:* for such allusions to names are found in Scripture: as Ps. 144.4. *Adam is like Abel;* and *all Adam is all Abel,* Psa. 39.5,11.

*{shall no more be called*} That is, *shall no more be, to be called;* for *to be:* as chap. 61.3. & 62.11. Mat. 5.9. Luk. 1.32,33. such shall no more get up, and creep into such places, as those titles belong to. Heb. *it shall not be called* to him *liberal;* or *liberal shall not be called* to him; for *he shall not be called.* See the like, Prov. 16.21. chap. 1.26.

*{liberal*} The word indeed imports *freeness, liberality, ingenuity;* as appears by Exod. 25.1. & 35.5. Psalm 68.9. & 110.3. and is used commonly in Scripture, for a *Prince* or a *Lord,* Mal. 1.8. Prov. 17.7. & 25.7. Psalm. 118.9. & 146.3. because such persons should so be, Prov. 19.6. as the word, *Lord,* with us, also in its first original, is said to import: and the term among the Greeks, commonly given to great potentates, implies as much, Luk. 22.15. And so, I suppose, the intent of the prophet here is, that no *Nabal shall be a Nadib;* that is, no *niggard,* or base-minded fellow, *a noble man,* or *a Prince.* Our ancienter translations render it, *gentle; A Niggard shall not be called gentle.* Had they said, *No niggard shall be called,* or *shall be a gentleman,* they had come well near home to the mark.

*{nor the churl said to be bountiful*} Heb. *and to the churl it shall not be said bountiful:* such a word, or term, shall not be given him: it shall not be his title, or his style. So chap. 19.18. & 61.6. & 62.4. See also Job 34.18.

*{churl*} The word here used, and not elsewhere found, seems to be much, if not altogether the same, in sense with the former: the original of it, is uncertain; one of the Jewish critics says, it comes of a word, that signifies, *to contain,* as a measure does, and consequently to measure, ch. 40.12. 1 Kings 7.26. and would have it import one that does all things, as by weight and measure, taking and keeping account of every trifle, and not parting with a grain, or a crumb, above weight or measure, such an one, as with the Greeks is termed, *μικρολόγος* & *Κυμινοπρίστης,* one, as we say, that will cleave a hair. Another of them, though not unwilling to derive it from the same root, but in another notion, as it signifies, *to contain,* that is, keep in, Jer. 2.13. & 6.11. Yet, rather, fetches it from another of no unlike notion, that signifies, *to restrain,* and shut up in prison, which is thence, also, so termed, ch. 42.7. Jer. 32.7. & 37.4. and so it should have, in it, a notion of *tenacity;* and denote one that hoards up his treasure, and keeps it with him, as imprisoned. A third says, it signifies one that has those words rife in his mouth, *mine own to myself:* alluding therein, to a saying they have among them, from Esau's words, to his brother Jacob, Gen. 33.9. of four sorts of men: the first, of those that say, *Mine thine, and thine mine:* and that is, *the way of the world* or the *way of tradesmen:* the second, that say, *Mine mine, and thine thine:* and that is the middle sort, *Esau's way.* The third, that say, *Mine thine, and thine thine own:* and that is the *Chasids* (they might have said the *Nadibs*) *the bountiful man's way.* The fourth, that say, *Thine mine, and mine mine own:* and that is *the wicked man's way.* Now either he meant it of the second, and then the *cilay* should not be so bad, as the *Naval,* as his fellow Rabbi holds: or of the fourth, and then the one may well be as bad as the other, as, in likelihood, there is little difference between them the prophet's manner, being very frequently to deliver the same thing in divers terms. See chap. 57.1.

*{bountiful*} Or, *magnificent,* as some; who with the Jewish critics, supposing this to go a step beyond the former, render that *munificent,* this *magnificent.* It is nowhere else found, save Job 34.19. where some would have it rendered *wealthy,* because they find *needy* there opposed to it, and the abstract form of it, Job 36.19. *wealth.* But they should consider, that it is there coupled with *Princes,* and the needy opposed to either. And I suppose it, therefore, to be as well as the former, a title of honor; and concur with those, who in their versions, exhibit *the noble,* in the one place, and *by nobility,* in the other. The words of the prophet, I conceive should be rendered, to express his mind aright: *nor shall any churl have the title of a Lord,* or the like; the Hebraism, being adjoined in the margin; *and to a churl it shall not be said, Lord;* for so it is pointed in the text: he shall not be saluted by, or graced with any such title of honor. For how the word should come to signify *bountiful;* or, as some would have it, but in the better part, *prodigal:* to have it a degree above *liberal,* I see not: nor do I well understand, what should move some translators of great note, to render it *noble,* in Job; and *liberal* here.

**V. 6.** *{For the vile person will speak villainy*} In this verse, and the next, I conceive a reason rendered, why such should not, nor indeed ought to be, admitted into place of office, or honor; to wit; because persons so affected, would but grossly abuse their places, and the power that should be conferred on them, by virtue of their places, to their own disgrace, and the wrong of others. Yet some read the word, as a continuation of the former sentence, *But he* shall be called (supplied from the foregoing verse, as Job 14.5. & 24.19.) *vile,* or *fool,* that *speaketh villainy,* or *folly,* Chap. 9.17. men shall be accounted such as their words and dealings declare them to be, Mat. 12.33,37. Joh. 8.39,44. 1 Joh. 3.7,10. But the former better agrees with the genuine sense of the foregoing sentence; and the text yields it of itself.

*{will speak villainy*} His communication will be correspondent to his inward base disposition. See Chap. 9.17. but here more specially applied to the words and speech of persons, in place of authority, and in exercise of their power, Prov. 30.15. Hos. 4.18. Mic. 7.3. whom such manner of speech worst beseems, Prov. 16.10. & 17.7.

*{and his heart will work iniquity*} That is, will devise and contrive it; for that is properly the work of the heart, Psa. 64.6. So Mic. 2.1. the work is ascribed to the heart, because there it is forged, and from thence it proceeds, Mat. 15.9. Some read it, *and whose heart worketh iniquity,* as before.

*{iniquity*} Which in all men is inexcusable, but in judges, and place of judicature, most abominable, Psalm 58.1,2. & 82.1,2. Prov. 17.15. & 24.23,24. & 28.21.

*{to practice hypocrisy*} Or, *in practicing* (as Chap. 3.8. & 10.2.) *profaneness,* or abominable wickedness, as the word commonly, yea, universally signifies. (See Chap. 9.17. & 33.14.) and as the next branch intimates.

*{and to utter error against the Lord*} Or, *and in uttering error,* as some, *of,* or *concerning the Lord:* which they expound of delivering and teaching false doctrine: and the particle here is sometime so used, as Job 42.7. but the prophet speaks not here of ministers, but of magistrates, and their giving unjust sentence, and passing erroneous dooms against the word and charge of God. See Chap. 28.7. the particle is used for *against,* as here, so Chap. 23.11. Thus, rather, I take it; than as some of the Rabbis, of impious speeches, concerning God and his providence; such as, Psalm 14.1. & 53.1. & 10.11,13. & 94.7. for these are usually in their hearts, not in their tongues, in their minds, not in their mouths.

*{to make empty the soul of the hungry; and he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail*} Or, *in making empty the soul of the hungry, and in making the drink of the thirsty to fail,* as before, or, *and in that he maketh,* &c. by unjust courses bereaving them of those means that should maintain them, and so causing them to starve, Chap. 3.14,15.

*{make empty*} A metaphor from emptying of vessels: as if they plucked their bread out of their bodies, and their meat out of their bowels, as Job 20.15,20,21. Jer. 51.44. or kept them from being satisfied, by withdrawing that from them, wherewith they should have been filled: as a river, or pool, is emptied, by deriving or diverting the streams that should feed it, Chap. 19.5,6.

*{make empty the hungry*} For by *emptying* to *make hungry,* or to starve. See the like, Chap. 24.10.

*{hungry soul*} That is, *person,* Psalm 107.9. but this phrase makes the speech here more emphatical.

*{the drink of the thirsty*} Not which he has, but which he needs, and would have, which he wants and desires.

*{he causeth to fail*} By withdrawing from him; which should procure it him when he thirsts: or, by such means, bringing him; as to hunger, so to thirst, and to perish by either; Chap. 5.13. Amos 8.13. See the contrary; Chap. 33.16.

**V. 7.** *{The instruments also of the churl are evil*} Heb. *And the churl,* or, *The churl also,* (as Chap. 29.19.) *his instruments are evil.* Where by *instruments,* some of the Jewish commenters understand, weights and measures: as if the meaning were, that such would use light weights, and scant measures, Amos 8.5. (though there the *shekel* is heavy, because, by it, they took their money) Mic. 6.10,11. supposing that thence also, such had that name; and the meaning to be, that such an one would forbear no evil course to enrich himself. But the prophet speaks not here of merchants, or tradesmen, but of princes, and men in place of authority and judicature. Others, therefore, rather by *instruments,* conceive to be meant, such under-officers, or adherents, as corrupt judges and great ones, do, ordinarily make use of by them, as instruments to negotiate with those, that have causes before them, or suits to them, or to help to bring about, and put in execution their wicked and unjust designs, Prov. 13.12. & 19.12. Amos 4.1. Zeph. 1.9. Or, as some of the Jewish doctors, such sleights and artifices, as persons so affected, are wont to use, for the perverting of judgment, and either bringing about, or smothering, and setting some fair and colorable pretense, upon their unjust and wrongful courses Mic. 2.1,3. & 7.3. Yet some would have it, he shall be called, or accounted, *a churl,* or, *a niggard, whose instruments,* that is, courses, *are evil.* See before, on v. 5,6. There is an elegancy of speech in the original, which our English cannot express: as if it were said, *The toolman's tools* are evil, or the like. *The churl his instruments;* as *a Ruler his servants,* Prov. 29.12. See ver. 1.

*{he deviseth wicked devices*} Heb. *he consulteth,* that is, *contriveth;* as Chap. 23.8. He will always be contriving some mischief or other; Psalm 36.4. The latter word, in its original, signifies *a thought,* or *design,* in general; but is for the most part, used for some wicked thought, design, or device and that not projected, or plotted only, but practiced; any vile, and abominable, either project, or practice, Levit. 18.17. & 19.29. & 20.14. And there was small reason for the Jewish critic, hence to collect, that the *Cilay,* here mentioned, is not so bad as the *Nabal;* because the one is said *to devise,* and *contrive,* whereas the other is said *to do,* and *to utter:* v. 6.

*{to destroy the poor*} Or, *the afflicted;* as the word properly signifies; but used for *poor;* because such more exposed to affliction and oppression, than others, Ps. 102. title, ch. 3.14.

*{with lying words*} Heb. *words of falsehood;* as Jer. 23.32. or *matters of falsehood:* as *words of iniquity,* for *matters of iniquity,* Ps. 65.3. and *a word,* or *matter of falsehood,* for *a false matter,* Exod. 23.7. By false suggestions, or wrongful dooms, to overthrow them in judgment, whom they ought to right and relieve, ch. 3.12–15.

*{even when the needy speaketh right*} Heb. *judgment;* as v. 1. Or, *and by speaking* against *the needy* in *judgment.* A defect of the particle, *against;* as ver. 2. of *in* as Ps. 9.16. Or as some, supplying the verb from the former member, *and* to destroy, or spoil *judgment, when the poor speaketh,* not regarding what he says; so some, not improbably.

**V. 8.** *{But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand*} So the most render it, and it is opposed to what was said, v. 6. of the *niggard.* Some read the words, *but he* shall be called *liberal,* or *munificent,* that takes *liberal,* or *munificent courses and persisteth in the same.* I conceive rather, that they ought thus to be read: *But the Prince shall take ingenuous courses, and by ingenuous courses shall he be established,* Prov. 12.7. or *and for such courses shall he stand;* as Dan. 11.31. The *Prince,* or the *Lord,* or the *honorable* man in those times (in disposition of heart & mind, answering his name) shall carry himself ingenuously, & honorably, forbearing, and abhorring such base and dishonorable courses, as the persons, before described, usually take & follow; and he shall not only take ingenuous and honorable courses, himself, but uphold and maintain others, also, in the like.

**V. 9.** *{Rise up ye women, that are at ease; hear my voice; ye careless daughters, give ear unto my speech*} The prophet in these words, makes entrance into his ensuing discourse, in the latter part of this chapter, concerning those troubles that were to come, before the establishment of the state, in manner before described; with an earnest exhortation unto those, whom it specially concerned: wherein, or by he excites them, rousing up themselves from, and shaking off that security, that at present possessed them, to attend diligently thereunto. See the like, in the like case, ch. 28.23.

*{rise up*} Either *awaking out of your sleep of security:* as Eph. 5.14. Or, *rising from your beds, on which you lie at ease, reposing yourselves:* as 2 Sam. 11.2. or, without special respect to any such present posture or disposal, setting other matters aside, listen seriously to what I say: as Numb. 23.18. for of *rising* to give reverence to God's word, as Judg. 3.20. seems not so well to fit here.

*{ye women*} and *daughters.* These two terms, some understand here properly of the weaker sex; as Chap. 3.16,17. The prophet directing his speech to them more specially, because they lived most at ease, and seemed, at present, most secure, as wanting that foresight, that the other sex employed in state-affairs, oft times has; as also, for that being as deeply faulty in some things, as the men, they were to suffer alike with them, in the troubles of the times, and were less able to endure hardship, Deut. 28.30,32.41. 2 Chr. 36.17. Ch. 3.16,17. Others think, that the men of that state, are so styled, here, for their effeminate carriage, and womanlike disposition. See Chap. 3.12. & 19.16. Others, lastly, suppose that thereby is meant, the towns and cities of Judah, (for this prophecy seems not to deal with Samaria; though some carry it over thither) which are commonly, in Scripture, compared to women, and were as daughters to Jerusalem, the mother-city, and at present, enjoyed much tranquility and peace, together with her, who neither also is here excluded. See the common phrase, Josh. 15.32,36,41,43. Lam. 3.51. And I take them both for the same: for I suppose that too nice, which some here have, who by *women* would have understood the greater cities, by *daughters,* the less. Howbeit, I suppose it, as was in the first place, propounded, to be directed to the women, the court-ladies especially; and by them to the men. See Ch. 3.16.

*{careless*} Heb. *confident.* Alluding to their vain confidence, for which they are so frequently taxed, Chap. 30.12. and 31.1.

**V. 10.** *{Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women*} So some read it, expounding it of the Babylonian captivity, which was to last for many years, Jer. 25.11. The words are in the Hebrew, *Days above a year;* as Job 23.2. or, *Days upon,* or *unto a year;* as chap. 29.1. or, (so some of the Jewish critics would have it) *Days with,* or *beside a year;* as Chap. 7.2. that is, as some, *two years: a year upon a year; days,* for *a year:* as Exod. 13.10. Numb. 9.22. but *days,* and *a year,* are here put as distinct things, which in those places is not. Some therefore would have it read, A year of *days above a year,* as 1 Sam. 27.7. which yet would amount to no more than the former; as 2 Samuel 13.23. & 14.28.
