So Ezek. 18.25,29. and 33.17,20. and so most here take it: sometime, *to weigh out*, as Job 28.25. or, *to ponder*, taken metaphorically: and by *weighing*, or *pondering* of things, to *explore*, or *examine* them: or, by searching into them, to attain to an exact knowledge of them: as by weighing of things in the balance, or at the beam, men come exactly to know their weight, Psal. 62.9. Dan. 5.27. So it is taken, Prov. 16.2. & 21.2. & 24.12. So the ancient Greek by the apostle retained, Rom. 11.33. 1 Cor. 2.16. renders it here, *who hath known the Lord's mind?* Who can so dive into his secret thoughts, or purposes, as to come to discover what he intends to do, or by what courses he means to carry on what he intends? And this way also divers go. Howbeit some of the Jewish doctors, to bring in the four elements, by *Spirit* here understand the *air*, as it seems to be taken, Prov. 30.4. and as for the *wind*, Joh. 3.8. And because the verb sometime signifies, also, *to dispose*, or, *establish*, 1 Samuel 2.3. they expound the words, *who hath ordered*, or *settled the air?* or, who is it, that *meeteth*, or *weigheth out the winds?* Job 28.25. And there ending the question, they make the answer to it, *the Lord*. But this nicety rents the text too much asunder. Either of the former is probable enough.

*{or*} Heb. *and*; as ver. 13. so ch. 17.8.

*{being his counselor*} Of his counsel or of counsel with him. Heb. *the man of his counsel*, or *his man of counsel*; as Psal. 119.24. There is a defect, either of the particle, as Rom. 1.29. 1 Pet. 2.4. which the apostle expresses by the verb-substantive, or of the note of similitude, as v. 6. So some; who read, *who as his counselor?* supplying also the relative from the former branch; as the Greek, and the apostle also does, Rom. 11.34. There is an allusion to such counselors, as kings use to have about them, and which they cannot well want, 1 Chron. 26.32. and 27.33. Prov. 11.14. and 24.6. See Chap. 3.3. and 9.6. See the same term in another sense, Chap. 46.11.

*{hath taught him*} Heb. *made him to know*; as Exod. 18.16. Prov. 22.19. Ezek. 20.11. Has instructed him in aught, or acquainted him with aught that he was ignorant of before: or showed him what he should do, or how he should do it. See Job 21.23. & 36.22,23.

**V. 14.** *{With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment? and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?*} Or, *with whom doth he consult, that he may* (as Josh. 24.9. Mal. 1.9.) *instruct him*, (Heb. *make him to understand*, as Psal. 119.27.) *and teach him the course of judgment*; (how to carry himself judiciously in his affairs, or uprightly, in execution of judgment) *or* (as ver. 13.) *may teach him knowledge, and acquaint him* (Heb. *cause him to know*) *the way of understanding?* Hebr. *understandings*: as Ps. 78.72. which some expound of variety and multiplicity of understanding: and so such plurals, sometime, seem to import, 2 Sam. 22.51. Psalm 18.50. Prov. 1.20. but yet sometime they seem to extenuate and diminish; as this very term, chap. 47.11. and so here, *understandings*, not for all manner, but for any manner of understanding. See the like, ver. 29. It is, in effect, the same, only somewhat enlarged, with the former, ver. 13. implying, that God, in no work of his, receives any instruction, or direction from any; as earthly kings and potentates are wont to do from their counselors, whom, in state-matters of great moment, or deep concernment, they usually confer and consult with, 2 Chron. 30.2. Est. 1.13.

**V. 15.** *{Behold the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance,}* This is added, to show the invalidity and inability of any human power, to oppose God in his purposed work, or in the least manner, to obstruct any passage of his providence: and withal, to encourage his people, not to fear any might or malice of man: but to rest steadfastly, with full confidence of heart, upon him, for the making of his promises good unto them, chap. 51.7,8,12. Psalm 60.11,12. and 62.8,9. and 146.3–6.

*{the nations*} As some, the Chaldeans, your lords and masters, at present, chap. 26.23. Or, rather, all nations, they, and others; (as before, ver. 6,7. and after, ver. 17.) are all of them put together.

*{as a drop of a bucket*} That hangs on it, or falls from it, in the drawing of it up; or that stays behind, when the water or liquor is poured out, and yet minishes not the measure: the former word is nowhere else found; the latter only, Numb. 24.7.

*{they are counted*} All one here with, *they are*; as it is in the former branch: so ch. 29.17. & 32.15. & v. 17.

*{as the small dust of the balance*} Or, *as the powder of the balance*: such as hangs on the scale, and yet alters not the weight; or stays still in it, after the spice weighed in it, is poured out: as a thing of no considerable worth, or weight: the word (in this notion nowhere else found) comes of a root, that signifies the breaking of clods to small dust, 2 Sam. 22.43. Ps. 18.42. or the beating of spices to fine powder, Exod. 30.36.

*{Behold*} In way of admiration, as before. So Chapter 29. verse 14.

*{he taketh up the isles as a very little thing,}* Or, *he taketh up, and throweth away* (for the word includes both: see ch. 63.9. with Jer. 16.13. & 22.26.) *the isles* (the lands or countries, as c. 41.1.) *as powder*: the word signifies any thing *beaten very small*, or *thin*, Exod. 16.14. Lev. 16.12. *thin*, or *beaten thin*, for *thin* powder, or powder so *beaten*: a defect of the subject, as ver. 10. expressed, ch. 29.5. The old Greek, by mistake of a letter, renders it, *he casteth them out as spittle*: and the letters, by reason of the near affinity of their figure, are taken the one, oft, for the other. See 1 Chr. 1.6,7,50,41,50. Jer. 2.20. & 15.14. See also, v. 12.

**V. 16.** *{And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering*} Or, *a sacrifice*, so called because it *ascends*, or *goes up*, upon the altar, Psal. 51.19. (for they narrow it too much, that render it, *a whole burnt offering*, from which it is there distinguished) rather than as some, because it goes up all into smoke, Psalm 37.20. Judg. 13.20. The meaning is, no creature, or matter, is sufficient to furnish a service of God, answerable to his infinite greatness; though all the beasts, harboring in that spacious forest of Lebanon, should be slain, and all the wood growing on it, felled to fire them with, it would come far short of a sacrifice, proportionable to his greatness unto whom it were to be tendered. See cha. 66.1. and of Lebanon, see Psalm 29.6. & 104.16. ch. 3.13. & 37.24.

**V. 17.** *{All nations before him, are as nothing, and they are accounted to him less than nothing, and vanity*} See Dan. 4.32. for the former; Ps. 62.9. for the latter.

*{before him*} In his sight; as Job 26.6. or compared with him; as Gen. 2.18,20.

*{are counted to him*} Either are so deemed by him, or are so in reference to him. See on ver. 15.

*{nothing, and vanity*} Or, *nothing*, or, *vanity*; *and*, for *or*; as ver. 13. *less than nothing*, or *a thing of nought*; a thing of no shape, or worth, or use. The word is used of that rude, confused, and shapeless mass, out of which the creature were afterward formed; Gen. 1.2. applied to things stripped of all their beauty, state, endowments, & furniture, and reduced to extreme desolation and confusion. See Chapter 24. ver. 10.

**V. 18.** *{To whom then will ye liken God?*} Heb. *And* (as Chapter 28.2,20.) *to whom will ye make God like?* what human creature, or counterfeit deity, can you imagine to be any thing like such an infinite and almighty essence, Ps. 89.6,8. and 96.4,5.

*{or what likeness will ye compare unto him?*} Heb. *and* (as ver. 13.) *what similitude will ye set him up?* Or, *fit him with?* it may well be understood of images, made to resemble and represent God, Act. 17.29. albeit the word be used also of furnishing a table, ch. 65.11. and of setting battle in array, 2 Sam. 10.17. the former whereof, might well suit with verse 16. the latter, with ver. 17. but that the term of *similitude* will hardly admit either. The scope hereof seems to be, not only to dissuade them from attempting to resemble God, by any visible shape or figure, Deuter. 4.12,15–19,23,25. or to strengthen them against the idolatry, though never so pompously set out, that they might be tempted unto, in Babylon, chap. 44.21. Jer. 10.1–13. Dan. 3.1,2. but chiefly, and principally, to confirm their faith, and to settle their minds in an hopeful expectation of their deliverance from God, according to his gracious purpose and promise, ver. 2. by setting forth, as his infinite might and majesty, so, the meanness, baseness, emptiness, and nothingness, of men or idols, or aught else whatsoever, that might enter into competition with him, or offer to make any opposition against him. See cha. 46.5. Jer. 10.6.

**V. 19.** *{The workman melteth a graven image*} Having laid forth God's inconceivable might, majesty, and immensity, he proceeds now to discover the vanity, baseness, and imbecility of idols. See the like, ch. 41.6,7. & 44.9,20. & 46.6,7. Jer. 10.3–5,8,9. Ps. 115.4–8. and 135.15,18.

*{workman*} Or, *brazier*, or *founder*; the word is a very general term. See of it, on Chap. 3.3. See also, verse 20. Chapter 41.7. and 44.11–13. But here, more specially, one that works in metals; as 1 Kings 7.14. 2 Chron. 24.12. Chap. 44.12. and 54.16.

*{melteth*} Or, *casteth*; as ch. 44.10. So their gods must pass the fire, before gods they can be.

*{a graven image*} He melts some metal, either brass, or some such baser stuff, because they will not be at the cost to have it all of massy gold, or silver; which being melted he casts into a mold, and so makes an image of it, to be further graven and polished, before it go to the goldsmith to be gilded, or overlaid with gold: so that in the words, there is a kind of anticipation, *he melteth*, or *casteth a graven image*, that is, metal to make an image, that being melted shall be graved: so chap. 44.10. See of the like, chap. 24.10. and 44.9. and 47.2.

*{and the goldsmith*} Heb. *the finer*: as it is rendered, Prov. 25.4. and the like, Mal. 3.2. or *founder*: as Judg. 17.4. See ch. 41.7. the term, though not so general as the former, yet comprehends *founders* of all sorts: though those more specially, that are employed in the finer sort of metals for the making and refining of them. So ch. 46.6. Jer. 10.9,14. & 51.7.

*{spreadeth it over with gold*} Exod. 39.3. beats out gold into thin leaves or plates: and therewith overlays and covers what the other had produced and polished, thereby to add the more show and state unto it, ch. 46.6. Jer. 10.9.

*{and casteth*} Heb. *a burning*, or *melting chains*, that is, silver to make chains, as before.

*{silver chains*} Heb. *chains of silver* (as, *gods of gold and silver*, Dan. 5.4. for *golden* and *silver* gods) therewith to adorn it, as 1 Kings 6.21. or to fasten it unto some post or pillar, or some staple driven into either; that it may not fall or stir, but stand fast and steady, bolt-upright; ch. 41.7. & 46.7. Jer. 10.5. for of such chains, also, is the word used Ezek. 7.23. Nah. 3.10.

**V. 20.** *{He that is so impoverished, that he hath no oblation chooseth a tree, that will not rot: he seeketh unto him, a cunning workman, to prepare a graven image, that shall not be moved*} The poorest man that is will have some god, or other, wooden one, rather than fail of one, Chapter 44.14,15. Deuteronomy 28.64. and is so sottish and senseless, as to imagine, that a silly wright, of a sorry piece of wood, is able to make him a god, Chapter 46.6. Jer. 10.3.

*{so impoverished, that he hath no oblation*} Heb. *impoverished*, or *penurious of oblation*: it is a word, in this form, nowhere else found; but one near it, for a *poor man*, Eccl. 4.13. & 9.15,16. another for *penury*, or scarcity, Deut. 8.9. Howbeit, because the word is here in an entire form, not such as is in regiment usual, some would have the text rendered, *he that is impoverished doth for an oblation choose a tree that will not rot*. But this another excepting against, as not regarding the pause at *oblation*, renders it, *he that is in danger voweth an oblation*. So the word is used in another form, for *to be endangered*, Eccles. 10.9. and with the Rabbines (says he) frequently. I adhere to the first, reading the words with a more familiar supply, *To him that is impoverished, an oblation is*. There is no man so weakened in his estate, but he will have some offering or other, he will find somewhat to furnish himself with, in this kind.

*{oblation*} Such as they offered toward the building of the sanctuary, Exodus 25.2. and 30.13. has nothing of any great value to lay out upon, or confer toward the making of his idol.

*{chooseth a tree that will not rot*} Or, *makes choice of some wood* (as Deuteronomy 4.28.) *that will not rot*: such as the cypress is said to be, much used, therefore, for such purposes, Theophrast, lib. 5. ch. 5. Pliny, lib. 16. ch. 40,41,42. See chap. 44.14. a defect of the relative; as Chapter 33.19. and so in the next branch.

*{cunning*} Heb. *wise*: as ch. 3.3.

*{workman*} *Wright, carpenter*, or *carver*: the word was before used, for one that works in metal, ver. 19. here, for one that works in timber, as also, ch. 44.13.

*{a graven image*} Or, *a carved* one rather, because of wood: not of stone, or metal.

*{that shall not be moved*} Or, *may not stir*; being fixed and fastened to the wall, or some other sure stay. See v. 19.

**V. 21.** *{Have ye not known? Have ye not heard? Hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?*} The prophet, in these words, is generally deemed to turn his speech to God's people, as charging them with extreme stupidity, if having not only the light of nature, and the sight of the creature, as other people had; but the word of God, also, and the story of the creation, and the administrations of God therein related, and registered, they should yet entertain such base conceits of the deity, as those heathen idolaters did: so chap. 41.8,9. & 44.21. Howbeit, I suppose, that he still persists in dealing with the heathen idolaters, whose folly, and stupidity he was laying forth before, ver. 18–20. admiring their blockishness and brutishness, if they never took notice of, or had never heard aught concerning God, or were not able by the very frame of the creature, though they had never heard word of him, to conceive a deity that had given being thereunto, and the infinite power and wisdom of him that had so done, Ps. 8.3,4. & 19.1–3. Rom. 1.19,25.

*{Have ye not known?*} Or, *Do ye not know?* as Ps. 14.4. & 82.5. & 92.6. ch. 44.18. Heb. *will ye not know?* as taxing their willful and affected ignorance: so Psal. 36.3. & 82.5. 2 Pet. 3.5. yet the future may be put for the present; as 2 Sam. 3.38. 2 Chron. 32.13. so in the next clause, Heb. *will ye not hear?* for, *have ye not heard*: did you never hear aught of those strange passages of God's providence, wrought for his people; the report whereof has gone abroad unto other nations far and near, Exod. 15.14–16. Num. 14.13,14. Josh. 2.10,11. ch. 59.19. 2 Chr. 32.31.

*{from the beginning*} Being understood of God's people, from the time that they first were a people, or that God severed them to himself, ch. 41.9. & 44.2. or, if of other people, also, from the very beginning of the world; the notion of a deity being engraven in man's heart, at first, and by tradition also propagated and transmitted unto posterity. Hebrews *from the head*: as Chapter 41.4.

*{have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?*} The particle *from* is not in the text: nor does the ancient Greek, or old Latin, therefore, own it; which divers interpreters, therefore, following, read the words, *have ye not considered the foundations of the earth?* Or, *do ye not understand the foundations of the earth?* To wit, that they were made, or laid by God, Ps. 102.25. But our English versions, all of them, admit it; and it is oft omitted, where it is to be supplied, as ch. 18.7. & 32.2. & 52.2. here to be fetched in from the clause next before-going: for explication, see Rom. 1.20. the best comment upon this place.

**V. 22.** *{It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth*} Or, as the margin has it, *Him that sitteth*; as continuing the sentence, *understand*, or *consider him, from the foundations of the earth, who sitteth*: or, as some of our former versions, *that he sitteth*: or, that it is, *he who sitteth*; as ver. 28. *upon the circle of the earth*; or, *above the circle of the earth*: as Gen. 1.20. as sovereign Lord and ruler of it, having heaven for his throne, and the earth for his foot-pace, Chapter 66.1. as, *the circle of the earth*, here: so, *the circle of the deep*, or the sea, Proverbs 8.27. and *the circle of heaven*, Job 22.14.

*{and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers*} Or, *as locusts*: as the word is rendered, 2 Chr. 7.13. where it appears to be one of the creatures that made havoc of their grain, which grasshoppers are not wont to do: and it seems, therefore, to be some kind of locusts (from which yet it is distinguished, Lev. 11.22.) or of some other kind very near unto it: such they are, even the greatest giants, and the mightiest of them, in regard of God, as the Israelites seemed such to the sons of Anak, Num. 13.33.

*{that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain*} Psalm 104.2. ch. 42.5. such curtains, as their tents did ordinarily consist of, Exod. 26.1. Cant. 1.5. ch. 54.2. Some render it, *as a canopy*: the word nowhere else used, some would have to signify *a fine*, or *thin* sheet, or veil: because it comes from a word, that has a notion of *thinness*. I suppose it rather to signify *a thin skin*, or *film*: because tents were usually made of *skins*, Exod. 36.19. and a word very near to it, of the same stock, is used for *a film*, or thin skin, overgrowing the eye, Levit. 21.20.

*{and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in:}* Heb. *to sit in*: as a general, in his pavilion, 1 King. 20.12. or, *to dwell in*, as his palace, Ps. 11.4. & 33.13,14. & 123.1.

**V. 23.** *{That bringeth the princes to nothing*} Or, *That bringeth* (Heb. *giveth*, as Chapter 41.2.) *princes* (for there is no article in the text) *to nothing*. See Job 12.21. Psal. 107.40. Chapter 41.11.

*{he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity*} *The judges*, that is, the *rulers*, Judg. 2.16. Act. 13.20. *as vanity*, or, *a thing of nought*. See v. 17. ch. 44.9.

**V. 24.** *{Yea, they shall not be planted: yea, they shall not be sown: yea, their stock shall not take root in the earth*} Heb. *Yea, they have not been planted, yea, they have not been sown, yea, their stock hath not taken root in the ground*. Which some render in the present tense, *they are not planted, nor sown, nor doth their stock take root*. Which they diversely expound, some applying it to idols, as having not so much firmness, as trees, or plants, that are set, or sown, and take deep rooting in the ground: which these do not. Others, of princes and potentates, before spoken of, as like, not to trees, or plants, such as before: but as grass, that is neither set, nor sown, but comes up of itself; nor takes any deep root, as trees do, and is therefore soon and suddenly gone, Psal. 37.2. ver. 6–8. But I see no cause, why we should alter the tense that the text exhibits. Which one of the Jewish commenters understands, as that which may be said of them, *Surely, they were never planted, nor sown, nor did their stock ever take root*: alleging to that purpose, Job 8.18. and the sense, indeed, is no other: but the words may be rendered, as thus depending on the former; he so brings them to *nothing*, that they are, *as if they had never been planted, as if they had never been sown, as if their stock had never taken root in the ground*: albeit, like goodly oaks, or cedars, they seemed to have taken such deep rooting before, that they could not easily be stirred, much less removed, or plucked up by the roots, Ps. 37.35,36. Ezek. 31.3–14. Job 18.16,17,19. the particle is thrice repeated, to add the more vehemency to the sentence; as the like, Gen. 43.8. Ezra 8.21. ch. 41.26. & 48.8. See the like syntax, and supply also, ch. 10.15. Job 39.16. supply likewise, Jud. 9.30. and the contrary expression, Job 14.9. especially if the term, there used, be (as some learned would have it,) a verb, not a noun.

*{and he shall also blow upon them, and they shall wither*} Or, *yea, let him but blow upon them, and they shall wither*; or, *for he doth but blow upon them, and they are withered*. Heb. *and he hath even blown upon them, and they shall be dried up*, or, *withered*. See the like, both matter, and model of speech, Psal. 103.16. the copulative, for the causative: as v. 26. See before, v. 7.

*{and the whirlwind shall take them away as stubble*} A bare blast of God's breath blowing upon them, shall be sufficient, not to blast them only, and cause them to wither away; but to blow them away, also, like stubble, or chaff, with a whirlwind, chap. 41.2,15,16. Job 15.30.

**V. 25.** *{To whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal?*} Or, *That I should be like him*; as Prov. 26.4. *and*, for, *that*: as ch. 53.2. See v. 18. ch. 46.5.

*{saith the holy One*} God, who is holiness itself; and none holy as he, 1 Sam. 2.2.

**V. 26.** *{Lift up your eyes on high*} To the heaven, to the starry sky, ch. 51.6. Job 35.5.

*{and behold who hath created these things*} Heb. *and see*; that is, *consider*; as 1 King. 20.7. Jer. 2.19,31. who it is that *created these*, to wit, the stars, that numberless host, (Gen. 15.5.) which there you see; and who is, therefore, far more excellent, than they, and of an infinite power, that was able to create them, Genesis 1.14,18. and 2.1. Job 26.13. Psalm 8.3. and 19.1,2. and 136.7–9. and 148.3,5.

*{that bringeth out their host by number;*} Who it is, *that bringeth out their host by tale*; that musters them, and keeps a list of them, as a general, or commander, does of his soldiers, and brings them forth, every one, in his due place, as a chieftain draws out his soldiers on a training day, into the fields, each one in his proper rank and station, Job 38.37. Psalm 104.19. and 147.4.

*{their host*} See Gen. 2.1. ch. 1.9.

*{he calleth them all by names*} Heb. *by name*; and so it would be rendered, as Exod. 33.17. *I know thee by name*; for as for that, Ps. 147.4. it is not aright rendered, *he calleth them by their names*; it is in the Hebrew, *he calleth names unto them*, that is, *he gives them names*, or, imposes names on them: the same syntax, that is, Gen. 2.20. and 26.18.

*{by the greatness of his might (for that he is strong in power) not one faileth*} By reason of his infinite power and greatness, he has another manner of command over his heavenly host, than any commander has over his companies; some of theirs may fail them: when they should appear before them, or attend upon them: it is otherwise with his; they appear each one constantly in his place, ready prest to do service to God, his general, in whatsoever he shall please to assign him unto, Judg. 5.20. Psalm 148.8. cha. 37.36. & 48.13.

*{of his might*} Heb. *mights*: as Ps. 78.51. So v. 28.

*{for that*} Heb. *and*: as Psalm 60.11. Chapter 64.5. So v. 24.

*{not one*} Or, *no one*; or, *not any*: to wit, of them, as ch. 34.16. Heb. *man faileth not*; *man*, for, *each*, or *any* one: as Exod. 25.20. Chapter 41.28.

**V. 27.** *{How sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest thou, O Israel?*} Hitherto the prophet had bent his discourse against the sottish folly, and brutish stupidity of idolaters, in their vain conceits concerning their base idols, and their ridiculous practices about them. Now he turns the stream of his debate unto God's own people, taxing them as persons that had been taught better things, for their diffidence and distrust, either of God's care of them, or power to relieve them, or both: *Jacob*, and *Israel*, for those of his posterity: as chap. 29.22,23.

*{My way is hid from the Lord?*} God looks not after me, nor takes notice of those things that do befall me, no more than as if they were concealed from him, and were hidden from his sight. So Gen. 4.14. Psalm 31.22. & 94.7. Howbeit, in Scripture, the term, of *being hid*, does oft import difficulty, and imply something *hard* to be done. So Deuteronomy 17.8. *if a matter be hidden from thee*; that is, *be too hard for thee* to decide. Jeremiah 32.27. *Is any thing hidden from me?* that is too hard for me to do? So also, Genesis 18.14. & Jeremiah 32.17. and it may likewise be so here understood, *My way is hidden from God*, or *is too hard for God*; that is the course to be taken for our delivery out of captivity, is a matter too difficult for God himself to effect: we account it a thing altogether impossible: yea, this very word seems so to be taken, Job 3.23. *to a man, whose way is hidden*, that is, involved in such difficulties, that he cannot possibly get out; for so it follows, *whom God hath hedged in*: See Lamentation 3.7. Hosea 2.16. whether way we take it, they are the thoughts and imaginations, even of God's own people, in the time of their captivity. See the one, Chapter 49.14. and the other, Ezekiah 37.11. the latter I rather follow, because of what follows, verse 28,29.

*{my way*} Not the course that I take; but that is taken with me: not, what I do, but what I endure: as, *my wrong*, Genesis 16.5. See Jeremiah 51.35. or, the course that is to be taken for me, or with me, for the effecting of my deliverance.

*{and my judgment is passed over from my God*} He regards not my cause, nor to right the wrong done me. So Job 27.2. and 34.5.

*{my judgment*} That is, *my cause, my right*, as Psalm 9.4. Lamentation 3.59.

*{is passed from my God*} Or, *passed away from my God*: as Jeremiah 8.13. or, *it is so past, that God cannot redress it*: it is a cure too hard for God himself; for in such a notion is this preposition oft used: see the places pointed to, in the former branch: spoken by them, as not expecting aught in this kind, from him: and that either supposing that he did wholly neglect them, or doubting of his ability, in some sort, to relieve them; their state being so low, and their condition so desperate; for that some such tang, and taint, these their complaints were touched with, appears by the answer returned thereunto, v. 28,29. See Jeremiah 30.12,13.

**V. 28.** *{Hast thou not known*} Or, *Dost thou not know?* as 1 Cor. 3.16. & 6.9,15,16,19. Are you yet to learn that which you have been so oft told and taught? Or, as our Savior to his disciples, Matthew 15.16. *Are ye also without understanding?*

*{Hast thou not heard?*} See verse 1.

*{That the everlasting God, the Lord, the Creator of the ends of the earth fainteth not, nor is weary?*} That God as he created the world at the first, so he still rules and governs it, and all things in it, from the one end of it to the other, without toil or travel, Job 38.24. Psalm 9.7–9. John 5.17. and is able therefore, having all power, both to deliver you, when he sees good, Chapter 63.1. and, meanwhile, to support and sustain you, to keep you from fainting and failing, be you of yourselves never so feeble, or, far spent, verse 29,31. Philip 4.13.

*{that*} A defect of the particle, as Chapter 4.3.

*{the everlasting God*} Heb. *God of perpetuity*, or *eternity*: as Genesis 21.33. See Psal. 9.10. & 10.16. & 90.2. & 102.12. Chapter 26.4.

*{creator of the ends of the earth*} Maker and ruler of the whole world, from the one end to the other, Chapter 41.5.

*{he fainteth not, nor is weary*} As men do oft, when they have over-wrought themselves, Judges 4.21. 1 Samuel 29.10. 2 Samuel 21.15. Chapter 44.12. the words may well be rendered, *he is neither tired nor toiled*, for that is the proper signification of either word.

*{there is no searching of his understanding*} His wisdom in the government of the world, and in the dispensation and disposition of events and occurrents, concerning the creature, is such, as is beyond the reach of man's shallow capacity, Psalm 147.5. Chapter 55.8,9. Romanes 11.33.

**V. 29.** *{He giveth power to the faint; and to him that hath no might, he increaseth strength*} He makes his might to appear in man's weakness, 1 Corinthians 1.17,18. 2 Corinthians 12.9. enabling those to do, and endure any thing, Philip 4.13. Collosians 1.11. who, of themselves, are able to do nothing, John 15.5. 2 Cor. 3.5. and 4.7. and 10.4,6.

*{to the faint*} Or, *the weary one*, or *the tired*, Chapter 50.4. Jeremiah 51.58,64.

*{no might*} Heb. *mights*: as verse 26. but there, *mights*, for, abundance of might, or might of all sorts; but here, *mights*, for, *any might* at all: as *understandings*, for, *any understanding* at all, Chapter 27.11. thus those plurals, that usually have a notion of abundance and excess, yet sometime have on the other side, (which few observe) an intimation of scarcity and want: but this most in the negative. See Chapter 16.18.

*{increaseth strength*} Gives abundance of strength. Hebrew *multiplieth strength*, or, *maketh it to abound*: as of glory, Daniel 11.39.

**V. 30.** *{Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall*} Such as are of greatest might and strength, and are best able, to endure labor and travel, and to hold out in such work, as they are employed about, yet shall faint and fail, when weak and feeble ones, by God assisted and supported, shall stand fast by it, and hold out to the last, Psalm 33.16. Amos 2.14. See the like frame of speech, Psalm 34.20.

*{even the youths shall faint, and be weary*} Or, *The youths may be even tired and toiled*, for the particle, *even*, (Heb. *and*: as chapter 11.6.) is joined to the former verb, and the latter verb has a notion of toilsome labor, Genesis 31.42. ch. 49.4. & 62.8. & 65.23. and both here seem potential, as these also, Psalm 34.10.

*{young men*} Or, *choice youths*; for that is the notation of the word; expressed also, Jer. 48.15. 1 Sam. 9.2.

*{shall utterly fall*} Heb. *shall stumbling stumble*; that is, *shall be ever and anon stumbling*: as folk, faint and feeble, or toiled and tired out, are wont to be, it is distinguished from *falling*, Psalm 27.2. ch. 8.15. though it may here include both; or by the antecedent imply the consequent; as Psalm 107.12. chap. 59.14.

**V. 31.** *{But they that wait upon the Lord*} Heb. *And*: the copulative for the adversative; as chap. 36.12. they that with patience and tranquility of spirit expect his aid, and the performance of his promises in their due season, Psalm 40.1. and 130.5,6. ch. 8.17. & 28.16. & 30.18.

*{shall renew their strength*} As Job 14.7. & 29.20. Eccle. 8.1. or, *change*: as Genesis 35.2. & 41.14. chap. 8.10. they shall have a new supply of strength, enabling them to bear up, and hold out, when they seem to be clean spent; Psalm 37.26. & 103.3. 2 Cor. 1.8,9. & 4.8,16,16. & 12.9,10. a defect of the pronoun possessive: as Chapter 13.22.

*{they shall mount up with wings, as eagles*} Fowls, that fly strongly, and swiftly; and that build and soar aloft, Deut. 28.49. 1 Samuel 1.23. Job 39.30. Proverbs 23.5. Jer. 49.16. Hosea 8.1. They shall as easily overcome, and get over all difficulties and obstructions, that encounter them in their way, as if they had wings to fly over them, Exodus 19.4. Deut. 32.11. Rom. 8.35,37. Rev. 12.14.

*{with wings*} Heb. *with feather*. So the word properly signifies, Psa. 68.13. & 91.4. but here, *feather*, for, *wing*; and *wing*, for, *wings*, as Psalm 55.6. Ezekiah 17.3.

*{they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint*} Or, *they shall run, and not be tired; they shall walk*, (that is, proceed, or, go on,) *and not be toiled*. See verse 28,30.

### CHAPTER 41

**V. 1.** *{Keep silence before me, O islands*} Whether this chapter joined to the former, make up one sermon, or be an entire discourse of itself, is not generally agreed; sure it is, that it is much of the same argument with the former. For in it God foretells, by his prophet, that it may not be ascribed to any other, what he intends to do, for the rescuing and reduction of his people; challenges the false gods to do, any of them, the like; and both them, and their worshipers, to hinder him in the execution of it; if they can, with all the power that they are able to make.

*{Keep silence before me*} Heb. *to me*; that is, *Keep silence*, and *hearken to me*; or, *with silence hearken to me*. Of such defective, or comprehensive forms of speech see on chapter 38.17,21. God standing up to debate his cause, by his prophet, against the enemies of his people, with them, and their idols, directs his speech to them, rather than to their idols, that were as well deaf, as dumb, Psalm 115.5,6. and as the manner of men is, where they are about to speak, unto multitudes especially, Job 29.9,10. and 33.31,33. Acts 21.40. requires silence, that he may be heard. So Chapter 48.14,16.

*{O islands*} Or, *Lands*; as Chapter 20.6. and 40.15. You people of several countries. So after, verse 5. yet some would have the islanders and borderers on the sea-coast, intended in this branch; other people in the next: but I suppose the same persons intimated in either.

*{and let the people renew their strength*} Let the nations make all the power they can, for the support of themselves, and their idols, and to hinder, if they be able, the work that I foretell, and intend to effect, for the delivery of my people. Of the phrase and defect of the pronoun in it, See on chapter 40.31.

*{the people*} That is, the Jewish people, say some, of whom, cha. 41.31. but the word is plural; and never used, but of nations of divers lands, chapter 17.12,13. & 43.9. & 49.1.

*{let them come near, then let them speak, let them come near together in judgment*} That we may parley, and debate the matter together: as ch. 1.18. they shall have free liberty to speak, and say what they can for themselves: they shall not say, that they were condemned unheard. So verse 21. chapter 45.20,21. and 48.14,16.

**V. 2.** *{who raised up the righteous man from the east*} The most interpreters, following the Chaldee paraphrast, and the main stream of the Jewish commenters, understand this passage of Abraham. Though some of the Jewish doctors interpret them of the Messiah; with whom, some of ours, also, therein accord. Howbeit, I suppose that the things here spoken, are meant of Cyrus, that was to deliver God's people out of the Babylonian thraldom, and to restore them, to their country and former freedom again (though a type of Christ, and of spiritual freedom, from the thraldom of sin and Satan, by him achieved,) to whom whatsoever is here said, does most exactly agree. See Chapter 44.28. and 45.1.

*{who*} Which of all your idols? or, Who but myself? verse 26. who so long before do now foretell it, Chapter 44.28. See verse 4.

*{raised up*} V. 25. ch. 45.13. Act. 13.23. He speaks in the prophetical strain, of a thing to come, as already done: and so in the two places pointed to: as all there agree.

*{the righteous man*} Heb. *righteousness*: which those that apply it to the Messiah, expound, *that just one*, Acts 22.14. *our righteousness*, Jer. 23.6. 1 Cor. 1.30. those that understand it of Abraham, *righteousness*, for, a man of *righteousness*; that is, *a righteous man*, Gen. 15.6. as, *peace*, for a man of *peace*, a peaceable man, Psal. 120.7. and, *wisdom*, for a man of *wisdom*, a wise man, Mica. 6.9. But the text may well be rendered, *in righteousness*: as chapter 42.6. and as it is expressly said of Cyrus, chapter 45.13. to manifest my righteousness and faithfulness, (for faithfulness is also a branch of righteousness, Hebr. 6.10. 1 John 1.9.) in the fulfilling of my promises, and in righting the wrongs done to my people, Chap. 1.27. and 46.13. 2 Thessalonians 1.6,7. the defect of the particle, *in*, is most frequent. See Ch. 26.8,18. and 28.7. and 33.7. and 34.2,13. but especially, ch. 45.23.

*{from the east*} Christ, and righteousness introduced by him, Dan. 9.24. from the eastern parts of the world; from Judea, Rev. 16.12. say some; Abraham, from Chaldea, situate eastward from Canaan, say others, Gen. 11.31. & 12.4,5. & 29.1. But in Scripture, Chaldea is constantly termed, as from Canaan, north, Jer. 1.13–15. & 4.6. & 6.1,22. & 10.22. But Cyrus rather, from Persia, lying east from Babylon, v. 25. ch. 46.11.

*{called him to his foot*} Abraham to go to and fro at his command, and as he should appoint him, Genesis 12.1. Hebrews 11.8. Or, Cyrus, whom he singled out to do him service, to be led by him, and be at his command, chapter 44.28. & 45.1,2,3,4. for that is it, which this phrase imports. Gen. 30.30. Judg. 4.10. Matth. 8.9.

*{gave the nations before him, and made him rule over kings?*} This some apply to the reproach of those two kings, Pharao, and Abimelec, rebuked by God for the wronging of Abraham, Genesis 12.17. & 20.3. Ps. 105.14. the most, to the victory that Abraham achieved against those four kings, Genesis 14.14,15. But as the former has no affinity with what here follows; so, nor does the latter suit well with the words ensuing: for though Abraham then overcame these four kings in fight, yet that he ever ruled over any king, or country, we read not. It is rather, therefore, meant of Cyrus, who subdued many countries and kingdoms, with their kings, and having subdued them: reigned over them, chapter 41.5.

*{gave nations before him*} To be subdued by him, ch. 45.1. the article is not in the text.

*{made him rule over*} Subdued to him: as Chap. 40.10. a defect of the pronoun, as Hosea 6.4.

*{he gave them as the dust to his sword, and as driven stubble to his bow*} Or, *made them* (continuing the sentence) *as the dust to his sword, as driven stubble to his bow?* or, *whose sword made them as dust, his bow, as driven stubble*. So that he beat them, as to dust, Psal. 18.42. and they were no more able to stand before him, than small dust, or dry stubble before a stiff gale or puff of wind, Ps. 1.4. & 35.5. & 83.13. ver. 15,16. ch. 40.24. Jer. 13.24. the demonstrative, for the relative; as Jer. 5.15.

*{gave*} Or, *made*: as Jer. 44.22.

*{them*} A defect of the pronoun: as Chapter 30.2. and 40.11.

*{sword, and bow*} The weapons of war, then most in use, Psal. 44.3,6. chapter 21.15. the one to smite with at hand; the other, to strike with at distance, Psalm 37.14.

**V. 3.** *{He pursued them*} As Psalm 18.37. or, *so that he pursued them*: as Psalm 109.27. carrying on the sentence to the end of the verse.

*{and passed in safety*} Hebrew *he passed in peace*; that is, both with safety, and success, 2 Samuel 3.21. Judges 18.6. without disturbance, or resistance, to any purpose: as Exodus 11.7. Chapter 45.1.

*{even by the way that he had not gone with his feet*} Or, *a way he had not gone with his feet*. For there is no more in the text; not turning back by flight, as Sennacherib, the way that he came, Chapter 37.29. or, rather, passing safely under God's conduct, (as Jer. 2.17.) chap. 45.2. through such places as he had not formerly been acquainted with; to wit, Abraham, say some, unto Damascus, Genesis 14.15. or, Cyrus, rather through Assyria, and the countries adjacent, into Chaldea, and unto Babylon. See on Jeremiah 50.2. & 51.46. no strangeness, or uncouthness of way, shall be any impediment to his passage; as chapter 42.16. a want of the relative there is in the text: as Chapter 42.16. and 55.5. Which yet will not need, if a learned late writer's note be admitted, who renders the text, *he shall not go the way with his feet*; that is, he shall proceed with that speed and expedition, that he shall seem rather to fly, than to go. But this, to me, seems somewhat strained.

**V. 4.** *{Who hath wrought, and done it?*} Who was it, or is it, that did, or does all this before spoken of, verse 2,3? *it*; as Chapter 31.15. or *these things*, as Psalm 22.31. Malachi 2.17.

*{calling the generations from the beginning*} Hebrew *from the head*; as Chapter 40.21. or, *Who is it that calleth the generations from the beginning?* or *from the first?* supplying the interrogative from the former branch. Who as he made man at first, so continues the race of mankind throughout all ages, Gen. 1.27,28. Acts 17.26,28. or, that has ruled, does rule, and shall rule, the whole race of mankind, from the beginning of the world, to the end of it: authority implied in *calling*, that is, in imposition of names, whereby persons, or creatures, may be called, Gen. 1.5,8,10. & 2.17. Dan. 1.7. and so in having them at *call*, and command. See on Chapter 40.26.

*{I the Lord, the first, and with the last, I am he*} The answer to the former demands. It is Jehovah alone, that has done all these things; and no counterfeit deity, none but he, Ps. 136.4. ch. 44.24.

*{the first and with the last*} Who have ever been, and ever shall be, Ps. 90.2. & 102.27. ch. 40.18. & 43.10. & 44.6. & 48.12. Rev. 1.17. & 16.5. & 22.13.

*{I am he*} That does all these things: or, *I am*, to wit, *the first; and with the last*: *I am*, in being: as John 8.58. *before Abraham was, I am*: the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive; as Psalm 44.4. *Thou he my King*, for, *Thou art my King*, or *I am the same*, as *Thou art he*, for, *Thou art the same*, Psalm 102.27.

*{with the last*} That is, continuing with, and ruling this whole world to the end of it, Psalm 146.10. or, before whom, there was none, nor shall any be after, that shall continue as long as any creature shall have being, chap. 43.10. A learned late writer, thus renders this verse, *Who hath wrought and done, and calleth the former generations?* (that is, those now past,) *I the Lord the first, and the latter?* (to wit, the generations that are yet to come, who calls, as before,) *I the same*. I propound it only, and leave it to the consideration of the learned.

**V. 5.** *{The isles saw it, and feared; the ends of the earth were afraid, drew near and came*} The effect that these strange works of God set on foot, for the deliverance of his people, in raising up of Cyrus, and making him so successful, had upon the idolatrous nations, far and near; to wit, that they were stricken with much amazement and affrightment; and laid their heads together, to consult, by what means, to help and secure themselves; which (silly sots) they could not devise how to effect, but by recourse had to their counterfeit gods, and by making them more idols, as if their safety consisted in the multitude of such fopperies, cha. 2.8. Jer. 2.28. & 11.13. Yet the words may be, and are, by some, thus read and rendered; *When the isles see it, and are afraid, the ends of the earth are affrighted, let them draw near and come*; and so forward. See at the close of v. 7. a defect of the adverb of time, as ch. 17.6. & 26.10. So v. 17. See v. 1. & ch. 44.11.

*{isles*} Or, *countries*, that is, the people of several countries. See v. 1.

*{saw it*} Considered or took notice of it; as ch. 40.6. Ps. 119.153,159. a defect of the pronoun; as ch. 37.1,9.

*{feared*} So Exodus 15.14,15,16. for to the circumstances and effect of the deliverance out of Egypt, does God oft allude, in foretelling, and relating of that other out of Babylon. See ver. 17–19.

*{the ends of the earth*} Not the earth itself; as Chap. 40.28. but the inhabitants of the utmost parts of it, whose habitation reaches to the land's end: as Psalm 65.8. & 67.7. & 98.3. verse 9. Jeremiah 50.26.

*{drew near, and came*} Not to God, to appear before him; but to take counsel together, how to secure and save themselves; as Joshu 10.1–4. & 11.1–5.

**V. 6.** *{They helped every one his neighbor, and said every one to his brother, Be of good courage*} They endeavored to hearten and encourage one another to hold out, and stand to it, in hope of help from their idols. So Exodus 14.5,6,9. 1 Samuel 4.6–9. Psalm 64.5.

*{every one his neighbor*} Or, *one another*. Hebrew *a man his neighbor*, as Genesis 11.3. Jeremiah 31.34.

*{said every one to his brother*} Or, *said one to another*: as Genesis 26.31. Jeremiah 34.17. a supply from the former branch; as Genesis 1.16. 1 Chronicles 10.11.

*{Be of good courage*} Hebrew *Be strong*, 1 Samuel 4.9. Psalm 27.14. and 31.24.

**V. 7.** *{So the carpenter encouraged the goldsmith*} The workmen, whose employment is about making idols, were right glad, and ready to take hold of the opportunity to be set on work about the forging and coining of new gods; loath, with Demetrius, to have idolatry go down, and their trade to grow out of request, Acts 19.24,27.

*{So*} Hebrew *And*; yet *so*, Chapter 37.9. & howbeit, the copulative here retained, is better.

*{the carpenter*} See Chapter 40.19,20.

*{the goldsmith*} Or, *Finer*, or *Founder*. See Chapter 40.19. and 46.6. And so some of the Jewish doctors; howbeit, some other of them, by the former, understand the *founder*; by the latter, the *workman*, that overlays it with plates; as Chapter 40.19.

*{and he that smootheth with the hammer*} The gold or silver plates, that the idol is to be overlaid with, Chapter 40.19. Jeremiah 10.9. a defect of the instrumental particle; as Psalm 17.13,14. yet some render it without any such supply. See the next note.

*{him that smote the anvil*} Or, as others, *he that beateth out the metal on the anvil*. But the former word, in Hebrew, is a noun, not a verb; and signifies not *a smiter*, but *smiting* as another of the same stock, Prov. 18.6. & 19.29. and thence a term for *an hammer*, Judg. 5.26. the latter word nowhere else in Scripture found, for *an anvil* (though the Jewish doctors, some of them, so expound it; and, some other of them, *an hammer*) comes of a word, that signifies, *to shake*, or *disturb*, and *trouble*, Gen. 41.8. Psal. 77.4. Dan. 2.1,3. whence a term for *a bell*, Exod. 28.33,34. but it is most commonly and frequently used for *a course*, or *a turn*, Gen. 18.32. Josh. 6.3. Some, therefore, of the Jewish commenters, read this passage thus; *the carpenter encouraged the founder*, or, *the metallist that smooths the hammer, for smiting on the anvil*, or, *for smiting by turns*. And to confirm this, they call in the Chaldee paraphrase, from whence they gather, that the former word *pattish*, should signify *an hammer* of the greater size; *a sledge*, the latter, to wit, *paam*, one of a smaller size, it being say they, the manner of workmen, to make use of the greater, for the beating out of their work at first; and of the lesser, afterward, for the polishing of it. Whereas, other of them would have the former word to signify the lesser hammer; and the latter, the bigger: that which is more agreeable to the words of the text, wherein the former seems to be the polishing hammer. See Chap. 44.12. But the truth is, the Chaldee seems not to take the word *paam*, for any *hammer* at all, either bigger, or less; but expounds it by the word *zimna*, that answers to *paam*, as it signifies, *a turn*, or *course*. It uses a word, indeed, withal, that in the writings of the Talmudists, imports *an hammer*, of any sort or size indifferently; whether one to beat iron out, or one to crack nuts with; as by the places, out of their discourses produced, appears. But that seems to appertain to the exposition of the foregoing word *holem*. Nor do I find any place alleged, either out of sacred Scripture, or Talmudical writer, wherein the word is taken, either for *hammer*, or *anvil*. I suppose, therefore, that this passage may well be thus rendered, *and the smoother with the hammer, the smiter by course*; that is, *he that polished the work, him that wrought at the forge*. Heb. *smiting*, for a man of *smiting*; a smiter, or one that smites, as men of *derision*, for *deriders*: such as use to deride, Prov. 29.8. Chap. 28.14. a defect of the substantive regent. Of the like whereunto, see on ver. 2. Howsoever, thus must their gods be handled and hammered, ere they can attain their deity.

*{saying, It is ready for the soldering*} It is sufficiently beaten out at the anvil, it is now time to put the parcels of it together, and to fasten, with solder, the joints one to another. Or, as others, rather, more agreeably to the original; *saying, of the solder* (so is the particle used, Chap. 38.15.) or, *of the soldering*, (the word is nowhere else used, but for *joints*, or *junctures*, in the plural, 1 Kin. 22.34. 2 Chr. 18.33.) *it is good*, the pronoun, for the verb substantive; as ver. 4. It is well soldered, the joints are well fastened one to another.

*{and he fasteneth it with nails, that it should not be moved.*} They fasten with nails, either the frame of plates joined together with solder, unto the wooden stock underneath it, that the joints may keep the faster, and hold the firmer together, (as the Jewish commenters understand it) or the image, itself, to some wall, post, or pillar, that it may stand fast, in the place assigned it, and neither fall, nor be stirred; as most of ours take it. See chap. 40.19. and 46.7.

*{he fasteneth*} That is, some one of them, or other; the verb taken indefinitely, as Gen. 48.1. *he told* (that is, *one told*) *Joseph*.

*{fasteneth it*} The idol; such as is mentioned, Chapter 40.19. the pronoun, for the noun, as Chapter 33.2. and 35. ver. 2.

*{that it should not be moved*} Or, *that it stir not*; a defect of the particle, as Psalm 93.1. It is not to be omitted, that some of ours read the whole passage, from ver. 5. hitherto, not as spoken in way of relation, what the enemies of God, and his, did; but delivered, by way of permission, and provocation; as if it were said, *Let them, when at the sight of these things, they begin to be troubled, draw near, and convene; let them assist and encourage one another; let the idol-makers join together, and conspire to make their work as firm as they can*. See the like, chapter 8.9,10. Let others consider, and judge of it.

**V. 8.** *{But thou Israel art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.*} From the idolatrous pagans, God turns his speech to his own people, endeavoring to confirm and strengthen them, against all fear from the adverse party, undertaking to secure them, and make them successful against all that should oppose them.

*{But*} Heb. *And*; as ver. 8.

*{thou Israel art my servant*} Or, rather, *thou Israel my servant*: or, *who art my servant*: and so forward, in way of compellation and description of the party spoken to, unto ver. 10. of *Israel* and *Jacob*: see ch. 40.27. To him was the promise, made before to Abraham, solemnly renewed, Gen. 28.13,14.

*{my servant*} Not as all men, yea, all creatures are God's servants at large, Psal. 119.91. but in a more special manner, taken into his family, to be his household-servants, to have them near about him; and to reside, himself, among them, Levit. 25.42. & 26.11,12. Deut. 9.28. Psal. 22.30. & 148.14. Eph. 2.19. See ch. 43.1. & 44.1.

*{whom I have chosen*} To be a peculiar people to myself, Exod. 19.4,5. Deut. 7.6. Psalm 135.4. Heb. *whom I have chosen thee*; a redundancy in that language rife, Psa. 1.4. & 144.8. the like is in the next verse.

*{the seed of Abraham*} His posterity: as Psalm 105.6. 2 Cor. 11.22. whom God for his sake regarded, Deuter. 7.7. and 9.27. and 10.15.

*{my friend*} So 2 Chr. 20.7. Jam. 2.23. whom I freely loved, Deut. 4.37. and who entirely loved me, Gen. 22.12. and with whom I was pleased to enter into a solemn league of amity, as well defensive, as offensive, Gen. 12.2,3. & 15.1,18. & 17.2,7. Thus is God a friend, even to his friends' issue, as well as to himself, Exod. 20.6. Psa. 37.26. & 115.13,14.

**V. 9.** *{Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth,}* Heb. *whom I have taken thee*; as before, ver. 8. The word, *Thou*, is here needless: there is, as a redundancy in the pronoun, so a defect in the verb: entire and full, it is thus; *whom I have taken*, or *took*, and *brought from the ends of the earth*, or, *from the land's end*; as Psa. 72.8. v. 5. to wit, in Abraham, their progenitor, in whose loins they then were, (as Judg. 2.1. God is said to have brought them out of Egypt in their parents, then all deceased, Num. 14.29–31.) and whom God took and brought from the land of Chaldea, unto the land of Canaan, in which also, afterward, he settled his seed, Josh. 24.2,3. Of the supply, see on Chap. 38.17,21. and see the like, Gen. 27.9. Jer. 30.10. yet it follows not hence, as some would infer, that Abraham was the party mentioned before, ver. 2. for the sequel is of no necessity. And the next branch does exclude the exposition of those, who would understand this, of the bringing of the Israelites out of Egypt. Nor do they seem to go less wide, who, either with the Jewish doctors, understand this passage of the deliverance of them from the captivity of Babylon, a place far remote from their own home, Chap. 39.3. Jer. 30.10. Or, as some of ours, of the elect, called out of all parts of the world, by Christ, Chap. 56.6,7. Matth. 8.11.

*{and called thee from the chief men thereof*} So is the word used, Exod. 24.11. and it signifies great ones, *chief*, or *choice* men, so termed; as *reserved*, and *set apart* from others of less reckoning: as the word, whence it comes, imports, Gen. 27.36. Num. 11.17. Eccl. 2.10. a borrowed term, from things that are kept close and safe under the *arm-holes*, Ezek. 13.18. Jer. 38.12. meant of Abraham, whom God called out of Chaldea, from those great men there allied to him, or among whom he lived, Gen. 12.1. Josh. 24.2,3. So rather, than as some, from the great men, their hard masters in Babylon, chap. 26.13. & 43.14. Or, as others, of the elect called, when the great ones are passed by, Matth. 11.5,25. 1 Corinth. 1.26,27.

*{and said unto thee, Thou art my servant, I have chosen thee*} That is, *I made thee my servant*: or, made choice of thee to be my servant, as Ezek. 16.6. *I said to thee, live*; for, I saved thy life, or, kept thee alive: and, *say to my soul, I am thy salvation*, for, do thou save me, Psal. 35.3. and so it is, the same in effect with the former, ver. 8. or, I made it known to you, that I had made choice of you to be my servant, and would not cast you off, Gen. 17.7.

*{and not cast thee away*} Or, *and have not refused thee*; as the word is rendered, chap. 8.6. Or, *and I will not cast thee off*; as 2 King. 23.27. See 1 Sam. 12.22. Psal. 94.14. Jer. 31.37. & 33.26. Rom. 11.1,2.

**V. 10.** *{Fear thou not*} Ver. 13,14. Chap. 8.12. & 37.6. & 43.1,5. Lam. 3.57.

*{for I am with thee*} Gen. 15.1. & 26.3,24. & 46.4. Exod. 3.12. Chap. 43.2,5. Jer. 1.8,19. & 15.20. Acts 18.10. that is, security all-sufficient, Psalm 23.4. & 27.1,2. and 46.2,3,11. Romanes 8. ver. 31.

*{be not dismayed*} As those that have nothing but their idols to trust to, ver. 5. the word signifies properly, *to look about*, Chap. 17.7,8. Or, *to look aside*, Chap. 32.3. as men are wont to do, when they are in distress, Psal. 142.4. then *to be amazed*; as in such cases men oft are, Chap. 29.9. and lastly, *to be dismayed*, as here. See ver. 23. Jer. 46.27.

*{for I am thy God*} I the true God, endued with all power, am your God, Gen. 17.7. Psa. 48.14. & 84.11. & 144.15. Cha. 63.1.

*{I will strengthen thee*} Or, *I strengthen thee*: and so, *I help; I uphold*: See ver. 12. cha. 40.29,31. Psa. 46.1.

*{yea, I will help thee*} Psal. 46.5.

*{yea, I will uphold thee*} Psal. 41.12. & 63.13. Cha. 42.1. the redoubling of the particle adds much weight to the words: as chap. 40.24. importing, that no strength, or aid, or support, shall be wanting, that in any kind shall be needful for them, 2 Cor. 12.9.

*{with the right hand of my righteousness*} Or, *by my right hand of righteousness*: that is, *my righteous right hand*. See on cha. 2.20. & 30.33. *a right hand of righteousness*, for, *a righteous right hand*: Or, a right hand working righteously; as, *a right hand of falsehood*, Psalm 144.8,11. for, *a false right hand*: or, a right hand working falsely and fraudulently. *God's right hand*, for his acting power, Psa. 17.7,14. & 118.15,16. *his righteous right hand*, for his active power exercised in righting the wrongs done to his people, and in the faithful performance of his free promises made to them. See Chapter 1. ver. 27.

**V. 11.** *{Behold, all that were incensed against thee, shall be ashamed and confounded:*} Of the note prefixed, see Chap. 10.33. & 30.27. & 40.10. Before, was a promise of all strength, aid, and support, to God’s people: Now, a denunciation of shame, confusion, and utter destruction, of their enemies and opposites, Exod. 23.22. Zach. 12.3.

*{incensed against thee*} So ch. 45.24.

*{ashamed and confounded*} Psalm 25.3. and 40.14,15. and 139.5.

*{they shall be as nothing*} They shall come to nothing, or be as a thing of nought, ch. 40.17. V. 12. Or, *they shall be as if they were not, or never were*, ch. 40.23,24.

*{they that strive with thee shall perish*} Heb. *the men of thy strife, or, of thy quarrel, or, thy men of strife, or, quarrel*; they that strove or quarreled with you: So Job 31.35. See Psalm 35.1. Chap. 50.8.

**V. 12.** *{Thou shalt seek them, and shalt not find them*} Or, *Thou shalt seek them, but shalt not find them*; as Cant. 3.1. & 5.6. Or, *Though thou seek them, thou shalt not find them.* They shall be so destroyed, that you shall wonder to think what is become of them, Job 26.7–9. Psa. 9.5,6. & 10.15. & 37.35,36. Dan. 2.33.

*{even them that contended with thee*} Heb. *the men of thy contention, or, thy men of contention*; your contendents. See v. 11. The word comes of a verb, that signifies sometime, *to flight, or brawl*, as Num. 26.9. sometime *to fight, or bicker*, as Ps. 60. title, it may here import either, or include both.

*{they that war against thee*} Or, *that war against thee*; that it may run in the same tenor with the former. Heb. *the men of thy war, or, thy men of war*; not that warred with you; but that maintained war with you, or waged war against you.

*{shall be as nothing, and as a thing of nought*} The whole passage may well be thus rendered; *they that contended with thee, shall be as nothing*, (ch. 40.23. Ps. 39.5. Hag. 2.3.) Or, *as that which is not*, (Gen. 30.1. Chap. 37.3.) *and those that warred with thee, as nought*; as (ch. 34.12. & 40.17.) Or, *as that that is gone, or hath failed, and is not*, Gene. 47.15,16. chap. 5.8. & 16.4. & 29.20. for both the negative particles are, in substance, the same.

**V. 13.** *{For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand*} Or, *It is I the Lord thy God, that hold thy right hand*; that is, hold you by your right hand, to keep you up, Psalm 63.8. & 73.23. ch. 42.6. & 45.1. & 51.18. or, go hand in hand with you, to assist you, as your friend and fellow in fight, Psal. 83.8. See Prov. 11.21. or, *that strengthen thy right hand*; and enable you to prevail against all your opposites, Psalm 80.17. Ezekiah 30.25. Hos. 7.15. so is the word used, Dan. 11.1,6.

*{saying unto thee*} Heb. *that am saying*, as before, *am holding*; that say unto thee, Lam. 3.57. See on v. 9.

*{Fear not, I will help thee*} Or, *I help thee.* See v. 10.

**V. 14.** *{Fear not*} As before, v. 10,13. Repeated again and again, to confirm them against the consideration of their powerful enemies, and their own weak and low condition.

*{thou worm Jacob*} That are such in the eye and estimation of your enemies, who trampled upon you as such a contemptible creature. See Job 25.6. Psa. 22.6.

*{and ye men of Israel*} Or, as some render it, *ye few men*: and so the ancient Greek: but then it should be, *men of number*, as Gen. 34.30. Deut. 4.27. Jer. 44.23. Others, *ye dead men*, that are as dead men, ch. 26.19. Ezek. 37.11–14. and so the old Latin. But they mistake the vocal point, for *men*, and *dead men*, in Hebrew, differ but in a vowel. Yet had they said *mortals*, it had not been much amiss. See on ch. 2.9.

*{I will help thee*} Or, *I help thee*: I am your assistant, verse 10,13.

*{saith the Lord, and thy Redeemer, the holy One of Israel*} Or, *even thy Redeemer*: that is, deliverer, and rescuer. So is the particle used, chap. 40.30. See chap. 54.5.

**V. 15.** *{Behold*} As Chap. 7.14. ver. 11.

*{I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument, having teeth*} Heb. *I have made thee* like unto such a cart, or sled, as they used to thresh out their harder grain with. Of which, see on chap. 28.25,28. (the note of similitude is wanting, as chap. 40.6.) a new one: and in that regard, the stronger, and sharper, being neither worn, nor blunted with use: as 2 Samu. 21.16.

*{sharp threshing instrument*} Two words are here used: the former whereof, *morag*, signifies a sled, in general, 2 Sam. 24.22. 1 Chr. 21.23. not found elsewhere: the latter, *charuts*, more peculiarly such an one, as was used, commonly, for threshing out of corn, chap. 28.25,28. as also, sometime, to torture men with, 2 Sam. 12.31. Amos 1.3. so called from a verb that signifies *to cut*, yet not, as *cut*, as some would have it: though the form be passive: and it is so, when taken for a *ditch*, Dan. 9.25. but of *cutting*, because it cuts the straw, in threshing out of the grain: nor is it an adjective, as our version makes it, rendering it *sharp*, but a substantive, either joined to the former, by apposition, as his fellow, in way of specification, as *a damsel, a virgin*, Deut. 22.28. *a woman, a widow*, 2 Sam. 14.5. *a woman, an harlot*, Judg. 11.1. *a man, an eunuch*, Act. 8.28. and so here, *a sled, a threshing one*; or, ruled by the former, as Joel 3.14. *the valley of the threshing, or, of the threshing sled*: or, as some there render it, *of concision, or cutting*: and so here, *a sled of cutting: or threshing*, that is, *a cutting or threshing sled*, to distinguish it from other sleds, that are used for other purposes.

*{having teeth*} Heb. *a master, or owner of mouths*: as, *an owner of wing*, for *a winged fowl*; or *one that hath wing*, Prov. 1.17. and *an owner of horn*, for *an horned creature*, or *one that hath horns*, Dan. 8.6. mouths, for *teeth*, or the like: here a sled, whose wheels are furnished with iron-spokes, or teeth, as we commonly term them, chapter 28.28. Amos 1.3. as *a sword of mouths*, for *a double edged sword*, Psalm 149.6. Prov. 5.4. and *a two-mouthed*, for, *a two-edged sword*, Heb. 4.12. and *to fall on, or by, the mouth*, for *the edge of the sword*, Genesis 34.26. Exodus 17.13. Luke 21.24.

*{thou shalt thresh the mountains*} I will make you able, not to withstand only, but to over-master, subdue, and destroy all your enemies, (see Judg. 6.7. 2 Kings 13.7. chapter 25.10. Amos 1.3.) be they never so great, or, strong, so lofty, or mighty, chapter 2.14. Zach. 4.7. fulfilled, as in many glorious victories, as well as deliverances, at sundry times vouchsafed God’s people, after their return from captivity, Zach. 2.5. & 12.2,3,6. so principally, and more fully accomplished in the reign of the Messiah, Dan. 2.34,35,44,45. 2 Cor. 10.4,5.

*{and shalt beat them small*} Or, *to small dust, or powder*. So the word properly signifies, Exod. 32.20. & 30.36. 2 Kings 23.7,15. chap. 29.5. you shall thresh them in another manner than corn is wont to be threshed. See chap. 28.28. See also, Matth. 21.44. a defect of the pronoun, as our reading yields it; such as Chapter 40.15. yet it may be rendered without such supply, *thou shalt thresh, and beat, or grind to dust, or powder, the mountains*.

*{and shalt make the hills as chaff*} See verse 1,16. Psalm 18.43.

**V. 16.** *{Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them*} You shall disperse them, and make an utter riddance of them; not like chaff, that stays in the floor, when the grain is there winnowed, reserved for some further use; but that, which upon winnowing in some open and high place, in a stiff wind, is carried clean away; or, upon winnowing on the floor, is, by the whisking of the wind, blown out of the floor, and so scattered, that it cannot be recollected; See Jer. 4.11. & 15.7. & 51.1,2. Dan. 2.35.

*{and thou shalt rejoice in the Lord, and glory in the holy One of Israel*} Or, *but* (as v. 8.) *thou shalt rejoice in the Lord* (as Ps. 9.14. & 13.5. & 14.6.) *thou shalt glory*, (as c. 42.14.) or *boast thyself*, (as Jer. 9.22,23.) *of the holy One of Israel*, ver. 14,16. ascribing to him, whatsoever he has enabled you to do, or has done for you, ch. 12.1,6. & 25.1–5. & 26.1–6.

**V. 17.** *{When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst; I the Lord will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them*} When my people, detained in captivity at Babylon, or elsewhere, Zach. 9.12. or by the way in their return home from thence, through waste places, v. 18,19. shall be in distress, through want of water, or other necessaries; and consequently, when any poor soul shall be in perplexity for want of any spiritual consolation, I the Lord will not be wanting unto them, for any necessary supply, Chapter 12.3. John 4.10. and 7.37. 2 Corin. 12.9. A defect of the particle *when*: as chapter 17.6. & 26.10. v. 5.

*{hear them*} By a gracious supply, show, that I have heard them, even by satisfying their desires, chap. 59.9,10. Psal. 107.5,6,9. Hos. 2.22.

*{their tongue faileth for thirst*} Sticking to the roof of their mouth, for want of moisture, Ps. 22.15. & 137.6. Lam. 2.11. *faileth*, as ch. 19.5. Jer. 51.30.

*{I the God of Israel*} Hereby showing himself so to be, verse 10,13.

*{will not forsake them*} Gen. 28.15. Josh. 1.5. 1 Sam. 12.22. Heb. 13.5. verse 9.

**V. 18.** *{I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water*} I will alter the very course of nature, and cause those places to yield water, where none ordinarily is, rather than my people shall want means of comfortable subsistence; an allusion to those extraordinary courses taken by him, for the supply of his with water in the wilderness, what time they traveled from Egypt to Canaan, Exod. 17.6,7. Num. 20.10,11. Ps. 105.41. & 107.35. & 114.8. ch. 35.7. & 44.3.

*{high places*} See Jeremiah 12.12. and 14.6. Howbeit, a learned late writer, would have it rather, *in low places*; as after, *in the valleys, in the plains*. See Chapter 13.1. Jer. 3.2. But it is rather *in high places*, in opposition to the valleys; in places as well of the one condition, as the other. See chap. 30.25. a place parallel to this.

*{in the midst of the valleys*} Or, *in the valleys*, as ch. 19.19. & 24.13. See Deut. 8.7. Ps. 104.8,10.

*{dry land*} Heb. *land of dryness*: as Psalm 63.1. Chapter 35.1. & 53.2.

*{springs*} Heb. *goings out, or issues*: and so, Ps. 107.33,35. for there is another term for *springs or fountains*, as before. See Ps. 74.14. & 84.9. ch. 12.3.

**V. 19.** *{I will plant in the wilderness, the cedar, the Shittah-tree, and the myrtle, and the oil-tree: I will set in the desert the fir-tree, the pine, and the box-tree together*} I will not furnish them (only) with water, to quench their thirst; but beset the way which they are to pass by, (where the heat of the sun might, for want of shade, annoy them, as in wild wastes, it oft falls out,) with such shroudy trees, as shall afford them shade, and may much refresh them in their travel, cha. 55.12,13. Yet the meaning is not, that God would, by miracle, cause such kind of trees to spring up in the way, where no such were before; but that he would, by his providence and provision, make their passage as convenient & commodious unto them, as if such a thing had been done. So v. 3. see Ps. 105.39. chap. 4.5,6. & 32.2.

*{plant*} Or, *place, or set*. Hebrews *give*: as Gen. 39.20. 2 Chr. 6.13. & 18.10.

*{cedar*} A goodly tree for shroud and shade, Ezek. 31.3.

*{Shittah-tree*} Divers conceits concerning this kind of tree, what it should be, because groundless, I spare to relate. The most of the Jewish commenters suppose it to be a choice kind of cedar; in regard whereof, some of them make the cedar here mentioned, and it, but one and the same tree; as if it were said, *the cedar of Shittah*; that is, the cedar that yields the Sittah-wood; which appears to have been a wood of some special note and worth. See Exod. 25.5. & 35.7,24. but they seem rather to be reckoned up here, as trees distinct, in like manner, as the rest. It is nowhere found mentioned in Scripture, save here, and about the furniture of the tabernacle. Concerning which, what fables the Talmudists tell us, of the Israelites planting them in Egypt, by Jacobs admonition, and their carrying the wood thereof out of Egypt, by Moses his direction; and of an whole wood of them, growing near to Mount Sinai, that the people should fell, wherewith to make them tabernacles, I forbear to insist on.

*{myrtle*} A very pleasant and delightful tree, of a fragrant smell, in regard whereof, it was, by the painims, dedicated to Venus: thence had Ester her name, Hadassah, Est. 2.7. by the Greek historians termed Atossa; the branches whereof, travelers, for their refreshment, (and as by them deemed to have some efficacy to keep them from weariness in travel) used to carry in their hands, by the way. See Pliny, liber 15. Chapter 29. it is reckoned among the shadowy trees, Nehemiah 8.15. See Zachariah 1.1.8.

*{oil-tree*} Heb. *tree of oil*; the olive tree, whose fruit yields oil, Exodus 30.24. Judges 9.9. Romanes 11.17. hence *the sucking of oil out of the flinty rock*; that is, from those rocky places, on which the olive trees grew, Deut. 32.13. Of the beauty and shadiness of it, see Hos. 14.6,7.

*{fir*} About this tree, also, there is some dissent among the Jewish masters, but the most agree it to be a fir: which is the more likely, because musical instruments were made of the wood thereof, as at this day with us, 2 Sam. 6.5. It is joined oft with the cedar, ch. 14.8. & 37.24. Zach. 11.2. See ch. 55.13. & 60.13. in which place, all these latter three trees are mentioned, and joined, as here, *together*.

*{pine*} This word being nowhere else found, but here, and chap. 60.13. is very ambiguous; the Rabbines, after their manner, where they are as uncertain, as others, say, it is a kind of cedar, and so leave us at random. Most of ours take it to be the pine, or the pitch tree: which some guess to be so called, from the noise that the branches thereof make, when they are shaken with the wind: and the root, whence it seems to spring, is used of such a noise, as horses use to make, trampling, or prancing with their feet, Judg. 5.22. Nahum. 3.2. Others derive it from an Arabic word, that signifies *eternity*: either because it holds his verdure all the year long: as some kind of flower, thence called by the Greeks, *Amarantum*, alluded to, 1 Pet. 5.4. & with us *everlasting*; or, because, though the wood, or timber thereof, is of long continuance: for they seem to stray further, who, by change of a letter, yet not altogether unusual, would have it deduced, either from the rosin, that it yields, or from another Arabic word, found in that version, Hos. 14.6. that signifies *to flourish*.

*{box-tree*} Of this, also, the Rabbines tell us, that it is a kind of cedar. Yet some of them say, that it is the brasil tree: and some, as our version has it, the box: it is no oftener found, than the former. Nor can I assent to a writer of great note, who in his version, renders it, *shadowy trees*, such, as groves commonly consist of, whence he would have them so named: as if it denoted no particular kind of tree: but such, in general, as yields much shade: such as those reckoned up, Nehemiah 8.15. and those pointed to, Hos. 4.13.

**V. 20.** *{That they may see, and know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of the Lord hath done this, and the holy One of Israel hath created it*} Or, *That men may see, and know, &c.* other people, as well as God’s own: for the verbs are indefinite. So Psalm 109.27. a place parallel to this. See ch. 40.26. verse 4.

*{consider*} Hebrews *lay*: to wit, their heart, to these things, or these things to heart: as it is more fully, ver. 22. cha. 42.25. Hag. 1.5,7.

*{the holy One of Israel*} ver. 14,16.

*{created it*} Has appointed it so to be: as Chapter 37.26. or, has effected it: the word is used, as of the creation and production of the creatures at first, Chapter 40.26. and 45.12,18. so, of strange works that may justly be deemed as works of creation, ch. 4.5. Jerem. 31.22.

**V. 21.** *{Produce your cause, saith the Lord*} Heb. *cause to come near*; as ch. 46.13.

*{bring forth your strong reasons*} Heb. *make to come near* (as Exod. 21.6. 1 Sam. 14.18. for the words are both of the same notion,) *your strong*, to wit, reasons, or arguments: a defect of the subject: as chap. 40.10.

*{saith the King of Jacob*} Psalm 44.4. and 89.18. and 149.2. cha. 33.22. God turns his speech to the idolatrous people, challenging them to produce the strongest pleas they can, in the behalf of their idols; and to prove the truth of their religion, by producing the like works foretold first, and effected afterward, by those whom they adore, to those of his before-mentioned, when they shall see them accomplished; and withal, take notice, how long before, warning had been given of them. See verse 1,2.

**V. 22.** *{Let them bring them forth, and show what shall happen*} A defect of the pronoun, as ver. 15. or, rather, without any supply, here needless; *Let them come forth, and declare what will happen.* Let your idols do it. He challenged the idolaters, before, to say what they could, for their idols. He tells them here, what he would have their idols to do. See ver. 23. There is an elegant consonancy in the Hebrew words, which our language cannot well express.

*{Let them show the former things what they be*} Let them show what they can foretell, or effect; or have formerly foretold and effected. So ch. 44.7. & 45.20,21. & 46.10. and 48.14.

*{that we may consider them*} Heb. *and we will* (as ch. 37.26. & 53.3.) *set our heart upon them*. See v. 21.

*{and know the latter end of them*} Or, *the issue of them*; how they came afterward to pass. Heb. *the posterity of them*; as Deut. 32.20.

*{or declare us things for to come*} Heb. *make us to hear* (as v. 26. Ps. 51.8.) *things to come*; as Gen. 41.35.

**V. 23.** *{Show the things that are to come hereafter; that we may know that ye are gods*} As verse 2. see verse 20. Hebrews. *And we shall know*; which may well be retained, else, as before, verse 22. the copulative, for the finitive.

*{yea, do good, or do evil*} To your friends, the one; to your enemies, the other; as I, for mine; verse 10–20. but neither of both can you do, Jer. 10.5. & 14.22.

*{that we may be dismayed, and behold it together*} Heb. *and we shall be astonished, or amazed, or dismayed* (as verse 5. and *behold*, before *and we shall know, and behold*: a defect of the pronoun, *it*; such as ch. 37.1,9. Or, (because sight goes, in nature, before astonishment, or amazement, as verse 5. (*when we see it*; as ch. 31.3. & 43.11. Jer. 34.1. Zach. 12.2.

**V. 24.** *{Behold, ye are of nothing*} See 1 Cor. 8.1. Or, *ye are less, or worse than nothing*: the particle is oft used, in a comparative notion: as Psalm 8.5. Job 11.6. the pronoun, for the verb substantive: as v. 10,29.

*{and your work of nought*} The work that is done about you, or by you: all that is done with you, or that yourselves do, is *less, or worse than nought*, as verse 29. or *worse than that of a viper*: so the word lengthened with one subservient letter, is found used, Job 20.16. Chap. 30.6. & 59.5. they are of less worth, than the hissing of such a serpent: or they do not only no good nor benefit, but much mischief to those that adore them, and adhere to them, Psalm 16.4.

*{an abomination is he that chooseth you*} To worship as gods, chap. 44.17. or, *most abominable* (as Lev. 18.22. ch. 1.13.) *is he that* (a defect both of the verb substantive, antecedent, and relative, as Jer. 2.8,11.) *delighteth in you*: as ch. 1.29. & 58.5,6.

**V. 25.** *{I have raised up one from the North, and he shall come*} God having challenged the false gods, to show what they have done, or can do: does now again relate, what himself had done. Some render the verbs, both, in the time to come, *I will raise up, and he shall come.* And they supply, for want of the noun following, the former verb, not one, as our version, as of a particular person: but a people: which does not recede much from the former, since that party, albeit he were but one, it is certain that he brought people, yea, peoples along with him. But we need not depart from the words of the original, that runs thus: *I raised up one, and he came*: (for so it was before, v. 2. in the question there, which this answers to, here, and it is spoken here, as of a thing already accomplished, as there: so ch. 43.14. & 45.13.) or, *I raised up one that he might come, or to come*: as v. 22,24. to wit, at my call.

*{from the rising of the sun shall he call upon my name:*} Or, *from the rising of the sun, one that might proclaim, or to proclaim my name*: as Exod. 33.14. Now, this some understand of Nebuchadnezzar the former, that subdued and captived God’s people, said, everywhere, to come from the North, Jer. 1.13,15. & 4.6. of Cyrus, the latter, that delivered them out of captivity, and is said to come from the East, Chapter 46.11. to show, say they, that both their captivity by the one and delivery by the other, were of God’s appointment and disposal. But I conceive, rather, with others, that Cyrus, is the party intended in either, who was a *Medo-Persian*, himself, of a medley race: a Persian, by Cambyses his father: and a Mede, by Mandane his mother, and carried along with him, in his expedition against Babylon, of his subjects out of both kingdoms, some out of Media, that lay more northerly to it, Jer. 50.3,9. others, out of Persia, that lay more to the East of it, ver. 2. Chap. 46.11. Yet some expound it of Christ, that should gather his dispersed out of all parts of the world, Psalm 107.3. Chap. 43.5,6. & 49.12. Mat. 8.11. Joh. 11.52. of whom Cyrus was a type. Howbeit, they make over-large reckonings, who by the *sun-rising*, would understand East and West; by the *North*, North and South, to hook in the whole world.

*{call upon my name*} So did Cyrus, say some, because the Persians worshiped no idols; but, rather, *proclaim my name*; as did Nebuchadnezzar, say some, who both praised him, himself, and proclaimed him to others, Jer. 39.11,12. & 40.2,3. Dan. 3.28,29. and 4.2,3,34. but it seems rather to have reference to that solemn proclamation of Cyrus: whereof, see 2 Chron. 36.22,23. Ezr. 1.1,2.

*{and he shall come upon Princes, as upon mortar, and as the potter treadeth clay*} Or, *that he might come* (as the like before) *or go* (as Gen. 7.1. Ezek. 36.22.) and tread down, or trample upon princes. (See the like defective, or comprehensive forms of speech, cha. 38.17,21. howbeit, the supply here, is from the branch ensuing, as ch. 23.5.) *as mortar, and he as a potter that treadeth clay*: a defect of the relative; as v. 24. see Psa. 18.42. Nah. 3.14.

*{Princes*} Such as God shall subdue to him; as Astyages, Cresus, Baltasar, and others. See ver. 2. chap. 45.1. or rather the Babylonian captains and commanders, Jer. 51.28,57.
