**V. 26.** *{Who hath declared from the beginning, that we may know? and before time, that we may say, he is righteous?*} Which of your gods did, or could, foretell this, that I foretold above one hundred, well near two hundred year, before it came to pass; and, you see, at length, fulfilled? See on chapter 13.22. See also, chapter 43.9.

*{declared*} See v. 22,23. or *declared this*: as ch. 45.21. & 48.14. See the like defect, 1 Cor. 9.10.

*{from the beginning*} Heb. *head*: as ch. 40.21. & 48.16. that is, long before: as in the next branch, *before time; or from before time*. Heb. *from before, or, from to the faces*: as Jer. 7.24.

*{that we may know*} Heb. *and we shall know*: as ver. 23. and so afterward, *and we shall say*.

*{He is righteous?*} He is to be justified and allowed of, in his claim, to a deity, he may justly go for a god; or, may deservedly, claim the name of a god, Deut. 25.1. cha. 43.9. See v. 23. and the like defect, 2 King. 10.9. Prov. 24.24. ch. 3.10,11. & 43.10,11. A late learned writer would rather have it rendered, *he is true*; because the word, in Arabic, is so commonly used; and *righteousness*, where it is given to God, does oft signify *truth*, as chap. 42.21. & 45.23. So the Chaldee, and the Greek, here: *it is truth*, the one; *true*, the other. And he renders thus the whole passage, *who will declare former things? we will know* (or acknowledge him, or them) *and those things that were before? we will say, he is true.* Let others judge of it.

*{yea, there is none that showeth, yea, there is none that declareth, yea, there is none that heareth your words*} There is never an idol of you, that foretold aught of it; nor priest, or prophet, belonging unto either of them, that reported it (Heb. *making to hear*: as ver. 22. ch. 52.7. & 53.1.) from them; nor any of your worshipers, that has heard aught of it, either from yourselves, or from any of you, by any of them, since neither yourselves can speak aught, Psal. 115.5. and 135.16. nor are any of your priests and interpreters able to say aught thereof, chap. 47.12,13. The repetition of the particle, makes the speech more emphatical: as chap. 40.24. So verse 23.

**V. 27.** *{The first shall say to Zion; Behold, behold them, and I will give to Jerusalem one that bringeth good tidings*} Or, as some, *I the first* (that is, God, v. 4.) *will say to Zion, Behold, behold them*: Or, as others, *I will give a prime, or chief one to Zion*, to wit, Christ, Cant. 5.10.) *and a bringer of good tidings to Jerusalem*, who shall say, *Behold, behold them.* Or, as others, again, *I will first give to Zion, and to Jerusalem, one joyfully publishing, Behold, behold them.* But these, all, invert the words of the text too much. I suppose the words may be best thus rendered, with least force to the text, and most fitness with the context, *I say first to Zion, Behold, behold them; and give to Jerusalem a bringer of glad tidings.*

*{The first shall say*} Or, *I first say, or said*; I am the first that signified aught to Sion, either concerning her deliverance, or the destruction of Babylon; and the persons, by whom either of these should be effected, that which none of your idols, or wizards, could do, v. 26. a defect of the verb: as Psa. 27.8.

*{Behold, behold them*} That is, say some, the things now foretold, and then fulfilled: but the pronoun is not a neuter, but a masculine, as our version well renders it: which some expound of the people under Cyrus his command, coming to ruin Babylon, and to release God’s people. See Cha. 13.4,5. & 21.9. Jer. 51.41,44. Others, of the Jews returning in flocks, and troops, from captivity. See ch. 49.12. the repetition adds more vehemency and evidence to it: as Cha. 65.1.

*{will give*} Or, *do give*: do send, do assign.

*{to Jerusalem*} This, and *Sion*, here, are all one: as Chap. 1.27. & 40.9.

*{one that bringeth good tidings*} That is, Cyrus, say some, Ezr. 1.1,2. Christ, say other, Chap. 42.1. & 61.1. John Baptist, say other, chap. 40.3. the prophet Esay, say others, who foretold all this, see chap. 61.1. But I conceive that no peculiar, or particular messenger, is here meant, but that the word is used collectively, *messenger, for messengers*: as Chap. 40.9. and 52.6,7.

**V. 28.** *{For I beheld, and there was no man; even among them, and there was no counselor, that when I asked of them, could answer a word*} God here drawing to a conclusion of the controversy, concerning the deity, or divine power of idols, and having formerly summoned all their proctors and patrons, to come in and plead for them, ver. 1,21. does now address himself to pass sentence, as a judge, where none appears in behalf of the party questioned, neither himself, nor any for him, that since they are not able to produce aught in their own defense, nor any other, in their behalf; he therefore concludes against them, that there is no matter of deity in them, but that they are mere vanity, counterfeit gods, and base idols, verse 29.

*{For I beheld*} Heb. *And I beheld*: that is, *But I looked about*, as ch. 31.2. Or, *Now when I looked about*, to see whether any would make appearance: as v. 17. ch. 30.20. & 35.4. & 37.9,36. Psa. 142.4. so afterward.

*{there was no man*} Or, *not any*, ch. 40.20. for it is used, not of man alone, but of any creature whatsoever.

*{even among them*} As v. 12. any of their idols. For I cannot agree with those, that understand it of God’s people: as chap. 59.16. and 63.3. the whole course of the context runs another way.

*{no counselor*} None that could give any advice what was fit to be done, ch. 45.21.

*{that when I asked of them, could answer a word*} Heb. *and I asked of them, and they returned* (the same construction with that before) *a word or aught*, Job 13.22. Jer. 26.2. Mat. 22.46. the verb taken potentially: as Jer. 2.23,32.

**V. 29.** *{Behold, they are all vanity*} Jer. 10.3,15.

*{their works are nothing*} See ver. 24.

*{their molten images are wind and confusion*} Molten images, distinguished from graven images, chap. 48.5. but put here for images of all sorts, both the one, and the other, promiscuously, as Jer. 10.14. & 51.17.

*{wind*} Of no solidity, stability, efficacy, or utility; but such as cause much sorrow and vexation to those that have dealing with them, Psal. 16.3. v. 24. Jer. 10.15. in regard whereof, they are sometime termed by a word that signifies *sorrow and pain*, chap. 10.10. and 48.5. like a puff of wind that passes away, and cannot be held or kept, Psal. 78.39. Prov. 10.15. & 27.16. and blasts, sometime, in its passage, Psalm 103.16. chap. 40.7. Ezek. 17.10. being no solid substance, cannot feed or nourish, Prov. 11.29. Hos. 12.1. yea, being enclosed in the body and bowels, not only affords no nutriment, and is a fit emblem, therefore, of labor in vain, whereof comes no emolument, Eccles. 5.16. Hos. 8.7. but disturbs digestion, hinders concoction, and produces, oft, pain, and torments intolerable, Chap. 26.18.

*{confusion*} Of this term, see on chap. 24.10. & 34.11. & 40.17,23.

### CHAPTER 42

**Ver. 1.** This chapter, and the two next ensuing, which together make up but one sermon, are much of one subject, relating and foretelling the blessings that God would confer upon his people; partly, by Cyrus, and partly, yea, principally by Christ, discovering the vanity of idols, and sottishness of idolaters, taxing his people for their incredulity, blindness, excesses, and obstinacy, the causes of their captivity; and yet promising pardon and restitution, upon their sincere repentance.

*{Behold my servant*} The words of God the Father, speaking of Christ, as the evangelist expounds and applies it, Mat. 12.18. so called, in regard of his human nature, and office of Mediatorship, Chap. 49.3. & 53.11. Phil. 2.7. Rom. 15.8. on whom are all the promises of God founded, Gen. 22.18. and ratified in him, 2 Cor. 1.20. And of the Messiah does the Chaldee paraphrast expound it, and some of the Jewish commenters, after him. Howbeit, some of them expound it of Cyrus; which some of ours, also, but as a type of Christ, admit. See Chap. 44.28. & 45.1. And if it be objected, that some things, hereafter spoken, will not agree to Cyrus, it is by them answered, that in the like prophecies, some particulars agree to the type, and not to the truth: as Psalm 22.6. & 40.12. Some to the truth, and not to the type: as Psalm 16.10. with Acts 2.29. and 13.36,37. Or, to the type, in one sense, to the truth, in another. So in those Psalms, wherein David is a type of Christ: as Psalm 2. and 16. and 22. and those, in which Solomon: as Psalm 45. and 72. Some things are spoken, that must, of necessity, be understood of them, in one notion, of Christ, in another: of Pharao’s daughter espoused to Solomon, and the church, to Christ, the one typified by the other, Psalm 45. the same may be said. Others of them, again, understand it of Jacob, and Israel (which the ancient Greek, therefore, has over-boldly thrust into the text) and the godly of his posterity, because the term is so oft given unto them, Chap. 41.8,9. and 44.1,2. & 21.24. & 45.4. & 48.20. And others, of the prophet Esay, unto whom they apply those places, Chap. 43.10. & 44.26. & 49.5. which a late writer also avows. But these two latter carry no probability at all with them.

*{whom I uphold*} Whom I am with, to strengthen, support and enable him, unto the office and work that I have assigned him, Ch. 49.5,8. Christ principally, chapter 53.10. John 16.32. & 17.4. Cyrus, as a type of him, chapter 45.1,2,5. Or, as the Jewish doctors read it, *whom I lean upon*: as kings do on those that serve them, 2 Kings 5.18. & 7.2,13. whom I trust unto, or rely upon, for the performance of what I entrust him with: and this, also, many of ours admit. See of Christ, Heb. 3.2. of Cyrus, chapter 44.28. But I find not where the word, here used, has this notion; the former, very commonly and constantly, Exodus 17.12. Psalm 16.5. & 17.5. & 41.12. & 63.8. cha. 33.15. & 41.10,13. and to that, therefore, I adhere. Heb. *I will uphold him*, the demonstrative, for the relative: as chapter 33.20,21.

*{mine Elect*} Or, *choice one*: the term is used of Moses, Psalm 106.23. of Saul, 2 Samuel 21.6. of Israel and Jacob, and his posterity, Psalm 105.6,43. & 106.5. chapter 43.20. & 45.4. & 65.9,15. See chapter 14.1. & 41.8,9. & 44.1,2. of Christ true, in a more special manner, set apart by God, for the work of mediation, chapter 43.10. John 6.27,29. & 10.36. 1 Peter 1.20. & 2.4. of Cyrus, as a type, designed for the deliverance of God’s people, chapter 44.28. & 45.3,4.

*{in whom my soul delighteth*} Or, *is well pleased*; Deuteronomy 33.11,24. Ezekiel 20.40. who alone is in special manner acceptable to me, Matthew 3.17. & 17.5. and no means of reconcilement, or free access to me, but by him, John 14.6. Ephesians 1.4,6. & 2.14,18. a defect of the relative: as Genesis 39.4. chapter 40.20. & 41.3. verse 5. and by a metaphorical respect had to man, *his soul*, for himself: as chapter 1.14. Amos 6.8. with Hebrews 6.13. which yet may have some reference to Cyrus, in regard of the work done by him, and, by God, accepted of, for the good of his people, Chapter 45.3,4. and whom he is, therefore, said to affect. See Chapter 48.14.

*{I have put my spirit upon him*} Or, *on whom I have put my spirit*: the like defect, with that in the first branch. Of Christ, see chapter 11.2. and 61.1. John 1.33,34. and 3.34. of Cyrus, see Ezr. 1.1. as of Sampson, Judges 13.25. and of Saul, 1 Samuel 10.9,10.

*{he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles*} He shall be their governor, executing judgment upon them, and among them, calling, converting, conquering, subduing, ruling, and over-ruling them by his word and Spirit, Psalm 2.8. and 45.4,5. and 110.2. chapter 2.3,4. and 49.6. Revelations 6.2. and 19.11–16. So of Christ: Of Cyrus, as proclaiming God’s mind and purpose to all people, concerning the restitution of his people, and executing of his judgment on those that detained God’s people in captivity, and such as adhered to them, Ezra 1.1. See verse 3.

**V. 2.** *{He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the streets*} Of Christ, some expound it, that he shall not come with noise and stir, or with pomp and state, as worldly princes and potentates are wont to do, but in a meek, still, quiet, and lowly manner, Zachary 9.9. Matthew 12.14,19. and 21.5. Others, that he shall not carry himself contentiously, and clamorously, with passion and perturbation; (for *anger and clamor*, go commonly together, Ephesians 4.31. and persons possessed with wrath and rage, are so loud, many times, that they may be heard abroad in the streets: therefore, Matthew renders it, *he shall not contend*) but shall advisedly and considerately demean himself, and dispose things with tranquility and calmness of spirit, chapter 11.2. (in which sense, also, some apply it to Cyrus) The Hebrew commenters conceive it to have respect unto worldly judges; who, in keeping courts, are fain to speak with extension of voice and vehemency, to cause men to keep silence, and attend to their dooms; which the Messiah shall not need, men being of themselves ready to hear and obey him, though speaking calmly and quietly to them, Genesis 49.10. 1 Kings 19.12. Psalm 18.44,45. Chapter 2.3.

*{lift up*} *his voice*: to be supplied from the following branch: as chapter 30.17. So verse 11. Yet some of the Rabbines supply, *face: He shall not lift up faces.* That is, *He shall not respect the person of any*, Exodus 23.3. Deuteronomy 16.19. 2 Chronicles 19.7. Matthew 22.16. Romanes 2.8–11. But the former seems the plain and genuine sense of the place.

**V. 3.** *{A bruised reed he shall not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench:*} Either, as the Jewish commenters, he shall not tyrannize over, but nourish and cherish the poor and feeble ones, such as are wont, by great ones, to be oppressed, Psalm 72.2,4,12–14. Ezek. 34.22,23. Or, as most of ours, he shall not deal roughly and rigorously with weak and tender souls, but shall support and strengthen them, deal mildly and gently with them, and be tender-hearted towards them, chapter 40.11,29–31. Ezek. 34.14. Some apply it to Cyrus, as an instrument of delivering and rescuing God’s then poor and feeble ones, as a shepherd his sheep, out of the hands of their oppressors, and from those countries, into which, by their cruelty, they had been scattered, chapter 44.28. and 45.13. Ezek. 34.4–6,12,13.

*{a bruised reed*} Or, *cane*. An emblem of inability, and imbecility: See chapter 36.6.

*{the smoking flax*} *Flax*, that is, a wick of flax; as *flax*, for *strings, or, threads of flax*, Judges 15.14. And so fully, *threads of tow*, Judges 16.9. *smoking*; having more smoke, than light, chapter 50.10. or, *burning dimly*, almost spent, and ready to go out; as those that are dim-sighted, and can hardly see, having almost lost their eyesight, of whom the word is used, Genesis 27.1. 1 Samuel 3.2. Zechariah 11.17.

*{not quench*} As chapter 43.17. Heb. *not quench it*: a redundancy: as Genesis 2.17. Matthew 21.41. He shall not blow out, but blow up, raise, trim, supply, snuff, and make to burn brighter, Exodus 27.21. 1 Samuel 3.3. The positive implied in the privative: as in the branch foregoing.

*{he shall bring forth judgment unto truth*} Though he favor the weak, yet shall he not spare the wicked, but judge according to truth and equity, Exodus 23.2,3,6. Leviticus 19.15. Deuteronomy 16.20. chapter 11.3,4. John 7.24. See verse 1,4. *truth* is used sometime for, *equity and fidelity*, Judges 9.16. chapter 38.3. and 48.1. sometime, for *the due and full performance of aught*, Joshua 2.12. 2 Samuel 7.28. John 1.14,17. It may well be taken either way here.

**V. 4.** *{He shall not fail, nor be discouraged, until he have set judgment in the earth*} He shall not faint, nor be disheartened, in regard of those difficulties that shall encounter him, in his pursuit of the work enjoined him, but go on courageously, until he have dispatched it: See John 17.4. Hebrews 12.1,3. See also chapter 45.1,2,5,13. The evangelist renders it, Matthew 12.20. *until he bring forth judgment unto victory.* That is, until he have overcome all oppositions that he shall meet withal, in the execution of the judgment to be executed by him, according to God’s purpose and appointment; and subdued all the enemies and oppressors of God’s people. This of Christ, see Romanes 8.36. and 16.20. 1 Corinthians 15.25. Revelations 3.21. and 6.2. Of Cyrus, chapter 44.28. and 45.1.

*{fail*} As a lamp, or taper, does when it is even spent, and the oil, or wax, that fed it, fails. For it is the same word that was of a wick, verse 3. And some, therefore, expound it of seeing clearly, and discerning things aright in judgment, chapter 11.2,3. See Deuteronomy 34.7. Zechariah 11.17. And they expound the whole passage thus; He shall be neither misled by ignorance and mistake; nor forced aside through fear. But I conceive the former here intended, when men faint, their eyesight fails, 1 Samuel 14.29. Lam. 5.17. For they are wide, who expound it, He shall do nothing in passion, or anger; because of that, Psalm 6.7. For the word there signifies, not *anger*, but *grief*; as Eccl. 7.3.

*{be discouraged*} Heb. *be broken*. The same word that was used of a *reed, or cane*, verse 3. or, *bruised*. For it differs somewhat from *broken*, verse 3. and it is used in a notion of *oppression*, 1 Samuel 12.3,4. chapter 58.6. Hosea 5.11. Amos 4.1. whence some here expound it actively, *He shall not oppress.* But the word is used passively, in the former sense, Ecclesiastes 12.6. Others, *He shall not run*; referring it to another root, and expounding it, either of timidity and cowardice, that sets men on running, chapter 21.14,15. Jeremiah 48.9. or of temerity and turbulency, that makes men run on head, Job 5.13. Proverbs 19.2. and so the meaning should be; He shall do all things considerately and advisedly, not hastily, or rashly: See verse 2. But I concur rather with the first.

*{until*} This particle is here taken, not in way of determination, as if he should then begin to faint and fail, though not before; as Genesis 24.19,33. and 27.44. and 49.10. 1 Samuel 1.22. Psalm 132.5. chapter 36.17. but in way of continuation; that so long he should persist and hold out, without fainting or failing, there being no needful mention of not fainting, or failing, any longer, than till then; because from thence forward, all difficulties being now utterly removed, there could be no suspicion, or fear of aught in that kind. So Genesis 28.15. Psalm 71.18. Canticles 3.4. chapter 22.14. Matthew 1.25. and 13.33.

*{set judgment*} Settled things in due sort, according to God’s appointment.

*{in the earth*} Or, *on the earth*, here below: as Psalm 73.6. Matthew 6.10. and 18.18. Or, *in the land*, to wit, of God’s people; as distinguished from other nations, mentioned in the next clause. So chapter 4.2. and 14.2. and 16.1. and 19.24. But whether way we take it, I cannot assent unto that late learned annotator, who, by *judgment*, understanding *condemnation*, (as the like term is used, John 5.24,29.) would have the words to be rendered, *until he lay condemnation along on the ground*: as some, says he, are said *to lay justice on the ground*, Hosea 10.7. that is, until he has utterly abandoned and abolished it. But this sense seems too coact, nor to fit so well in this place.

*{and the Isles shall wait for his law*} The *Isles, or, Lands*: as verse 10. chapter 41.1. and 51.5. and *lands*, for, *people, or, nations*: as chapter 37.18. Not the Jews only, but the Gentiles also: the people of divers countries, shall willingly, and readily receive and embrace his doctrine and dictates. *Law*, for, *doctrine*: as chapter 1.10. See Genesis 49.10. Psalm 18.43,44. chapter 2.3,4. Acts 2.42. and 13.49. and 14.1.

**V. 5.** *{Thus saith God the Lord*} The former word signifies *might and power*: and so the Greek, sometime: as Exodus 20.5. and some of ours constantly express it, *the mighty God*: though that in a version need not, no more than for us, in English, to say ever, for *God, the good God*; albeit the term of *God* be deemed, not without good ground, to come from the word, *good*. Of the latter, see on ch. 1.2. verse 8. This large description of God is here inserted, as well to intimate his ability to go through with whatsoever he undertakes, as his fidelity in making good all his promises.

*{he that created the heavens*} Or, *heaven*: see ch. 1.1. Gen. 1.1. ch. 40.26. & 48.13. Zach. 12.1.

*{and stretched them out*} Or, *it*: as a curtain, or canopy, Psa. 104.2. ch. 40.22.

*{he that spread forth the earth*} Made it appear above the water wherein it lay, as buried and drowned before, Gen. 1.9. Psa. 136.6. ch. 40.22. & 44.24. 2 Pet. 3.3. The same word that is used of the sky that overspreads the earth, Gen. 1.6–8.

*{and that which cometh out of it*} Heb. *the offsprings, or, the proceeds of it*: as ch. 34.1. See Gen. 1.11.

*{he that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein*} Or, *thereon*, rather; as verse 4. breath, and spirit of life, Genesis 2.7. & 6.17. Proverbs 24.27. Job 33.4. Acts 17.25,28.

**V. 6.** *{I the Lord have called thee*} Christ my Son, and servant, Psa. 2.8. Heb. 5.4,5. See ver. 1.

*{in righteousness*} In a just and righteous course; or, in faithfulness, to fulfill my promise, ch. 1.27. & 46.13. Acts 13.23,32,33. See cha. 41.2. & 45.13.

*{and will hold thine hand*} To direct and assist you, Psa. 16.8. & 73.23,24. ch. 41.13. & 42.1. & 45.1.

*{and will keep thee*} From miscarrying, Psalm 17.8. and 91.11. ch. 49.2.

*{and give thee for a covenant of the people*} To be a Mediator and a ratifier of the covenant, plighted between me and my people the Jews, Gen. 17.4,17. & 22.18. Deut. 5.3. & 29.10–12. ch. 49.8. Rom. 15.8. 2 Cor. 1.20. Hebr. 7.22. & 11.24.

*{for a light of the Gentiles*} Or, *to the Gentiles*. To comfort and cheer them up, as light is cheerful and delightful, Eccl. 11.9. Psal. 27.1. Or to bring them out of spiritual darkness, into the light of grace and life, ch. 9.2. and 49.6. Luke 2.32. Acts 13.47. and 26.18,23. Col. 1.13. Or, to go before them, and conduct them in the way that tends and leads to life eternal, Luke 2.22. A metaphor taken from such as go before passengers, journeying in the dark, with a light: or to the pillar, that by night, conducted the children of Israel in the desert, Exod. 13.21,22. Num. 9.15. and 10.33. Psal. 105.39.

**V. 7.** *{To open the blind eyes*} To enlighten the minds of those that were, by nature, spiritually blind, with the sound knowledge of saving truth, ch. 35.5. Acts 26.18. 2 Cor. 4.4,6. Eph. 1.18. and 4.18,19. Rev. 3.18.

*{to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison-house*} The same thing, in divers terms repeated, to deliver them from the thraldom of sin and Satan, whereof their captivity in Babylon, was a type, ch. 45.13. and 49.9. and 61.1. Zach. 9.11. Luke 4.18. Rom. 6.6,14. Col. 1.13. 2 Tim. 2.26. Tit. 2.14. Heb. 2.14,15.

*{prisoners*} Heb. *prisoner*. But taken collectively: as Psa. 79.11. & 102.20. chap. 10.4. and 24.22. properly, *a bound one*, Psalm 68.6. Whence also the prison house is called *an house of band, or, bonds*, Jer. 37.15.

*{prison*} Heb. *closure*: or *house of closure: or, shutting up*: as Psalm 142.5. ch. 24.22. where the notation of the word is, *closure*: for an house, or place of enclosure, as *restraint*, for an house, or place of restraint, 2 Kings 25.29. Jer. 52.33.

*{sit in darkness*} Or, *in the dark*: as Psalm 88.6. Like prisoners in a dungeon, into which light has no access, chap. 9.2. Luke 1.79.

*{prison-house*} Heb. *house, or, place*, (for the word is in Hebrew, a very general term, Job 8.17. 2 Sam. 15.17. Psalm 84.3. Prov. 8.2. Ezek. 1.27.) *of restraint*: as 1 Kings 22.27. 2 Kings 17.4. Jer. 37.4. and 52.31. verse 22. It is used with an ellipsis either way, sometime, *house, or, place* alone, as some take it, chapter 14.17. sometime, *restraint* alone, for *house, or, place of restraint*; as above.

**V. 8.** *{I am the Lord, that is my name*} Or, *This*, to wit, *Jehovah*, Exod. 15.3. *is my name*, Psalm 83.18. the name, whereby I am, and will be discerned, and distinguished, as having my being of myself, from all idols, and false gods, that have their being from others, Exo. 3.14. Deut. 6.4. 1 Kings 19.21,22. And thereby I will also, in a more special manner, be known to my people, in making good all my gracious promises to them for their good, Exod. 6.3. For the Talmudists, and those that follow them, are here most ridiculous, who read the words, *Hu is my name*; and thence coin us a new name of God, which they use in some of their prayers: as they do also *Ap’hu*, from 2 Kings 2.14. Whereas the word signifies no more than *this, or, that*, here; *he also*, there.

*{and my glory will I not give to another, nor my praise to graven images*} I am jealous of my glory, and will not suffer it, therefore, to be imparted to any other, but will severely avenge myself on any that shall so do, Exod. 20.5. Deut. 4.15–19,23,24. Or, I will not suffer my glory to be impaired, as it would be, should I fail in the performance of any of my predictions, or promises; and so give idolaters occasion to advance their idols above me. See chapter 48.11.

*{to another*} To any other, simply. Or, to any other (that is, *strange*: as Mar. 16.17.) *another*, for, *another god: or, a strange god*: as Psalm 16.4. A defect of the substantive, (as ch. 43.12.) taken collectively in either.

*{graven images*} For images of all sorts. See on chapter 41.29.

**V. 9.** *{Behold the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare: before they spring forth I tell you of them*} As in times past I have been true in my promises, so will I be for time to come, Josh. 7.5. and 23.3,5. 1 Kings 8.23–25. Or, as my predictions to Ezekiah, concerning the Babylonian deportation so long before delivered, have already been effected. So now I foretell other things, concerning the downfall of Babylon, and the deliverance of my people, temporally, by Cyrus, spiritually, by Christ; long before any seeds, or signs of either, appear. That which before he challenged any of their false gods to do; and whereby he confirms his own divine power, and convinces them as counterfeits. See chap. 41.22–24,26,28,29.

*{spring forth*} Or, *bud out*, Gen. 2.5. And as there, when no sight of any such matter yet appeared, or means that might produce it.

*{tell you*} Heb. *make you hear*; as ch. 41.26.

**V. 10.** *{Sing unto the Lord a new song;*} *A new song.* That is, say some, an excellent one: or rather, *a new song, of a new matter, for a new mercy, upon a new occasion*. For it has reference to those new matters, mentioned, verse 9. See ch. 43.19. Jer. 31.22. Psalm 32.7. and 33.3. and 96.1. and 98.1.

*{and his praise from the end of the earth*} Or, *from the land’s end*: as Psalm 72.8. ch. 24.16. Either from all parts, where God’s people remained as exiles, as ch. 11.12. or where Babylon had exercised her rigor, ch. 14.5–7,16,17.

*{ye that go down to sea*} That are employed in shipping, as merchants, or, as mariners, Psalm 107.23. Let all praise God everywhere, both by sea and land, Psalm 96.11,12.

*{and all that is therein*} Heb. *the fullness thereof*: as Psalm 96.11. and 98.7. Yet not fishes, but men, that trade and traffic there. For that seems over-nice that some here have, that the islands themselves should be called the *filling of the sea*, as being set in the sea, like pearls, or precious stones, in the hollow of a ring, or other jewels: Because of such the word is sometime used, Exod. 25.7. and 28.17.

*{the Isles, and the inhabitants thereof*} Or, *lands*, as verse 4. or, *sea-coasts*, and those that border upon the sea: as Chapter 24.15.

**V. 11.** *{Let the wilderness, and the cities thereof, lift up their voice*} See the like defect, verse 2. See chapter 35.1.

*{the villages that Kedar doth inhabit*} The Arabians, or Ishmaelites that dwelt in scattered villages, or in tents, Gen. 25.13. Chap. 21.17.

*{let the inhabitants of the rock sing*} Or, *of Petra*, the chief city of Arabia: See Chapter 16.1.

*{let them shout from the top of the mountains*} That is, as some, those that are most savage, such as mountaineers commonly are, Jer. 3.2. but to be civilized under the kingdom of Christ, chapter 2.4. and 11.6–9. Others think it an allusion to those sentinels, or, watchtowers, situate on the tops of high hills, or other eminencies; from whence messengers used to call people together, to acquaint them with what good tidings they brought. chapter 40.9.

*{top*} Heb. *head*: as chapter 2.1.

**V. 12.** *{Let them give glory to the Lord, and declare his praise in the islands*} Or, *Lands, or Countries*: See verse 10.

**V. 13.** *{The Lord shall go forth*} To wit, to war against the enemies of his people: See chapter 37.36.

*{as a mighty man*} Or, *a mighty one*: so Job 16.14. Psalm 78.65.

*{he shall stir up jealousy*} Or, *his jealousy*; that is, his raging wrath, and fierce indignation, Prov. 6.34. so Deut. 19.20. chapter 59.17. fitly termed *jealousy*, because proceeding from a vehement and ardent affection, both of love to his people, and regard to his own honor, Deut. 4.19. chapter 37.32. Zach. 1.14. a defect of the pronoun; as chapter 40.12. he will set with much fury and fierceness upon them: See Psalm 78.38.

*{like a man of war*} Heb. *a man of wars*, as 1 Chronicles 28.3. a man much exercised in wars, that has fought many battles: See Exodus 15.3.

*{he shall cry*} Or, *shout*, Psalm 78.65. as military men use to do, in giving the onset, in joining battle in the field, or onslaught in the assault of a city: See Jer. 48.33. Amos 1.14.

*{yea, roar,*} Like a mighty fierce lion, that breaks in with violence upon the flock; and with his hideous roaring, affrights both sheep and shepherd, Amos 1.2. and 3.8. or, *make an hideous cry*; for the word that signifies *roaring* properly, is another, this is nowhere found, but here, and Zeph. 1.14. and imports a louder and more hideous cry, than the *shout* before-mentioned.

*{he shall prevail against his enemies*} Or, *behave himself mightily,* *or, play the valiant man*, Job 13.25. See Psalm 118.15,16.

**V. 14.** *{I have long time holden my peace, I have been still, and refrained myself*} Or, *I have restrained myself*, for there is no copulative in the text; so chap. 41.16. The words of God himself, (in regard whereof, some prefix the word, *saying*, as Psalm 105.15. Acts 7.32.) professing, that he had long forborne to execute judgment, and take vengeance in the behalf of his people, (as Psalm 50.21. and 83.1.) restraining his wrath, (ch. 48.9. & 62.1.) like a woman in travail, striving to hold in her breath; for the next branch seems to imply some allusion thereunto, see Jeremiah 44.22. the word is used of Joseph, Genesis 43.21. & 45.1.

*{long time*} Heb. *from an age*. So Genesis 6.4. Jeremiah 5.15.

*{now will I cry like a travailing woman*} Or, *cry out*; (the word is nowhere else found) as a woman in pain, that being not able to hold her breath any longer, cries out in her travail, and can have no ease, or rest, until she be delivered, Chap. 26.17. Rev. 12.2. Hence, some would have one of the Hebrew midwives, in Egypt, termed *Pua*, Exodus 1.15. which may not be altogether improbable, because they are conversant about women, in such cases; or rather, because with much *cry*, her mother had been delivered of her; as Jabez his mother, of him, with much *pain*, 1 Chr. 4.9. for they seem to mistranslate the word, who render it, *to hiss*, as some kind of serpent, whose name comes near it, Chapter 14.29. & 59.5. for that name is deemed to come from another root: nor does that seem to be the tone of women in travail. See Chapter 29.4. The meaning is, I will now hasten the execution of my wrath, with all speed, without further delay; as if I travailed, and were in pain, until it were executed. See Chapter 1.24. & 65.6. Luke 12.50.

*{I will destroy, and devour at once*} Heb. *smitten down*: as Job 5.5. or, *sup up*, as Jeremiah 2.24. and 14.6. An allusion to such ravenous wild beasts, as do so suddenly swallow down what they have slain, that they may seem to go quick down their throats, or to be slain, and swallowed at once, Psalm 124.3. yet because the former word signifies, properly, *to lay waste, or, make desolate*, some apply the former word, to the lands, or countries, the latter to the inhabitants. See Ezek. 36.3. where both words are joined together, as here.

**V. 15.** *{I will make waste mountains, and hills, and dry up all their herbs*} The herbage that the mountains afford to man and beast, Psalm 50.10,11. and 65.12. & 72.3,15. and 104.13,14. & 147.8. The meaning is, he will lay desolate the whole country of Chaldea, and of those that were adjacent and adjutant to it, Chapter 13.9. Accomplished by Cyrus, in his expedition against Babylon. He compares the vengeance that he intends to execute upon Babylon, to a devouring fire, that consumes all before it. See Deut. 32.22. Psalm 83.13. & 97.3. Joel 2.3. They seem to wring the text needlessly, who by *mountains, and hills*, here understand cities and towns; by the *herbage*, their inhabitants.

*{and I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools*} ch. 50.2. It was so done by Cyrus, in the siege of Babylon. See Jer. 50.38. & 51.32.

*{islands*} Or, *dry lands*, as Jer. 47.4. verse 10.

**V. 16.** *{And I will bring the blind by a way, that they knew not, I will lead them in paths that they have not known*} Meant partly, of the Jewish people, that had lived so long in grief and perplexity, that their very eyesight seemed to fail them, with long expectation, for their fore-promised deliverance; (as Psalm 6.7. & 31.9. & 38.10. & 119.81,82,123. Lam. 4.17. & 5.17.) and whom, after their deliverance, God would bring home into their own country, by such ways, as they had not gone, nor been acquainted with, before, chap. 43.19. & 49.9,11. Jer. 31.9. & 50.5. as he did before time, in their passage from Egypt to Canaan, Jer. 2.17. partly of those converts, either Jew, or Gentile, who being by nature blind, but enlightened by the Spirit of grace, Cha. 35.5. & 43.8. John 9.13,17. 2 Cor. 4.5,6. Ephe. 1.18. & 4.18. & 5.8. Hebr. 6.4. & 10.30. Rev. 3.17,18. should be entered into, and led on, in a new way, that tended to life and peace, Chap. 11.16. & 35.8. Luke 1.79. Heb. 10.10. such a way, as they had never walked in, nor had heard of, before, John 14.6. Rom. 15.20. a defect of the relative; as Psalm 81.5. Prov. 5.6. cha. 55.5. Jer. 5.15.

*{lead*} Or, *make to go*: so Psalm 25.5. & 107.7. Prov. 4.11. Chapter 48.17.

*{I will make darkness light before them*} Turn their adversity into prosperity, say some, and so the metaphor is oft used, Ester 8.16,17. Psalm 112.4. but because the speech is of a way the meaning is, rather, of making their passage clear, through obscure and dark places, as with light he went before his people, in their journey, through the wilderness, Exodus 13.21. for the spiritual sense, of directing the godly through the dark and blind ways of this world; see Psalm 89.15. chapter 11.4. John 8.12. & 12.35. Eph. 5.8. 1 John 1.5,6.

*{and crooked things straight*} Heb. *into straightness*; or, *turn uneven ways into a plain*. I will remove all the impediments that may impeach their free passage. So ch. 40.41. & 45.2.

*{These things will I do unto them*} Or, *for them*, Chapter 26.12.

*{and not forsake them*} But as well conduct them, and bring them safe home, as deliver them out of thraldom. See chap. 41.17.

**V. 17.** *{They shall be turned back, they shall be greatly ashamed, that trust in graven images, that say to molten images, Ye are our gods*} The idolatrous people shall be utterly confounded, when they shall see how unable their sorry gods are to save them; and see what the true God has done for his, Psalm 97.7. Chap. 1.27. & 41.11. & 45.15.

*{be turned back*} As men that are forced to flee, and turn their backs in fight, to their foes, Joshua 7.8. Psalm 44.10. or, that turn their faces back, from being seen, for shame, 40.14. & 129.5. or that shuffle, and traverse their ways, out of shame and repentance for what they have done, Jer. 2.18,36,37. or that turn back, with shame, the same way they came, when they fail of their expectation, Psalm 6.10. ch. 37.29,37.

*{greatly ashamed*} Heb. *be ashamed with shame*, Jer. 6.15. but here, by way of intention; there of diminution.

*{graven, and molten images*} See chapter 41.29.

*{Ye are our gods*} Exodus 32.4. chapter 44.15,17. Jer. 2.26,27. Hosea 14.3.

**V. 18.** *{Hear ye deaf, and look ye blind, that ye may see*} These words some suppose to be spoken to the Gentiles, blinded with sottish superstition, and erroneous conceits concerning their idols; and that notwithstanding what they had heard, and seen done by the true God, in the behalf of his people, in despite of their idols, chapter 40.21. & 44.18–20. Jer. 10.14. But most take them, as spoken to the Jews themselves, of whom many still continued such, notwithstanding all that from time to time they had heard and seen, concerning God, and the wondrous works wrought by him, Jer. 4.22. Eze. 12.2. Chapter 6.9.

**V. 19.** *{Who is blind, but my servant, or deaf, as my messenger, that I sent? who is blind, as he that is perfect? and blind, as the Lord’s servant?*} This some understand, as spoken in way of correction of, or diversion from what he had spoken before, verse 18. as if he should say, what do I blame and tax the Gentiles for their deafness and blindness, when as mine own people and their leaders, also, are herein as bad and defective as any. See the like, chapter 28.1–7. Mat. 15.14,16. But the most, by way of confirmation, as rendering a reason, why he gave his own people these titles because they deserved them as well, yea, rather, than any other. See verse 20. Rom. 11.25. 2 Corinthians 3.14.

*{my servant*} Israel, who should have more light, and better sight, than other people, having the light of my law among them, Psalm 19.7,8. & 119.105,130. Prov. 7.23. Psalm 147.19,20. Rom. 3.1,2. See verse 21.

*{my messenger*} Collectively taken for *messengers*: as Ch. 40.9. & 43.27. their prophets and teachers, that should be God’s messengers to hear from God, and declare to his people, what from him they have heard, Deut. 33.10. Mal. 2.7,8. 2 Cor. 5.20.

*{that I sent*} A defect of the relative; as verse 16.

*{he that is perfect*} The priests, and prophets, that should be unblameable, and of better abilities, than the common sort of men, that they might be lights and types to others, John 5.35. 1 Tim. 3.2. & 4.12. Titus 2.7. but were, many of them, blind and bad guides, Chap. 3.12. & 28.7. & 56.10,11. Matthew 15.14. & 23.16,17,19. or God’s people in general, whom by his gifts and favors, wherewith he had furnished them, he had made complete, Ezek. 16.14. and ought to have been perfect, as God their Father, whose children they professed themselves to be, is perfect, Gen. 17.1. Deut. 18.13. & 32.4,5. Matthew 5.48. John 10.41. Hence some suppose the Turks to be called *Mussalmans, as perfect ones*; though others, *as reconciled, or saved*. Howbeit, others render the word here, *he that has been recompensed, or rewarded*; or, *on whom many benefits have been bestowed*; (for the word sometime signifies simply, to deal well, or ill, with one, Psalm 7.4. Joel 2.25.) the Jewish people, on whom God had conferred so many blessings above any other people, Exodus 19.4,5. Deut. 4.7. Amos 3.2.

*{as the Lord’s servant*} In a special manner. See Chapter 41.8.

**V. 20.** *{Seeing many things, but observest not, opening the ears, but he heareth not*} Deuteronomy 9.3,4. chapter 6.9.

*{Seeing*} Or, *Seeing he seeth*. and so after, *opening, he openeth*; a defective, but emphatical form; as if he should say, *he seeth well enough, and setteth his ears wide open*. See verse 22.

*{many things*} So many wonderful works of God wrought for you, and among you, Deut. 4.3,4.

*{but*} Heb. *And*; as Chapter 29.13. and so in the next branch.

*{observest not*} Do not duly consider them, as a wise people would do, Psalm 106.7. & 107.43. Chapter 1.3. Some seem to understand it, of observation in practice: as Rom. 2.19–23. but the former seems more probable, as the peculiar office, for which the mind makes use of the eye: there is a defect of the pronoun: as Chapter 41.15.

*{opening the ears*} Listening, in show, at least, as if they did hearken, and desire to hear and attend, ch. 58.2. Jer. 42.2,5,6. Ezek. 14.1,3. & 33.30,31.

*{he heareth not*} No more regards, or observes, than as if he heard not at all, Ezek. 33.32. hears with the outward ear, but not with the inward: Of which, chap. 50.4,5. Matthew 13.9,14; there is a transition from person to person; as if God spoke in the first place to some of them, as by way of reproof; in the latter, to others of them, as in way of complaint. See chap. 29. Jer. 6.16. & 7.26.

**V. 21.** *{The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake, he will magnify his law, and make it honorable*} Or, *to magnify his law, and make it honorable*. The like syntax is, 1 Samuel 2.3. Prov. 23.35. Eccl. 10.1. Hosea 1.6. & 9.9. God’s pleasure is to magnify and honor his law, as well by execution of justice upon the transgressors of it, as by making good his promises unto those that observe it, Deut. 29.19,20. & 32.47. & 33.2. Or, as some other read it, *God was pleased for the making of him* (to wit, that people) *righteous, he gave him a great* (a large, or excellent) *law* (that is, many precious instructions and precepts) *to make him illustrious*, Deut. 4.7,8. Or, as others, again, *God delighted in him* (set his love and affection upon him, Psalm 149.4. ch. 62.4.) *for his righteousness’ sake*; (his fidelity, v. 6. in fulfilling his promises made to their fathers, Deut. 7.8.) *he magnified and dignified him with his law*, Psalm 147.19,20. cha. 43.4. Rom. 3.2. there is a defect of the pronoun, *it*, in the first of these: as Chapter 41.23. and *his*; as verse 13. and so also in the third, of *him*; in the second and third: as Hosea 6.3. in the third, also, of the preposition, *with*; as Psalm 17.13,14. The first and last, seem most probable, to me, especially, the last.

**V. 22.** *{But this is a people robbed and spoiled*} Or, *Yet*. Heb. *And*: as chap. 29.2. Yet after all these favors and honors conferred upon them, see what calamities and miseries are now befallen them, for their neglect of God, and their willful obstinacy against him and his precepts, v. 19,24. who has therefore exposed them to direption and thraldom, without relief or release hitherto: For he speaks, as to the Jewish people, yet remaining in thraldom, ch. 10.6. & 28.13. howbeit, some expound this of the Samaritans, or ten tribes, then in captivity, when this was spoken, without hope of release, or return. See 2 Kings 17.

*{spoiled*} Or, *trodden down*: chapter 17.14. See the last branch.

*{they are all of them snared in holes, and they are hidden in prison-houses*} They are taken, as beasts or birds, in snares and pitfalls, Psalm 35.7. and 124.7. Chapter 8.15,16. and 28.13. Lamentations 4.20. Ezekiah 17.20. & 19.4,8,9. and cast into dungeons, where they remain in strict custody, as close prisoners, Ps. 88.8. ch. 24.17. Lam. 3.2,6,7.

*{snared*} Or, *ensnaring, he hath ensnared, all of them*: as verse 20. ch. 59.13. Jer. 14. Eze. 114. so is the word taken, Pr. 29.8. that is, *they are all fast ensnared*: either by God: as verse 24. Lam. 3.6,7. Or, by the enemy: as 2 Kings 25.5,7. for the verb is here taken indefinitely: as Chap. 18.5. they are kept manacled and fettered, as birds, or beasts, ensnared, Psalm 107.10. howbeit, a learned late writer would have it rendered, *they sigh all of them*: from another root that so signifies, Jer. 4.31. but the former is more regular.

*{in holes*} Or, *dungeons under ground*; an allusion to such pits or holes in the ground, as either are made to catch beasts in, or that beasts themselves use to harbor in, 1 Sam. 4.11. Job 30.6. chap. 11.8. Ezek. 19.8. Nah. 2.12. Yet some read it, *in ensnaring the young men, or, choice ones, all of them*: supposing the word here used, to be the same with that, 1 Sam. 9.2. chap. 40.30. but the Jewish commenters, generally, make it two words, and render it, as our text does, and as the course of the context evidently leads: Only they acknowledge the alteration of one tittle, from the usual pointing of it; and understand it, some of them, of such holes and caves, as for succor and safety they had betaken themselves unto, to shroud and shelter themselves in: See Judges 6.2. 1 Sam. 13.6. ch. 19.21. where yet they should be surprised; but the former is more agreeable to what follows.

*{hidden*} Enclosed, or close shut up: as Joshua 10. verse 16,18.

*{in prison-houses*} Heb. *houses of restraints: or, of persons restrained*. See verse 7. *they are for a prey, and none delivereth: for a spoil, and none saith, Restore*] They are in a strait captivity, and none either by word or deed, endeavors to right or release them, Chapter 14.17.

*{a spoil*} Or, *a treading*: but the former, rather, here, for the word following: so Jer. 30.16.

*{saith, Restore*} As Gen. 20.7. 2 Kings 8.6.

**V. 23.** *{Who among you will give ear to this? who will hearken, and hear, for time to come?*} To amend and reform himself, and to grow wiser and warier, from time to time, by the present afflictions: considering from whom, and for what they come, Jer. 9.12. Mic. 6.9. Or, as some, by looking backward on judgments formerly inflicted, Joshua 22.17. Neh. 13.18. Zach. 1.5,6. Or, as others, again: how few are there, that hearing these judgments denounced, do, for the preventing, or averting of them, timely reform themselves, 2 Chr. 36.15,16. Jer. 5.12.

*{for time to come*} Heb. *for after*: Or, *for backward*: as chapter 1.4.

**V. 24.** *{Who gave Jacob for a spoil, and Israel to the robbers?*} *Jacob and Israel*, the same: as ch. 41.8. See verse 22.

*{did not the Lord, he against whom we have sinned?*} Or, *had sinned*: See Judges 2.11–14. and 3.12. & 4.1,2. 2 Chro. 36.16.

*{for they would not walk in his ways, neither were they obedient to his law*} Heb. *And*: which may well stand, as continuing the sentence: *and would not walk in his ways, nor obey his law*. Howbeit, the copulative is sometime used for the causative; *for, or because*: as chap. 64.5. or the discretive, *yet*; as verse 20,25. and so it is an aggravation of their sin, by their obstinacy and senselessness under it, ch. 57.1,17. Jer. 5.3.

*{be obedient*} Heb. *hear*; as 1 Samuel 15.22. Psalm 81.11.

**V. 25.** *{Therefore hath he poured upon him the fury of his anger, and the strength of battle*} Therefore, in the fervor and fierceness of his wrath, did he send in a powerful enemy upon him, that, with fire and sword, overran him and his country, and destroyed all on every side, 2 Kings 23.32. & 24. & 25.

*{Therefore*} Heb. *And*; as Chapter 37.20,27. & 38.20.

*{he poured out*} As Psalm 79.6. Jer. 10.25. an allusion to great storms, that pour down such spouts of rain, as those in the Levant Seas, and in Egypt, where a whole cloud, sometime, suddenly dissolving, does not drip, or descend in drops, (that is esteemed a prodigy with them,) but falls flat down, in a violent manner, with a continued stream: Or, unto the pouring of water out of some great vessel; not by small parcels, as in watering of grounds in a gentle manner; but violently, all at once, in an instant, Rev. 16.1. See 1 Samuel 7.6.

*{the fury of his anger*} Or, *his anger with fervor; or in heat; or,* (as others, keeping more strictly to the order of the terms in the text) *fervor in his anger*: a want of the preposition: as verse 21. ch. 41.2. Else the word entire is used in regiment, as sometime, for the contract. See Jer. 10.10. so our version takes it; and then it would be rendered *the heat of his anger*, word for word, *of his nose*. See ch. 13.9. & 51.17.

*{strength of battle*} Or, *war*, chapter 21.15. & 36.1.

*{and it hath set him on fire round about*} Set city and country, all on a light fire, chapter 9.18,19. Jer. 39.8. & 52.13.

*{yet he knew not*} Heb. *And* (as verse 20,22.) *he knew not, he took no notice of it*: as chapter 1.3. Jer. 3.13. Hos. 7.9. a defect of the pronoun *it*, as verse 21. and so in the last clause.

*{and it burnt him*} Or, *and though it burnt him*: a defect of the latter particle; chapter 30.20. Job 19.26. Prov. 29.19. Some refer the former to the country round about the city; this, to the city itself, Jeremiah 37.8.

*{Yet he laid it not to heart*} Heb. *upon heart*: as Job 22.22. their extreme stupidity, not sensible of, or effected with God’s judgments present upon them; nor repenting of their sins, though scorched with the fire of God’s wrath for them, Jer. 55.3. Amos 4.11. Revelations 9.18–21. & 16.8–11.

### CHAPTER 43

**Verse 1.** *{But now*} Or, *Yet now*. Heb. *And now*: as Chapter 42.22,25. Which entrance, shows, that this chapter has dependence upon the former; and, that therein the prophet continues on his discourse, begun in the former: as, also, the same thereby appears to be held on in the next. See chapter 44.1. It is, as if he had said, Though a great part of my people, yea, the main body of them continue still, notwithstanding my wrath thus poured forth upon them, thus obstinate and impenitent, chapter 42.25. yet will I have care of my chosen ones among them, whom I will protect, and in my due time, restore. Or, as some, though the other ten tribes continue in thraldom, and are like still so to do; yet have I more special care of you, my people. See chapter 42.22. But the former agrees better with the main course of the context.

*{Thus saith the Lord, that created thee, O Jacob: and he that formed thee, O Israel*} Who at first made you, and molded you into a national church and state, at the bringing you out of Egypt, Chapter 37.11. and 41.8–10. and 44.1,2. *Jacob and Israel*, one, and the same; as Chapter 41.8. yet, here, taken, not for the promiscuous multitude; as Chapter 42.24. but for the true Israel, the Israel of God, Psalm 125.4,5. John 1.47. Rom. 9.6. Gal. 6.16. the rather, termed by the name of Jacob and Israel: because the whole issue of Jacob were comprehended in the covenant, Deut. 33.5,28,29. Rev. 7.4. where Ismael and Esau, with their issue, lost their interest therein, Gen. 17.21. and 21.12. & 25.34. Galatians 4.30. Hebrews 12.17.

*{for I have redeemed thee*} Chapter 41.14. and 44.22.

*{I have called thee by thy name*} I have taken special notice of you, and have a special care of you: as Exodus 33.17. chapter 40.26. Psalm 147.4. Or, I have chosen you, and called you to be my people, and by that title, distinguished you from all other people, Exodus 19.5,6. Chapter 1.9. and 42.6. So Exodus 35.30. For that seems too slight, that some would have to be the meaning, that God gave Jacob the name of Israel, Genesis 32.28.

*{thou art mine*} Chapter 41.8,9. So Psalm 119.94. and this confirms the latter exposition, of the former words, *thou art mine*, both because I have made you, Psalm 100.3. and because I have bought you, 1 Cor. 6.20. and because I have culled you out, and called and taken you to myself, Deuteronomy 7.6. and 26.18. See verse 7.

**V. 2.** *{When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee: and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burnt, neither shall the flame kindle upon thee:*} I will secure and safeguard you, amidst all dangers and difficulties, meant, here, by *fire and water*, as Ps. 66.12.

*{the waters*} Or, *water*; as ch. 3.1. as when through the Red Sea, Exod. 14.22. for thereunto, he here alludes.

*{I will be with thee*} Some read it, *I was with thee*; as relating what he had formerly done, as ver. 3. but I suppose the former, rather here, intended: as chap. 41.10. *I will be with thee*, to preserve you from drowning, Psalm 78.53. & 106.10.

*{and through the rivers*} *And when thou passest through the rivers*: to be supplied from the former branch; as 2 Chronicles 10.11. *through rivers*, as through Jordan, sometime, Joshua 3.17.

*{walkest through the fire*} *Goest through, or, walkest in the fire*; as those three in the furnace; with whom, the angel was in the fire: which, though it burnt up those that cast them in, yet could not so much as singe their apparel, Dan. 3.21,22,25,27.

**V. 3.** *{For I am the Lord thy God, the holy one of Israel, thy Savior*} ch. 4.13,14. & 49.26. & 60.16.

*{I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia, and Seba, for thee*} Heb. *instead of thee*: as verse 4. to save you from destruction, which might otherwise have befallen you: as Prov. 11.8. & 21.18. This most understand of God’s turning Sennacheribs forces against Egypt and Ethiopia, upon the tidings brought him of Tirhaka’s coming against him, when he was making toward Jerusalem to besiege it, and so saving it from being sacked thereby, chapter 37.9. But I cannot conceive this to be the meaning of the place. For though it be true, that that rumor startled him, and made him think upon retiring, yet was it not that, but the fright that he took, upon the unexpected blow given in his camp, that enforced him to flight; not to invade Egypt or Ethiopia, which he was in sorry case then to do; but to get him home, with as much speed as he could, into his own country, chapter 31.8,9. & 37.36,37. Only one of the Jewish commenters expounds it, of the Egyptian firstborn, whom God destroyed, when he saved the firstborn of Israel, in lieu of whom, afterward, he took the Levites, Exodus 12.12,23,29. Num. 3.12,13. which though it come not full home to, yet gives an hint of that, which I conceive here intended; to wit, that God destroyed the Egyptians, for the saving and rescuing of his people, when he drowned them in the Red Sea, being upon eager pursuit of them, Exodus 14.30–38. & 15.9,10. and as for that of the *Ethiopians, or Cushites*, and the *Sabeans*, their brethren, Genesis 10.9. and living, in likelihood, not far asunder, it may well have reference to that remarkable defeat of that vast army, the greatest, upon record, in Scripture, given to the Cushites and their complices under King Asa, together with the spoil of the cities; among which is mentioned, the plundering of their tents, with their camels and cattle, the common commodities of the Arabians, among whom these Sabeans seem to have been situate, as well as the Cushites; chapter 45.14. Jeremiah 49.29. See 2 Chronicles 14.9,15.

**V. 4.** *{Since thou hast been precious in my sight, thou hast been honorable, and I have loved thee, therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life*} Or, *Because thou wast precious in my sight, wast honorable, and I loved thee: Therefore have I given men for thee, and people for thy sake.* So it may well be the same, in effect, that he had said, before, with an adjection of the reason, why he had so done.

*{Since*} Or, *Since that; or, For that; Or, because*: Heb. *From that*, for, *Because of*: as Num. 14.16. Psalm 12.5.

*{hast been precious in my sight*} As Psalm 116.15. but the word, here, is a verb; and so the next: So also, 1 Samuel 26.21. 2 Kings 1.13,14. Psalm 72.14. See further, chapter 60.9.

*{I have loved thee*} Or, *I loved thee*. Or, *do love thee*, Deut. 7.7,8. Jer. 31.3. Hos. 1.1. Mal. 1.2.

*{therefore*} Heb. *and*; as chapter 42.25.

*{will I give*} Or, *gave I*, as verse 3.

*{men*} Heb. *Adam*: of which name, see on chapter 2.9. here taken at large, for men indefinitely, or any man whatsoever: as chapter 2.22.

*{for thee*} Heb. *in thy room; or, in thy stead*: as verse 3.

*{nations*} Whole countries, or people: see verse 3. for the time past; and ver. 14. for time to come.

*{for thy life*} Or, *for thee; for thy person*: as Psalm 3.2. & 7.5. Hebre. *for thy soul*: So rather, as 1 Samuel 26.21. than, as some here, *at thy desire*: as Deuteronomy 23.25.

**V. 5.** *{Fear not, for I am with thee*} Verse 1,2. chapter 41.10,11. & 44.1,2. Jeremiah 30.10. & 46.27.

*{I will bring thy seed from the East, and gather thee from the West*} I will bring you home from all those places, where, in captivity, any of you do abide, Chapter 11.11,17. fulfilled, temporally, by Cyrus, Ezra 1.1. verse 14. Chapter 45.4. according to God’s promise, Deuteronomy 30.3,5. spiritually by Christ, chap. 66.19. Zacheriah 8.7.

*{thy seed——thee*} Both the same; you, the seed of Israel, Psalm 22.23. Jeremiah 23.8. Or, you, and your children, Jeremiah 30.10. & 46.27.

*{from the East*} Heb. *Sun rising*: as chapter 41.2.

*{West*} Heb. *Evening-coast*, chap. 45.6. from all parts of the world, chapter 11.12. for the other two follow, verse 6.

**V. 6.** *{I will say to the North, Give up; and to the South, keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth*} No remoteness of place shall hinder their return, Deuteronomy 30.5. chapter 11.12. Jeremiah 46.27.

*{sons and daughters*} All of either sex, Deuteronomy 32.19. 2 Cor. 6.18.

**V. 7.** *{Even every one that is called by my name*} See on verse 1. Chapter 63.19.

*{I have created him for my glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him*} To wit, this people, verse 21. See also, verse 1. Or, *whom I have created-and formed-and made*; the positive, for the relative, as ch. 33.20,21. & 42.1. & 46.4.

**V. 8.** *{Bring forth the blind people, that have eyes; and the deaf, that have ears*} Some conceive this, as spoken, by way of challenge to the Gentiles, who were as blind and deaf, for all their eyes and ears, as their idols, which they adored, Psalm 115.5,6,8. and see, if they can yet produce aught, in defense of their idols, verse 9. Others, as spoken by way of reproof, to those willfully obstinate among God’s own people: Of whom, chapter 42.16,20. as called upon, to see now, what they would not formerly believe: So Hab. 1.5. Acts 13.41. But some again, applying it to the former promise, verse 5,6. read the words in this manner, *I will bring forth the blind people, and, or with, them that have eyes; and the deaf with them, that have ears*: I will bring them out, of all sorts, as well sick, and defective, as sound, and entire, Jer. 31.9. or, as others, *I will bring forth the blind, and they shall have eyes; and the deaf, and they shall have ears*: Those, that were naturally blind, shall then be enlightened; and those that were naturally deaf, shall have their ears then opened, chapter 29.18. & 35.5. & 42.7,16. The word may be rendered, either, *Bring forth; or, Bringing forth*: for the infinitive, and the imperative, are here all one; and it may, therefore, by an usual Hebraism, be read, either, *Bringing, bring ye forth; or, Bringing, I will bring forth*: the like form, see Ec. 4.2. & 9.11. Jer. 14.5. But the first exposition seems clearest, and most agreeable to the course of the context.

**V. 9.** *{Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled*} See Chapter 41.1.

*{who among them can declare this, and show us former things?*} Heb. *first*, as verse 18,27. Which of their idols could foretell these, or the like things? See chapter 41.21,22. & 44.7.

*{Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified*} Let them produce witnesses, to testify that they have foretold things, as I am able to do, that so they may be proved to be gods indeed, and no counterfeits. See ch. 41.23,25.

*{bring*} Heb. *give, or give in*: as verse 6.

*{or let them hear, and say, It is truth*} Otherwise, let them acknowledge that, which they are hereby convinced of, to be true, to wit, that the Lord alone is the true God, and they all but base idols, ch. 41.29. & 42.8. or, let them hear such witnesses, as I am able to produce, and they will be convinced of the truth of what I say, and compelled to acknowledge it.

*{or*} Heb. *and*; as chapter 40.13,17.

*{It is truth*} See the like concise speech, Chapter 41.26. *truth*, that is most truth: as Psalm 119.142. John 17.17.

**V. 10.** *{Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord*} You my people, (for to them he now turns his speech, (who have had from time to time, so pregnant and plentiful proofs of my divine power and providence are able to give testimony sufficient for me. For I cannot accord with those, who expound it of the Gentiles, who by the preaching of the gospel, should give testimony unto God’s truth, which formerly they did not believe, ch. 52.14,15. 1 John 5.10. but adhere to the former; for that which follows, ch. 44.8. where the same thing is repeated.

*{and my servant whom I have chosen*} This is diversely expounded by interpreters, as well Jewish, as Christians. Some expound it of the Jewish people, with whom the Gentiles should attest, ch. 41.8. & 42.19. Others, of each of God’s servants, whom he should hereafter choose and call, John 3.33. 1 John 5.10. Others, of Esay the prophet, by whom God had foretold these things; so the Jewish commenters most of them, and some others. Others, of the prophets and other God’s ministers and messengers, taking the word collectively, John 1.7. Acts 1.8. and 5.32. 1 John 4.14. Others, of Cyrus, who by his edict, and act, also gave testimony thereunto, 2 Chroni. 36.21,22. Ezra 1.1–4. chapter 44.26,28. & 45.1. Others, lastly, of the Messiah the Lord Jesus; and so the Chaldee paraphrast, and most of ours, chap. 42.1. & 55.4. John 18.37. These two last are most probable; and the latter of these two, the principal.

*{that ye may know, and believe me, and understand that I am he*} These things, and many other, have been from time to time foretold you, yea, many of them, long before told you, you have seen already accomplished, and the residue shall, in their due time, be effected, by such instruments as I have designed thereunto, my Messiah especially, that you may be further confirmed in the faith and belief of that, which I now call you to attest.

*{know, and believe*} As John 6.69. 1 John 4.16.

*{that I am he*} The only true God, verse 11,12. ch. 41.4. John 17.3. or, as some, *that I am*, that I have an existence; which these idols have not, 1 Cor. 8.4. the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive; as chap. 9.15. verse 3. yet here I cleave to the former, for that which here follows.

*{before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me*} Chapter 44.8. & 45.22. none before him, because from eternity; before idol, or aught else was, Genesis 1.1. John 1.3. Col. 1.16,17. nor any after him, because he is unto eternity, and shall be, when all idols shall be abolished, Psalm 90.2. Jer. 10.15.

*{no God formed*} Or, *nothing formed of God*: he seems to give a privy nip to the heathens’ idols, as being of man’s making, and a time, therefore, when they were not, receiving their being from another: whereas the true God having his being in himself, and from no other, must of necessity be before all other. See ch. 44.10.

**V. 11.** *{I, even I, am the Lord*} Deuteronomy 6.4. Psalm 83.18. and 86.10. chapter 42.8. and 45.21. there is an emphasis in the redoubling of it, as verse 25.

*{and beside me there is no Savior*} None that is absolutely able to save, chapter 45.21. and 63.1. Hosea 13.4. James 4.12.

**V. 12.** *{I have declared, and have saved*} I have foretold the deliverance of my people, and have fulfilled what I foretold, chapter 37.35,36. and 46.10. Some of the Jewish writers restrain it to their deliverance out of Egypt. I promised it long before, and in due time, made it good, Genesis 15.13–16. Exodus 12.40,41. but of such restraint, there appears no necessity.

*{I have showed, when there was no strange God among you*} I made known to you, what I intended to do, what time I brought you, by mine own power, out of Egypt, & had no other God therein assisting me, nor you any other, either to foretell what was intended to you, and much less, that could effect it for you, Deut. 32.12. Jer. 2.2. or, as some read the words, by way of transposition, *I, and no strange, or, other, God, among you, did cause you to hear* (as chapter 41.22,23.) *these things*: a defect of the pronouns; as chapter 1.15. the one; and chapter 41.26. the other.

*{when there was no*} Heb. *and there was no: and, for, when*, as chapter 33.1. or, *and no*; for this particle is sometime a bare negative: as 1 Samuel 21.8. Jer. 38.5.

*{strange God*} A defect of the substantive: as chapter 42.8. Psalm 16.4. Some of the Jewish writers understand it, of God’s speaking to them, in Mount Sinai, rendering the words, *I made you to hear*, (my voice in the mount) *and there was no stranger among you*: there was none there, but you my people; Deut. 4.10,12,13,33,36. and 5.24,26. But the former seems more probable, and more agreeable to God’s present purpose. See Deuteronomy 32.12. Jer. 2.2.

*{therefore ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, that I am God*} You, to whom I made such things known before, and afterward fulfilled them, verse 10.

*{therefore*} Heb. *and*: as chapter 42.15.

*{that I am God*} Heb. *and I am God*: as chapter 22.20. & 37.16.

**V. 13.** *{Yea, before the day was, I am he*} Heb. *Since day*, (as Exodus 10.6. Jer. 36.2. since any day was,) *I am*; (as John 8.58.) the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive; (as Psalm 24.10. and 44.4. 2 Kings 7.7,10.) or, *I am the same*, as Psalm 102.27. chapter 46.4. The middle way I like best.

*{and there is none that can deliver out of my hand*} Heb. *no deliverer; or, none that delivereth*: So Job 10.7. and so of the *ram*, Daniel 8.4. but there the meaning is, no man, and for that time; for of the *goat* is the same afterward said, verse 7. that none could deliver the ram out of *his hand*, (that is, *his power*, as Psalm 22.20. and 49.15. but here it is, *none*, either God, or man: Which though Nebuchadnezzar presumed to say of himself, yet he shortly after found false, and was enforced to confess, that no god could deliver so, as the true God did, Daniel 3.15,17,29.

*{I will work, and who shall let it?*} *I will work*, as Ezek. 20.14,22. or, *I wrought*; the word is the same. Heb. *and who shall turn it back? or, reverse it?* or, *what I do, who can undo?* the indicative, for the potential, as in the former branch. See Job 9.12. chapter 14.24,27. Daniel 4.35.

**V. 14.** *{Thus saith the Lord your Redeemer*} That rescues, and delivers you out of your troubles, Genesis 48.17. chapter 41.14. and 44.24.

*{the holy One of Israel*} Verse 3. chapter 47.4. and 48.17.

*{For your sake I have sent to Babylon*} Or, *I will send to Babylon*: The Medes and Persians, under the conduct and command of Cyrus, chapter 13.3,17. and 14.1. and 21.9. and 44.28. and 45.1,4.

*{and have brought down*} Or, *will bring down*, by them.

*{all their nobles*} Heb. *bars*, Psalm 137.13. either bring down their great ones, and nobles, chapter 13.4. Jer. 51.35. or, break open, and cast down their forts, and strongholds, chapter 45.2. See Jer. 51.56. or, as some, *will bring them all down flying; or, all their flyers*; for so the word, also, sometime signifies: as chapter 15.5. enforced by flight to shift for themselves. See chapter 27.1. The pronoun is wanting in the text: as chapter 40.31.

*{and the Chaldeans, whose cry is in the ships*} Heb. *their outcry, or shout, is in the ships; or,* as some, *to the ships*: the positive, for the relative: as chapter 41.1. *the ships*, for, *their ships*; as, *their bars*, before.

*{whose cry*} The word is ambiguous; and signifies, sometime, *a shout of exultation and joy*, chapter 35.10. and 51.1. To which purpose, some read the words, *together with their ships, or shipping*, (for so the particle is used, Psalm 55.16. Hosea 5.6.) *which they vaunt of*. Sometime, it is put for any loud cry, in general, 1 Kings 22.36. and more specially, for an outcry in prayer, 1 Kings 8.24. Psalm 17.1. and 142.6. or other the like, proceeding from confusion, distress, or grief, Jer. 14.12. Lam. 2.19. and so most here take it, either *whose cry is to the ships*; (so is the particle used, chapter 10.22. and 8.8. and 30.29.) all whose cry is, *to the ships, to the ships*; as chapter 22.5. *to the hills, to the hills*: or, that cry out aboard their ships, and shallops, by which they seek to escape; the city being taken, when they find the water so shallow, being turned away, and so drained by Cyrus, that it is not deep enough to bear the vessels wherein they have embarked themselves. See Jer. 50.38. and 51.32.

**V. 15.** *{I am the Lord, your holy one*} As verse 11. or, *Even I the Lord*, as the note of continuation is there supplied: as if he had said, *It is even, I the Lord, I say, your holy One, &c.* that have done, or will do this; that sent, or will send, Cyrus, he went not of his own head, to Babylon, but on mine errand: though he had other ends of his own, yet I sent him, for your sake, verse 14. See the like, Genesis 45.5,7,8. and 50.20. chapter 10.6,7.

*{the Creator of Israel*} verse 7.

*{your King*} To save you, Psalm 44.4. and 74.12. and 149.2. chapter 33.22. for that is the office of a king, to protect his people, to save his subjects, 1 Samuel 10.19,27. Hosea 10.3. and 13.10,11. Mic. 4.9.

**V. 16.** *{Thus saith the Lord which maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters*} Or, *that made a way in the sea*, when he made the Red Sea passable for his people, Exodus 14.22,29. *and a path in the mighty waters*, when he made Jordan fordable for them, being then at the highest, Joshua 3.7,10. Zach. 11.3. as if there had been a beaten path through either of them, as on some plain, chapter 63.11,13,14. See Psalm 77.19,20. chapter 44.27. Thus interpreters generally, implying, that no difficulty in the way, should hinder the passage of his people, in their return from Babylon to their own country, no more than aught did, or could, in their journey thither, at first. Howbeit, I suppose that the *sea, and mighty waters*, are here, one and the same: as Exodus 15.1,10. and the rather, for that which follows, verse 17. which no way agrees to Jordan, wherein none were destroyed.

**V. 17.** *{Which bringeth forth the chariot, and horse; the army, and the power; they shall lie together, they shall not rise; they are extinct, they are quenched, as tow*} Or, *who brought forth the chariot, and horse; the army, and the power*; (who drew out all Pharao’s horse, and forces, out of his own country into the wilderness; the like whereunto, see Judg. 4.7. and from off the land into the sea, Exod. 14.4–9,23.) *that they might lie together*, (in the bottom of the sea, Exod. 14.27,28. and 15.1,14. like a lump of lead, Exodus 15.10.) *and not rise*; (Exod. 14.13,28. Psalm 106.11.) *that they might be extinct, even quenched, as a wick*. Heb. *as flax*; Exod. 9.31. Hosea 2.4. so rather than *tow*; for there is another word for that, Judg. 16.9. ch. 1.31. *as flax*, for, *as a candle-wick made of flax*, ch. 42.3. when water is cast on it, or it is cast into the water. In which term, some suppose an allusion to that commodity of flax, which Egypt was famous for, ch. 19.9. and 23.3. Thus the text flows smoothly, that sounded harshly, and ran abruptly before. The defect of the final, or finitive particle, is not unusual. See Psalm 93.1. ch. 40.27. and 41.7. And the defect of the copulatives no less, which oftentimes make the sentence the quicker, and more emphatical: See Exodus 15.9. Judges 5.17. cha. 33.22. and 37.27. and 40.24. Some of the Jewish commenters, expound this of Sennacherib, and his forces, whom God drew out of Assyria to their destruction, chap. 7.18. and 37.36. Others, of the Babylonians and Chaldeans, whom God would draw out into the field to fight with the Persians, to their own ruin. As also some, of God’s drawing out the Medes and Persians, to destroy the Chaldeans, chapter 13.17. But these regard not the connection of this verse with the former. That of the Egyptian is here related, to show, how able God is, both to deliver his people, be they never so distressed; and to destroy their adversaries, be they never so powerful, by ways, and courses, unexpected.

**V. 18.** *{Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old*} Not that God’s former mercies should not be remembered, or regarded, for those they are everywhere called upon to keep in mind, and think upon, Exodus 12.42. and 13.3. Deuteronomy 4.9,10. and 9.7. and 16.3. and 32.7. Psalm 78.6,7. and 105.5. and reproved for forgetting, and not regarding them, Psalm 78.11,42. & 106.7,21. But the meaning is, that those things, which he now foretells, and intends to do, partly, in their temporal deliverance by Cyrus, but principally, in their spiritual deliverance by Christ, should be so great, and so remarkable, that they might be sufficient, of themselves, to assert his divine power, though all the former were clean forgotten; or, as the most, that in regard of them, the former, though great and wonderful, should, in a manner, neither be minded so much, nor regarded. See Jer. 16.14,15. and 23.7,8.

*{former*} Heb. *first*, verse 9,27. So Rev. 2.5.

**V. 19.** *{Behold, I will do a new thing*} Heb. *Behold, I am doing a new thing.* This some expound, of the renewing, or making all things new, 2 Cor. 5.17. Rev. 21.5. but neither the text itself, nor the intendment thereof, will admit it; they also seem to strain the word, needlessly, too far, who by *new*, would have meant *excellent*. It is apparent, that the meaning is, that he will do some new thing, beside, and divers from what he had formerly done, some such thing as he had not done before, as Jer. 31.22. Num. 16.30. So, *sing a new song*, a song newly composed, not made, nor sung before, for a new benefit, a new deliverance, chapter 42.10.

*{now it shall spring forth*} Or, *it is even now springing forth*; it is even working already: as 2 Thess. 2.7. it is a metaphor, from plants, that bud and blossom before they bear fruit; and the former gives warning of the approach of the latter, Num. 17.8. so Psalm 8.11. Zach. 6.12. See chap. 13.22.

*{shall ye not know it?*} Or, *do ye not perceive it?* This he seems to say, as speaking to those that remained in captivity at Babylon, about the time of Cyrus his preparation for that expedition, or when he was now upon his way thither: For his preparations were great; and took up some time, chap. 13.2,4. as also, his way long, and passage difficult, that took him up a year or two, at least: See chap. 13.5. Jer. 51.46.

*{I will even make a way in the wilderness*} *A way*, that is, a plain, or a free *way in the wilderness*; where the ways are wont to be uneven with hills and dales, and obstructed with thickets, and overgrown with brambles and briars: I will make a convenient and easy passage for my people returning, by waste places from Babylon, to their own country, free from all such lets and impediments, as might hinder or impeach their passage: See chapter 40.3,4. & 49.11.

*{and rivers in a desert*} I will furnish them with a plentiful supply of all necessaries, that they may not faint by the way, chap. 41.17,18,19. and 49.9,10. Jer. 31.9. He alludes to the water, that he gave before time, from the rock, in the wilderness, Exodus 17.6. Num. 20.8–11. Psalm 105.41.

*{desert*} Heb. *waste*: for so the word properly signifies, Psalm 106.14. & 107.4. So verse 20.

**V. 20.** *{The beasts of the field shall honor me: the dragons, and the owls; because I give waters in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen*} The very brute beasts, and wild creatures, shall fare the better for the passage of my people through the wastes they abide in, being cheered with the refreshments that they shall receive from the water wherewith I supply my people; as the water that God, in former times, gave, in like case, to his people, was a refreshment to their cattle as well as to themselves, Num. 20.8. and the wild beasts, also, had benefit thereby, as well as by the Egyptian carcasses that they fed upon, Psalm 74.14.

*{beast*} For *beasts*; taken collectively; as Psalm 50.10. 2 Samuel 21.10. they seem wide, that understand by *wild beasts*, here, savage people.

*{honor me*} In their kind: who as they are said to *cry to God*, when they lament for want of food, Psalm 104.21. and 147.9. so are they said to *praise him*. Psalm 145.9,10. and 148.7,10. when they are cheerfully affected upon such refreshments, afforded to them; as implying what they would do, had they that reason and understanding, that man has, to conceive from whom such things come.

*{dragons*} See chapter 27.1.

*{Owls*} Or, *Ostriches*: as some: see Lam. 4.3. Heb. *the owl's daughters*, as chapter 34.13.

*{to give drink to my people*} Heb. *to make my people drink*: as Jer. 25.17.

*{my chosen*} See verse 10, chapter 41.8. and 44.1.

**V. 21.** *{This people I have formed for myself; they shall show forth my praise*} Or, *The people that I formed for myself shall recount*, or *should recount* (as chapter 26.9.) *my praise*: the positive, or demonstrative, for the relative: as Psalm 74.2. and 104.8. and 142.4. This some understand, as to be done of the people refined, and reformed by their afflictions, chapter 48.10. and returned from captivity, Psalm 102.18. Others, of the duty that was required of God's people, whom, for that end, he had formed, verse 7. but they had exceedingly failed in; and this agrees well, both with the sequel, wherein God complains of their default, and failings herein, verse 22–24. and with God's intendment, in this place, to set forth the freeness of his mercy, in this their delivery, verse 25. and it is, as if he had said, having an eye back to the former words, verse 20. the very brute beasts shall, in their kind, and as well as they can, do that which many of you, whom I formed for that purpose, do not.

**V. 22.** *{But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob:*} Or, *Yet*: Heb. *And*; as verse 1. chapter 44.1. You have not been so careful to serve and worship me, as you should and ought to have been, being for that end and purpose formed into a church and state, by me, that you might serve and worship me; the invocation of God's name, being put for his whole service and worship, as Psalm 79.6. Jer. 10.25. though some understand it of not seeking to God, in their troubles and distresses, 2 Chronicles 28.22. chapter 9.13. & 22.8–13. & 64.7. Daniel 9.13. Hosea 5.13. and 7.7,14. Amos 4.6–11. But the former seems the genuine sense of the place.

*{but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel*} You have been weary of me and my service; you have counted it, not a benefit, but a burden to you, Psalm 81.11. Mal. 1.13. But some read the words, *thou hast wearied me*; as, say they, the word is taken, Eccles. 10.15. Mal. 2.17. and that is said, indeed, verse 24. but the verb is here, in another form, than there; or than in either of the places produced. Others read them, *when thou wast afflicted by me*. Of which before. Others, *when thou tookest pains with me*; as if the meaning were, that when they did take much pains in outward observances, they did not serve God, but an idol of their own framing, a God that would accept of such formal courting, and compliments; though neither proceeding from inward devotion, nor accompanied with a religious course of life: that which seems aimed at, Prov. 21.27. Jer. 7.9,10. Hosea 7.14. Zach. 7.5,6. and the particle, indeed, signifies, as well *when*, as *but*: and so ch. 36.10. Joel 2.12.
