Howbeit, a learned late critic, controls this generally received version; and would have it rendered, either by way of assertion, *I am; and I only* (as Deut. 15.4. Num. 22.35. 2 Sam. 12.14.) *hereafter*: or, by by way of interrogation, *I am, and is there any more besides me?* And this his rejection of the received reddition to strengthen, he observes, that another form of speech is used in the like, concerning God, chap. 45.6. But that very place, if the manner of the Hebrew language be well observed, will help to justify the received version here: for it is a thing very usual in Hebrew, to swallow up the preposition intervenient between the verb or the noun, and the pronoun affixed to either, which yet must of necessity be restored, or supplied, to make the sense entire: hereof, see instances, not a few, on Chap. 28.15. & 48.10. & 49.24. & 65.5. the particle *besides* then, expressed there, being (as of necessity, it must, to make the sense entire,) supplied here; the version there *is none, I*, that is, *but I*, or *beside me*, will be warrantable; because suitable to that parallel place, and agreeable to many other the like constructions.

*{I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children*} You thought it impossible, ever to be deprived of your king and Kingdom, whereunto you seem to be wedded, as to an husband, by an indissoluble band; or, of your people, that are as your children, or, as some, your posterity, your issue, that should succeed constantly, in your Kingdom. See Rev. 18.7.

*{sit as a widow*} Heb. *sit a widow*: as Gen. 38.11. or, *sit as a widow*, the note of similitude supplied: as Lam. 1.1. which here wants, as verse 3. I shall not sit desolate, as widows use to do.

*{know*} Experimentally: *sustain*, or *suffer*; as Gen. 2.9. Eccl. 8.6. 2 Cor. 5.21.

**V. 9.** *{But these two things shall come unto thee, in a moment, in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood*} It shall befall you clean contrary to your expectation, or presumption rather, in both, and in both at once; yea, both shall betide you, suddenly, and in as much extremity as may be, the loss both of sovereignty, and of subjects together; or, of posterity, to sway the scepter of your state successively, the line of Nebuchadnezzar being with Baltasar cut off, Dan. 5.30,31. See the like ch. 51.19.

*{But*} Or, *Yet*. Heb. *And*. So Chap. 40.31. and 42.20,25.

*{in a moment*} Or, *suddenly*. When it is least thought on, or looked for, Job 21.13. and 34.20. Psalm 73.19. See ver. 11.

*{in one day*} At one time together: not so precisely: as 1 Sam. 2.34. but as Rev. 18.8.

*{they shall come upon thee, in their perfection*} They shall come full, or fully upon you. Heb. *according to their entireness*, or, *perfection*, your calamities, in either kind, shall be exceeding great. See the next clause.

*{for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments*} *For*, or *with, thy manifold witchcrafts, for thy mighty enchantments*, shall they come upon you *exceedingly*; for the last word is an adverb, and signifies, *very much, very greatly, abundantly exceedingly* and is used commonly, to express the superlative degree, which the Hebrews want, Gen. 1.31. Exod. 1.7. Psal. 119.4. and there is a pause at the word next before it, which shows, that it has reference to somewhat else before that, and to no noun substantive, which it will not fitly accord with, but some verb, which out of the former branch, therefore is to be supplied; as Gen. 1.16,30. 2 Chr. 10.11. Prov. 15.15. ch. 43.2. And so our ancient versions had it, *they shall mightily fall upon thee*.

*{for*} As the particle is used, Gen. 18.28. Jer. 18.18. and then are her sorceries, or witchcrafts, and enchantments, here mentioned, as one procuring cause, also, of her downfall; or, *with*, that is, together with; as 1 Sam. 1.24. Jer. 11.19. Hos. 5.6. and then the meaning is, that all her magical sleights, and cunning fetches, should stand her in no stead, but should all fail, and fall together, with her, and her state v. 12,14,15.

*{sorceries*} Or, *witchcrafts*; (for thence the word for *a witch*, Exod. 22.17.) whereby is understood, as well her politic devices, wherewith she circumvented, and deluded, and so either won to her, or kept with her, great Princes and potent people: as if they had been bewitched, and enchanted by her: but her magical arts, and practices also, wherein that state abounded v. 12,13. therein treading, and tracking the steps of Nineveh, by whose ruin she rose, called, *a Mistress of witchcrafts*, Nah. 3.4. as also the spiritual Babylon that succeeded the secular, did herein also, not come short of either. See Rev. 17.2,3. & 18.23.

*{the great abundance of thine enchantments*} Heb. *the might*, or *power, of thine enchantments*; for so the word signifies, and is so rendered, ch. 40.29. Nah. 9.3. derived from a word, that signifies *a bone*, and is used, also, for strength; because the bones are the strength of the body, Job 21.23. It is true, that the verb is used, as well for *to abound* or *to be many*; as *to be strong* or *mighty*, Psalm 40.5,12. chap. 31.1. and the adjective from it, descending likewise, Chap. 60.22. but the substantive here used for *might*, rather than for *multitude*, as in the places pointed to, where alone it is found; so that not only the variety and numerosity of her sleights and policies, but the powerfulness and prevalency of them, is here also intimated: neither whereof, yet, should be able to secure her against God: For there is no power, or policy: no might, or sleight of any, that can prevail against him, Proverbs 21.30. Chapter 28.15,17,18.

**V. 10.** *{For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness*} Or, *Because* (Heb. *And*, as Chapter 64.5.) *thou hast trusted*, In your wicked courses, your wiles and sleights before mentioned: or, your means and might thereby acquired, Psalm 52.7. Chapter 28.15.

*{thou hast said, None seeth me*} You have deemed yourself even out of God's eyesight, and your designs and projects so cunningly contrived, so closely and covertly carried, that they could not possibly be descried, or discovered by any, Psal. 64.5. & 94.3. Chapter 29.15.

*{Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee*} Or, *hath made thee to turn away*; or, *hath turned thee aside*, Chap. 57.19. You did imagine, but vainly, as by experience it will appear, that your sleight and skill would secure you: and your trusting thereunto; made you transgress the more freely: that which Solomon, therefore, forewarns his son, to beware of, Proverbs 3.5. such *wisdom and knowledge, falsely so termed*, 1 Timothy 6.20. *puffeth up*, 1 Cor. 8.1.

*{and thou hast said in thy heart, I am, and none else besides me*} See v. 8.

**V. 11.** *{Therefore shall evil come upon thee, and thou shalt not know from whence it ariseth*} Heb. *thou shalt not know the morning thereof*: or *the rising of it*; that is, *the morning*, or *rising, whereof thou shalt not know*: as ver. 4. *morning*, for *rising*: as evening, for, sunsetting; opposed to sunrising, Chap. 45.6. You shall not know, either from what region it shall arise; or, on what day it shall come: alluding to the rising of the sun, whose approach produces morning; and withal, giving a privy nip to the practice and profession of their wizards, by that state so much relied upon, who by the course of the stars, and the rising and setting of them, undertook to presage, and foretell, what would every day fall out; and by whose help, they made account that they might easily foresee, and prevent, consequently, any evil, that was on foot, or intended against them, ver. 12,13. It may have reference also to Cyrus his sudden surprisal of them, ere they were aware of him. The Babylonians little dreamed, when they arose at Court, from their upsitting at their revels, that their city was surprised; and the tidings of the unexpected surprisal of it, was even then posting apace to them. See Jeremiah 51.31.

*{and mischief shall befall thee, and thou shalt not be able to put it off*} Or, *which thou shalt not be able to avoid*, or *to avert*: as chap. 37.27. Heb. *to expiate*, cha. 28.18. a metaphor from such expiations, as being duly performed, did free the party so expiated from penalty, Num. 16.46–48. you shall neither be able to foresee it, nor to free yourself from it, Jer. 50.24.

*{and desolation shall come upon thee suddenly, which thou shalt not know*} Or, *which thou dost not know*: as Prov. 27.1. a defect of the relative, as ch. 44.2. or, *when thou shalt not know it*, what time you think not of it: as Mat. 24.39,50. the adverb of time supplied: as ch. 17.6. & 26.10. & 41.17.

**V. 12.** *{Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries*} Or, *witchcrafts*, or *witcheries*: as ver. 9. In way of derision he calls upon them, to muster up all their devilish arts & devices, to try what in their distress, they are able to do for their indemnity, and deliverance by them. Some both here, and v. 9. would have read instead of *enchantments*, and *witcheries*, *enchanters*, and *witches*: but these terms in Scripture are no where so used; two other words of the same stock with these, are used for either, Psalm 58.5. Jer. 27.9. Howbeit, there may in this place, be an ellipsis, or want of the subject; as in divers places, the like is found: *enchantments*, for, men, or masters, of *enchantments*: and *witcheries*, for men, or women, masters, or mistresses, of *witcheries*, that is, professors, or practicers, of such hellish arts, *enchanters*, or *charmers, wizards*, or *witches*: as Nineveh is called, *a mistress of witcheries*, that is, a great practitioner in such kind of abominations, Nah. 3.4. so is the *harvest*, put for the *harvestman*, ch. 17.5. See more there: if we take it for the arts, or practices themselves, the text would be rendered, *stand up now with them*: as armed, and furnished with them: as 2 Kings 11.11. See ver. 13. if for the professors, and practicers of them, it would be rendered, *stand now among them*; as consulting with them, or seeking aid and advice from them, ver. 13.

*{wherein thou hast labored from thy youth*} Or, *with whom*, as ver. 15. having reference, either to the practices themselves, or to the practicers of them. These kinds of arts, the Chaldeans were anciently so much addicted unto, that the professors of them, were, among other nations, known, and called commonly, by the name of Chaldeans. See Diodore l. 3. c. 8. and Tully *of divination*, l. 2. and their magicians were highly esteemed with them, and great men in the state. See Dan. 2.2. & 4.6,7. & 5.7,8.

*{from thy youth*} From your first beginning to rise, and grow up into a state. See the like, Jer. 22.21.

*{if so be thou shalt be able to profit, if so be thou mayst prevail.*} Try whether the one, or the other, be able to do you any good, or to stand you in any stead; to avail you in aught, or to prevail aught for you; against the evil that is coming upon you. So ch. 30.5,6. & 45.20. Lam. 4.17. See the like ironies, Jer. 22.20. & 46.11. v. 15.

**V. 13.** *{Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels*} You do but tire out yourself in vain, in studying how to save yourself, one while by one course, another while by another. So ch. 16.12. Jer. 2.36,37. & 4.14.

*{let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators stand up, and save thee, from those things that shall come upon thee*} Call for all your wizards to stand up for you, and to improve their skill, and power, to the utmost, in your behalf. So chap. 41.1. & 43.9. Baltasar called for them all; but none of them all knew what to advise him, or how to save him, Dan. 5.7,8.

*{astrologers*} Heb. *viewers of the heavens*: not such, as view so as David did, Ps. 8.3. and as God's people and others, are willed to do, ch. 40.26. to consider, and contemplate the incomparable glory, wisdom, power, and providence of God, discovered, and brightly shining forth in them, Psal. 8.1. & 19.1–4. & 104.1–4. Rom. 1.21. but that gaze on them, to read the fates, and fortunes (as they term them) of men, and states, persons, and people in them; and to foretell thence, what good, or evil, shall betide them: building upon such fond, groundless, superstitious, and ridiculous principles, as by the Devil's suggestion, (such are the good angels that these seducers and deluders of people tell us of, if they have them from any that pretend so to be,) or from the flashy fancies of their own addle brains, that they have framed and forged to themselves, Jer. 10.1. and the Hebrew doctors, therefore, affirm the term here used, to come from an Arabic word, that signifies *to decide*, and to denote such, as take upon them, *to decide*, and determine things of future contingency, by the view of the sky. Howbeit, some take upon them, here, to alter the text; and, because this word is in Scripture no where else found, to read instead of it, the word used elsewhere, for *an enchanter*, or *charmer*, Deut. 18.11. Psal. 58.5. of the same stock with that, ver. 9,12. but taken in another sense; so as it is no where, save in a feminine form, found used in Scripture, as it signifies *a consociater*, or *conjoiner*; expounding the words, by an inversion of terms; *such as consociate, or conjoin the stars*, (that observe the conjunctions of them, for the drawing of dooms and predictions from them) *by contemplating of the heavens*: such an inversion of terms, some also would have, Ps. 35.7. But these seem to be somewhat overbold with the text.

*{stargazers*} Heb. *those that gaze upon the stars*. Another term given to the same persons, to those of the same profession, among whom there were those as Tully reports, that vaunted of skill, gathered from the observation of the courses and conjunctions of the stars, for above, or about, as some, forty, yea, as some, seventy thousand of years; so many thousands, before there were either stars to be observed, or men to observe them, the world having not, as yet, seen near six thousand years.

*{monthly prognosticators*} Heb. *that give notice, instruct*, or *make to know things concerning the months*; the word properly signifies *the new moon*, Psa. 81.3. Ezek. 46.3. but is used commonly for *the month*; because the *new moon*, among the Jews, began the *month*. Those that take upon them, to tell beforehand, the occurrents of each month, as our prognosticators also do.

*{stand up, and save thee*} Heb. *stand up, and save thee*; for the copulative is in the text: or *stand up to save thee*: as that particle is also oft used, Josh. 24.9. cha. 19.12. & 53.2.

**V. 14.** *{Behold they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them*} They shall be as stubble to the fire, in the day of God's wrath, Chapter 1.31. and 5.24. Exodus 15.7. Nah. 1.10. Zeph. 2.2. and it may be, also, made fuel, matter for ordinary fire, as the Philistines' idols, 2 Samuel 5.21. and the Jewish false prophets, Jeremi. 29.22.

*{they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame*} Heb. *their souls* (as ch. 44.20. Ezek. 14.14. *from the hand* (as Ps. 22.20. & 49.15.) *of the flame*, that is, *of the fire*: as Luk. 16.24. they shall not be able to save themselves; much less to save others, v. 13,15. ch. 46.2. Ps. 146.3,4.

*{there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it*} They shall utterly perish, and nothing of them remain, that may yield the least help, or hope, that may afford the least comfort: a metaphor taken from wood, or fuel, so burnt and consumed to ashes, that not so much as any coal, cinder, or ember, is left, that may be of any use, afford any heat, or help, to kindle a new fire again. See the like in another notion, Ch. 30.14. or, as some render it, *shall not be a coal to warm* with, or *fire to sit before it*, that is, say they, the fire which the Medes and Persians shall kindle at Babylon, among the Chaldeans, shall not be such a fire, as men are wont to sit by for warmth in winter, Jer. 36.21. but such a wasting and consuming fire, as shall destroy and devour all before it, Ps. 50.3. & 97.3. cha. 9.18. & 10.16. & 24.6. & 26.11. Jer. 51.25,31. But the former sense seems the sounder, both for what went before, and for what follows after. v. 15. However, the negative is to be supplied from the former branch; or the disjunctive instead of it to be inserted; as Ps. 9.18. See on ch. 28.28.

**V. 15.** *{Thus shall they be unto thee, with whom thou hast labored, even thy merchants from thy youth*} Or, *Thus shall thy merchants be unto thee*, (that is, in like manner shall it be with you, as in regard of your wizards, so in regard of your merchants) *with whom thou hast tired thyself* (as Jer. 51.58.) *from thy youth*. For there seems to be a trajection in the words of the text. The like, whereunto, is found Rev. 13.8. compared with ch. 17.8. there; as this, with ver. 12. here: either of these readings does well fit those, who, by *merchants*, here understand her *wizards*. Howbeit, if we regard the distinctions in the Hebrew, the text would thus be read; *Thus shall it be with thee, in regard of those, with whom thou hast tired out thyself*: (for there is the middle distinction) that is of your wizards: and then follows; *thy merchants*, or *thy traders, those that have traded with thee* (as *thy campers*, for those that camp against you, Psal. 55.5.) *from thy youth shall wander every one to his quarters*: and this I take to be the genuine reading of the place.

*{thy merchants*} All that had any trading with her, from foreign parts, which were not a few, (as with Nineveh before, Nah. 3.16.) partly, in regard that she was now become the head city of the Empire; and partly, also, in regard of her convenient situation for trade, by reason of the great rivers, upon which, and near unto which, she was seated. See the like of the mystical Babylon Rev. 18.11.

*{from thy youth*} Since you began to rise to a more absolute empire, by the declination of the Assyrian Monarchy, the trade of Nineveh, that fell with it, being then transferred, and devolved unto you. See v. 12.

*{they shall wander every one to his own quarter:*} Heb. *passage*. They shall flee away as fast as they can, each one to his own home, to his own country, when they see how it goes, or is like to go with you. Or, they shall flee each one any way, that they can find free passage by, for his own safety, unto any place, where they suppose they may be secured, and leave you alone, to shift, as you can, for yourself. See the like of her soldiery, Jer. 51.9.

*{none shall save thee*} Neither your merchants; for they shall forsake you: nor your wizards; for they shall perish together with you; verse 14.

### CHAPTER 48

**V. 1.** *{Hear ye this*} This chapter is, also, much of the same both subject and frame, with divers of the former, especially the 43. and 44. For in it, the Lord reproves the disobedience, rebelliousness, and obstinacy of his own people; lays before them, his power, and his providence, whereof by many evidences, they might be convinced; shows, by what means they might have prevented many mischiefs that had befallen them; and yet promises, having refined them by such afflictions as they had undergone, by Cyrus freely to set them free, and restore them again.

*{Hear ye this, O house of Jacob*} Ch. 44.1. & 46.3.

*{which are called by the name of Israel*} Which profess yourselves to be Israelites, and bear that name, but do not answer your name, are not so in truth, Rom. 2.17. & 9.6. They vaunted themselves of Israel, as of Abraham, Mat. 3.9. John 8.33. whereas, indeed, they neither resembled, nor imitated, either Israel, or Abraham, Mat. 3.7. John 8.37,39,40.

*{and are come forth out of the waters of Judah?*} That are of the lineage, or offspring of Judah, descending and issuing from him, as streams, or rivulets, from a wellhead, or spring, Deuter. 33.28. Psalm 68.26. See the like metaphor, Prov. 5.15–18. And this is an higher degree of honor and dignity, that these men arrogated to themselves: for all the twelve Tribes were descended of Jacob; but we, say they, are of the stock of Judah, the royal Tribe, Gen. 49.8,10. which had retained the service and worship of God with them, when the other fell away to idolatry, 2 Chron. 11.13–16. and 13.8–10.

*{which swear by the name of the Lord, and make mention of the God of Israel*} That swear by the true God, as professing to serve him, ch. 19.18. & 45.23. as every nation is wont to swear by that god they serve and worship, Gen. 31.53. when as yet they yield him no obedience, but abuse his name to evil purposes, Jer. 5.2. Hos. 4.15. Zeph. 1.5. and make mention of him, when they swear, Exod. 23.23. Josh. 23.17. or more generally have the name of God oft in their mouths as well out of oaths, as in oaths, as if they reverenced and regarded him, when, indeed, they do nothing less, Chapter 29.13. Jerem. 12.2.

*{but not in truth, nor in righteousness*} As an oath ought to be taken, and God's name to be used. See Jeremiah 4.2. and 5.2.

**V. 2.** *{For they call themselves of the Holy City*} As it is styled, Mat. 4.5. & 27.53. Heb. here, *the city of holiness*, or rather, *the city of the Sanctuary*. For there is an article of special designation before the noun governed: and so ch. 52.1. which, indeed, was the main ground why it was called and accounted, by an eminency, *the holy city*, in regard of God's Sanctuary there seated, and his name or worship there settled, Deut. 12.11. 2 Chron. 7.12,16. of this city Jerusalem, Ch. 52.1. they professed themselves to be citizens, even fellow citizens, with God's holy ones, Eph. 2.19. Now as the text is here read, it seems to render a further reason, of what they were formerly said to profess, to wit, that they were of Jacob's family, and Judah's issue; for they were of Jerusalem, the head city of Judah; which being yet a further matter of honor, and an higher dignity, to be citizens of so honorable and holy a city, might well help to confirm the former, because it was an adjection thereunto. But some read the words rather, *Though they call themselves of that city*; as having reference to the last words of the former verse, *not in truth, nor in righteousness*: though, or albeit, they profess themselves to be such as is hereafter mentioned; and the particle here used, is very frequently thus taken, in a discretive notion; which, not observed, has made some places the more obscure; as that, Gen. 8.21. & 48.14. Psa. 25.11. but so clearly, Josh. 17.18. Ps. 23.4. ch. 12.1. See the like, Chapter 58.2.

*{and stay themselves upon the God of Israel*} Make as if they trusted, and relied upon God, Mic. 3.11. Rom. 2.17. Joh. 2.23–25. and 6.64. Acts 8.13,23. a metaphor taken from some stay, that a man leans upon for support. See Chap. 36.6.

*{the Lord of hosts is his name*} Or, *whose name is the Lord of hosts*; as Chap. 47.4. Jer. 48.15.

**V. 3.** *{I have declared the former things from the beginning, and they went forth out of my mouth, and I showed them: I did them suddenly, and they came to pass*} Or, *The former things which I declared in times past, and which came out of my mouth, and which I showed; I did suddenly, & they came to pass.*] This is here mentioned, as oft before; partly, to assert God's divine power and providence: partly, to tax them for not adhering sincerely and constantly to him, notwithstanding those evident proofs thereof exhibited unto them, and partly, to strengthen the faith of the godly, partly in firm expectation of the future performance of those things that now he promised, See Chap. 41.22,26. & 42.9. & 43.9–13. & 45.21. & 46.10. The relative is wanting in the two first branches: as chap. 47.11. supplied by the positive in the third, as chap. 46.4. ver. 1.

*{former*} Heb. *first*: as chap. 46.9.

*{from the beginning*} Heb. *from then*; as chap. 44.7. verse 5. Since the time that I first took you to be my people, chap. 43.4. or, rather, more generally, in times past, chap. 46.9.

*{went out of my mouth*} Either by way of prediction, Psal. 89.34. or, by way of determination, Lam. 3.37,38. Chap. 45.23. See Verse 5.

*{showed*} *made to hear*, Or, *to be heard*: Chap. 41.23. & 42.2. ver. 20.

*{I did*} Whatsoever I foretold, or promised, I failed not in due time to effect, Josh. 21.45. & 23.24. chap. 45.23.

*{suddenly*} Either when they were least expected and looked for, Chap. 30.13. & 47.11. or at the very instant of time prefixed, Exo. 12.41. so Mal. 3.1.

**V. 4.** *{Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass.*} A reason why God was pleased to foretell things to his people, long before he did them; that they might not, when they were done, be ascribed to any other beside himself, by them: which he foreknew that they would be too prone to do.

*{Because I knew*} Heb. *From my knowing*; as ch. 31.4. & 53.5. Ps. 12.5. where the particle is used in a causal notion. See it in another, concerning the same subject, that is here insisted on, Deut. 9.24.

*{obstinate*} Heb. *hard*: Exod. 32.9. & 33.3,5. & 34.9. Deut. 9.6,13. & 31.27.

*{thy neck is an iron sinew*} Or, *an iron sinew is in thy neck*: a defect of the preposition; as Ch. 34.13. & 44.12. Heb. *a sinew of iron* as *a yoke of iron*, Deut. 28.48. and, *a rod of iron*, Psal. 2.9. for, *an iron yoke*, and, *an iron rod*: *an iron sinew*, for, *a stiff, hard, tough one*; as it is expounded in the places above mentioned.

*{thy brow brass*} Or, as some, *steel*: as the word is supposed to signify, Judg. 16.21. Jer. 15.12. Lam. 3.7. Heb. *brazen*; as we say, *a brazen brow*: or, *a steely*, as the word is used, Lev. 26.19. Job 6.12. and Psal. 18.34. *a bow of steel*: *a brow of steel*, or, *a steely brow*, for, a brow as hard, as if it were of brass, or steel, that is, exceeding hard. See the like phrases of *rocky faces*, Jer. 5.3. and of *stony*, and, *flinty hearts*, expressing an extremity of obstinacy, Eze. 36.26. Zach. 7.12.

**V. 5.** *{I have even from the beginning declared it to thee: before it came to pass, I showed it thee.*} See on ver. 3. the pronoun *it*, is here wanting as, chap. 46.11. See also, ver. 6.

*{lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them:*} The proneness even of many even among God's people, to ascribe unto their false gods, what God himself has done for them, Jer. 44.17,18. Hos. 2.5,8. as the heathen people used to do, Jud. 16.23. Of the word *idol*, here used, see on Chap. 10.10.

*{and my graven image, and my molten image hath commanded them*} Or, *given them in charge*; as Chap. 38.1. & 45.11. appointed them thus to come to pass. See before, *Gone out of my mouth*, ver. 3.

*{and*} Or, *or*, the copulative disjunctively; as Chap. 44.10. & 45.9. Some one, or other of mine idols.

**V. 6.** *{Thou hast heard; see all this: and will not ye declare it?*} Or, *Consider all this, which thou hast heard*; (all that I have showed you, or made you to hear, ver. 3,5.) a defect of the relative, as ver. 3. and will you dissemble what you have heard from me so long before, and not acknowledge it yourselves, and acquaint others with it, that you may be witnesses in my behalf, of the truth thereof, unto them? Chap. 43.10. & 44.8. See Chap. 43.19. Some would read the words, *and do not you yourselves publish it?* that is, publicly acknowledge it, in the celebration of your solemn rites and feasts, which you observe as memorials thereof, Psal. 81.1,2,3. Exod. 12.25–27. Lev. 23,16. Deu. 16. See the like of Christ's death, 1 Cor. 11.26. And this sense seems not improbable. Others would have it read; *and have ye declared it?* that is, have you by the help of any of your idols—foretold, any of that, that I have so foreshowed to you, Chap. 43.9. & 44.7. So the negative should be taken for an interrogative, as some would have it, Mal. 1.10. But I suppose it no more so in the one place than in the other; and doubt much, whether so in any. There might be some better color for such a form, from our version, 2 King. 1.3. if it were right: but the double negative seems there more vehemently to aver; as that triple one, Heb. 13.5.

*{I have showed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them.*} Or, *I show thee* (Heb. *make thee hear*, as ver. 5. *at present*. Heb. *from now*, as chap. 59.21. as before, *from then* ver. 3,5. (*new things*) as chap. 43.19. *and hidden*, Heb. *kept close*, or *reserved*, Prov. 7.10. Jer. 33.3. *which thou knowest not*, to wit, before, as v. 7. the copulative with the positive, put for the relative, as chap. 37.27. & 44.14. Some read the words, *and there are things reserved* (to be revealed, and done hereafter) *which* *thou knowest not*, but are as yet ignorant of. But the former runs more smoothly: Yet further to convince you of your willful obstinacy, I acquaint you again, with other of my secret counsels, which shall also in their due time be fulfilled.

**V. 7.** *{They are created now, and not from the beginning, even before the day, when thou heardest them not, lest thou shouldest say, Behold I knew them.*} Or, *They are brought to light now*, (as things are, when created (*and not in time past*, (not formerly. Heb. *from then*, as ver. 3,5,8.) or *before this day*, (the copulative disjunctively, as ver. 5. and the pronoun wanting, as Josh. 22.16,18,29. 2 Chro. 35.25.) *when thou hadst not heard of them*. Heb. *and thou heardest not of them*: as chap. 33.1. & 43.12. lest you should pretend that some other way, or from some of your idols, you had been made acquainted with them before, ver. 5. *knew*, for *knew* before, as ver. 6,8.

**V. 8.** *{Yea, thou heardest not, yea, thou knewest not: yea, from that time, that thine ear was not opened*} Or, *even* when (supplied from verse 7. to carry on the sentence depending upon it,) *thou hadst not heard, even*, when *thou knewest not; even* when *thine ear had not formerly* (Heb. *from then*: as v. 7.) *opened*; that is, opened itself, as ch. 45.8. Can. 7.12. or, *been open*, as ch. 60.11. to wit, to hear aught from any other concerning these things, that are now by me revealed to you. The repetition of the particle, *yea*, or *even*, does much quicken the sentence and make it more emphatical; as the like, chap. 40.24. Most interpreters understand it of the spiritual *opening* of the inward ear, Deut. 29.4. Chapter 50.5. as if God should intimate his free favor unto them, in revealing these things, yea, and in making them good to them, even when they continued in their obstinacy, when they stopped their ears, and would not hear, Psal. 58.4,5. Chap. 28.12. Zach. 7.12. But the former sense is the plainer.

*{for I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously*} That you would be ascribing them, and the foreknowledge of them, either to your idols, and your soothsayers, or to yourself, ver. 5,7. Heb. *wouldest dealing treacherously, deal treacherously*; as chap. 24.16. or, *Because* (as chap. 59.14.) *I knew*, that is, foreknew knew beforehand, as ver. 7.) *that thou wouldest deal very treacherously.*

*{and wast called a transgressor from the womb*} Heb. *a transgressor*, or, *a revolter*, (as, chap. 53.12.) *was called upon thee*, as chap. 62.2. for, *to be*, or, *to be accounted*, and commonly known to be: as chap. 58.12. & 60.3. I might well deem, that in future time, you would so demean yourself, because you had been prone (as was well known) to such carriage of yourself, from your beginning, Deut. 9.7,24. Chap. 63.10.

*{from the womb*} From the time that I brought you out of Egypt; which was as the birth of that state and church, chap. 46.3. Jer. 2.2. & 22.21. & 31.30. an allusion to man's natural birth, Psal. 51.5. & 58.3. of which also, some, but without good ground, understand it; this passage implying somewhat, not common to all, but peculiar to that people.

**V. 9.** *{For my name's sake will I defer mine anger; and for my praise, will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off*} Or, *for my name's sake*; (that is, for mine own self, ver. 11. Chap. 43.25. Psal. 25.11. & 106.8. Ezek. 36.31.) Or, *because of my name*, (whereby you are called, vers. 1. being accounted my people, Chap. 64.9. Jer. 14.9. Ezek. 20.9. & 36.20.) *do I foreslow*, or, *stay my anger*, or, *I am so slow to anger*; Heb. *will I prolong*, or, *do I prolong mine anger*: Now *to prolong anger*, may be taken two ways, either for *to lengthen it*, that is, to continue long in it as Psal. 85.5. *wilt thou draw out thy wrath from age to age?* though another word be there used; and so one of the Jewish writers would have it here taken, but renders no reason of it: and it seems directly contrary to the main scope of the place; but it may be taken also for *to stay* it, and suppress it, that it break not forth, that it stir not: as of the Ark it is said, Num. 9.19,22. *when it stayed*, and stirred not; where the same word is used, that we have here: and so it is used in this place; as also, Prov. 19.11. the discretion of a man *doth stay, and repress his anger*: or, *make him slow to anger*: not makes him *defer*, or, put it off, till he find opportunity to vent it: and thence *slow to anger*, Deut. 34.6. Num. 14.18. *and for my praise*, (as some, that I may have a people to serve and praise me, Psalm 102.18. 130.3,4. Ch. 43.21. 64.11. or rather, that I may gain thereby to myself, the praise of my might, and my mercy, Psal. 65.1. & 75.1. ch. 12.1. for mine honor, and my glory, Ps. 106.8. v. 11.) *do I restrain it* (to wit, *mine anger*, supplied, as the particle, *for*, also, from the former clause:) See Psal. 78.38.) *from thee*, (that is, from seizing upon you) or, *for thee*, (that is for your good) *that I destroy thee not*, Jer. 30.11. As it was of my free favor, that I chose you at first, Deut. 7.7,8. & 9.4–6. so is it of my mere mercy, and respect to mine own honor, that I have hitherto spared you, and not utterly destroyed you, and that I still forbear so to do, Num. 14.12–18. Psal. 106.45. Lam. 3.22. Some read the words. *I will seal unto thee, that I will not cut thee off*: and it is true, that the word which signifies *to seal*, differs but in one letter from this; but yet in such a letter as makes several roots; and the Jewish critics inform us that this word, which as they speak, has no mate in Scripture, is a word of the Eastern, that is, of the Syrian, language; and signifies *to obstruct, stop*, or *restrain*, and that more especially, *the nose*, which among them, therefore, is also so termed: that which suits passing well with the words of the former branch, where the word rendered *anger*, as it is very commonly used, does properly signify *the nose*, because by puffing at the nose, anger is usually discovered: and God is said *to smoke at the nostrils*, when he shows himself *angry*, Psal. 18.7,8. And so on the contrary, he is said to foreslow, and restrain his breathing out at the nose, as if his nostrils were obstructed and stopped, that he could not freely breathe at them; when he keeps in, and restrains his anger, and suffers it not to break out, or fly out so freely and fiercely, as otherwise it would do; hence the phrase *a man long*, or, *slow of breath*: that is, one that breathes slowly; opposed to one that *breatheth high*, and big, Eccl. 7.8. and *a man of long*, or *slow nostrils*, that breathes slowly at the nostrils, Prov. 15.18. & 16.32. opposed to one of *short breath*, or *quick of breath*, Prov. 14.17. and, *of short* or *quick nostrils*, Prov. 14.29. that is, one that breathes at the nostrils, short and quick: the former, used for one that is slow to wrath; the latter, for one that is of an hasty disposition. See further, on Jer. 15.15.

**V. 10.** *{Behold I have refined thee, but not with silver*} Some render it, as here, in the time past; *I have refined thee* by many afflictions already, and yet are you never the better for them, Jer. 5.3. Others rather, in the future, *I will refine thee*, Ch. 1.25. Jer. 9.7.

*{not with silver*} Or, *as silver*; *as silver*, in some respects, Psal. 66.10. to purge and purify them, Dan. 11.35. Mal. 3.2,3. yet in some respects, *not as silver*, that is, not so exactly, and exquisitely, as silver is wont to be fined, which the finer uses to keep in the fire, till all the dross be wasted, and wrought out of it: intimating, that he would not deal overstrictly, and severely with them: but use much moderation in chastising of them: regarding their infirmity, who would be themselves utterly consumed, if God should hold them so long in the furnace, until their drossy matter were all melted out of them. See Psal. 103.9,14. & 118.18. Chap. 27.7,8. & 57.16. Jer. 10.24. and 30.11. Some render it, *not into silver*: as if he had said, all my melting of you, so full of dross, and other base metal you are, has not hitherto made you, nor will ever make you become good silver, Chap. 1.21. Jer. 6.27–30. Ezek. 22.18–22. Others, and so the ancient Greek, *not for silver*: as if he had said, I have got nothing by sending you into Babylon, such another furnace as Egypt was, Deut. 4.20. and melting you there. So Psal. 44.12. Chapter 52.3. But these two latter seem not so natural.

*{I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction*} Or, as others *I will choose thee*; that is, make a choice one of you, by purifying of you through afflictions, and fitting you thereby for myself, chap. 1.25. Dan. 12.10. Mal. 3.2,3. Acts 14.23. Heb. 12.10. 2 Tim. 2.20,21. 1 Pet. 1.6,7. Rom. 7.14. See chap. 49.7. But some other read the words: *I have selected*, or *set thee apart, for the furnace of affliction*: to be therein tried, and purified more & more better than you have hitherto been. I suppose that to be most genuine which the Jewish commenters, most of them, on the place give, *I have made choice of a furnace* or, *a melting pot*, rather, *of affliction for thee*. Heb. *I have chosen thee*: that is, *chosen* for *thee*: as, *given me*, for, *given to me*, Josh. 15.19. Judg. 1.15. as we also speak concisely, in either: so, *come us*, for, *come at us*, chap. 28.15. *dwell thee*, for, *dwell* with *thee*, Psal. 5.4. and many other the like: *in the furnace*, or *a furnace*, or, *melting pot*; for the verb of *choosing* here used, has this preposition (as another also) prefixed before the noun after it, vacant, according to the manner of that language. So Deut. 7.7. & 14.2. *the Lord chose to thee*, for, *the Lord chose thee*: and 1 Sam. 10.16. and Psal. 105.26. *hath chosen in him*, for, *chosen him, a melting pot*, for so the word properly signifies, Prov. 17.3. & 26.21.) *of affliction*, that is, affliction to be, as, or, for, a melting pot: as, *the sign of circumcision*, Rom. 4.11. that is, circumcision to be a sign. So that the meaning is, that God had appointed their affliction in Babylon, during the time of their captivity there, to be as a melting pot unto them, as the like in Jerusalem, had formerly been, during the siege, Ezek. 22.18,19.

**V. 11.** *{For mine own sake, even for mine own sake will I do it*} That which he says elsewhere, *I wrought for my name's sake, that I might not be polluted in the sight of heathen people*, Ezek. 20.9,14,22. where the word is the same, as also, chap. 43.13. and the word may well be so rendered here; *For mine own sake will I work*. I will have a regard to mine own honor and credit, though you deserve nothing less, than what I do intend to do; and then there needs no supply: otherwise, *it* or *this*, is to be supplied: as ch. 10.13. ver. 5,6. Ezek. 36,37. Mal. 3.17. See chap. 44.23. there is an emphasis in the repetition: as Psal. 115.1. Chap. 43.25. as if he had said, *for myself alone*, as Psal. 51.4. and not for you, or for any desert of yours, Ezek. 36.32. See ver. 9.

*{for how should my name be polluted?*} Heb. *how should it be polluted?* to wit, *my name*; supplied from ver. 9. otherwise how would mine honor be eclipsed and obscured in the minds of people: as if I were not able to save, or to deliver my people? See Num. 14.15,16. Deut. 32.27–37,38. Josh. 7.8,9. Psalm 42.10. and 115.1,2. & 106.8. Ezek. 36.20.

*{and I will not give my glory to another*} Or, *to any other*: as Exod. 34.14. I am very chary, and jealous of mine honor, and cannot endure any corrival in it, Exod. 20.5. & 34.7. Deut. 4.24. and 5.9.

**V. 12.** *{Hearken unto me, O Jacob, and Israel my called*} Whom I called out of Egypt, Hos. 11.1. or, whom I have called to be my peculiar people, Ch. 44.1. 1 Cor. 1.14,26,27. or that are called by my name, as my people, Chap. 43.7. & 63.19. as, *so the called of Jesus Christ*; that is, not called by him only, but to be his, and by calling made his, Rom. 1.6. See chap. 44.1. & 46.3.

*{I am he*} Or, *I am*; or, *I am the same*. See chap. 41.4. & 43.10. & 46.4. & 47.8.

*{I am the first, I also am the last*} Chap. 41.4. & 44.6.

**V. 13.** *{My hand hath also laid the foundation of the earth*} Psal. 102.25. Chap. 42.5. & 45.12. & 51.13.

*{and my right hand hath spanned the heavens*} Or, *doth span the heavens*; does mete them out, as a workman does his work in meting whereof, when he makes use of the hand, he does it with the right hand rather than with the left. Or, as some, *the palm of my right hand hath spread out the heavens*: the word is used, Lam. 2.22. of mothers, or nurses, that either dandle their little ones in their hands, or lay them out to stretch their limbs, that signifies the measure of an hand spread out, or *a span*, Ex. 25.24. Psal. 39.5. See Ch. 40.12.

*{when I call unto them, they stand up together*} Or, *I call them, and they stand up together*; according to the former reading, a defect of the adverb: as Chap. 41.17. ver. 21. according, to the latter of the copulative; than which, nothing more frequent. The celestial bodies are as servants, that stand attending on Princes, or great persons, 1 King. 1.2. & 10.8. Prov. 22.29. ready prest at a word, or a beck, to obey me their Sovereign Lord, Maker, and Master; and to go instantly about whatsoever I enjoin them, Psal. 119.91. & 148.8. Mat. 8.9. See Chap. 40.26. All this is here related, to assure them of God's power, and all sufficient ability, to effect their deliverance according to his promise. So chap. 40.26,27.

**V. 14.** *{All ye assemble yourselves, and hear*} These words seem to be spoken by the prophet in his own person: and so most take them; because the Lord is spoken of in the third person, in the latter end of this verse: and the prophet speaks of himself in the first person, in the latter end of verse 16. But there is no necessity thereof: for God speaks of himself of in the third person, as chap. 37.24,31. & 40.19,31. in the next verse, God himself still speaks in his own person, as Chapter 37.24,32. & 40.29,31. in the next verse, God himself still speaks in his own person: and the prophet oft passes suddenly from person to person, in that 16 verse, as appears plainly by the fifteenth, interjected, at least if not in the sixteenth itself. The words therefore I suppose to be spoken, as by God himself: and that to his people, to convince them of his divine power, showed in foretelling of things so long before; and to be further manifested in the fulfilling of them. So ver. 12,16. and so to the nations, chap. 41.1. & 43.9.

*{Which among them hath declared these things?*} Which of the heathen idols has foretold aught of them? Chap. 41.22,23. and 44.7. & 45.21.

*{The Lord hath loved him*} *The Lord*, that is, *I* (as ver. 15. the noun, for the pronoun, as chap. 2.1. & 3.4,5,6,8. 2 Tim. 1.18.) *do love him*, to wit, Cyrus: as, *he fastened it*, to wit, the smith, the image; So, *he said*, for, God said, Gen. 15.14. and, *he wrote*, for, God wrote, Exod. 34.28. and, *he went*, for, the King went, 2 King. 25.4. I do so far forth affect, and favor Cyrus, as to prosper him in his proceedings, and to honor him with glorious success in his undertakings, having made choice of him, to overthrow Babylon, and to free my people there detained, chap. 45.1–4. See ch. 52.1.

*{He will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans,*} Or, *he* (that is, Cyrus, as before) *shall* (as in the next clause) *do his* that is, the Lord's) *pleasure*, chap. 44.28. See there: *and his arm* (that is, his warlike power, as chap. 30.30. & 59.16.) *shall be upon the Chaldeans*: shall light heavy upon them, to disperse, and destroy them. See chap. 43.14.

**V. 15.** *{I, even I have spoken*} Or, *I, even I*, (as chap. 43.25.) *have spoken it*; a defect of the pronoun: chap. 46.11. and a return again to the first person.

*{yea, I have called him;*} I have raised him up, according to my purpose and counsel, by a secret instinct, Chapter 45.4,13. and 46.11.

*{I have brought him:*} Heb. *made him to go*, or, *caused him to come* sent him to *Babylon*, Chapter 43.14. on mine errand: to do me service there, Ver. 14.

*{he shall make his way prosperous*} That is, *I will make his way prosperous*: the third person for the first; as before ver. 14. or, *his way shall be made prosperous*: the verb taken indefinitely, as Cha. 46.6,7. or, *he shall prosper in his way*: the verb taken neutrally, and the preposition supplied, as chap. 55.11. which I take to be the genuine syntax, as well here, as there.

**V. 16.** *{Come ye near unto me, hear ye this.*} See on ver. 14.

*{I have not spoken in secret from the beginning*} Heb. *from the head*, as chap. 41.26. This some understand of God: as chap. 45.19. that, he had in public, and openly, delivered his oracles from time to time, unto his people, ever since that he took them, at first, to himself, Num. 11.25,26. Jer. 7.25. Others of the prophet Esay, as professing of himself, that he had openly delivered, and publicly declared God's Mind and Will unto them, ever since God had called him unto that office, chap. 6.8,9. & 50.4,5. I rather follow the former, the very same being protested by God himself, in the place there pointed to.

*{from the time, that I was, there am I*} This, those that conceive it to be spoken of God, understand two several ways; some, in the time past, as if it were said, ever since that aught was, or had being, I was there: to wit, at the creating of them: as noting God's eternity, Prov. 8.22–30. chap. 43.10,13. & 44.6. or, *from the time, when that was*, (to wit, of my taking you unto me) I have been *there*, present among you, in my prophets, by my Spirit, Deut. 18.15,16. Chap. 59.21. and 63.11. Some rather, whom I concur with, of the time to come: *from the time that this shall be*, (when the time appointed shall come, wherein this great work, which is now foretold you, is to be put in execution,) *there*, will *I be* present and ready at hand, to carry on the work, and to cause it to be accomplished: the same, in effect, with that, Chap. 46.11. and ver. 15. Those that understand it of the prophet, take it also two several ways: Some, *from the time before which it was done, there I was*: so the old Latin, and they that follow it; that is, say they, I foresaw things to come as evidently, as if I were present at the doing of them, Chap. 13.2. so Joh. 8.56. but I see not how the words will admit this reading. Others, ever since God's charge came to me, (as Hos. 1.2.) I have constantly attended it, chap. 21.8. So Jer. 6.26. Hab. 2.1. For that is most ridiculous, that some of the Jewish commenters here suggest, of all the prophets being present with Moses, on Mount Sinai, at the giving of the Law, and so Esay among the rest, Deut. 33.2.

*{and now the Lord God, and his Spirit hath sent me*} This likewise some conceive spoken by Christ, the Word Joh. 1.1. and Wisdom, of the Father, Prov. 8.1,23. by whom he reveals himself, and his Will and purposes to his people, Mat. 11.27. Joh. 1.18. Zach. 2.9,11. 1 Pet. 1.10–12. sent by the Father, and the Spirit, to acquaint them with those gracious promises, as well the spiritual ones, as the temporal, that were types of the spiritual, Ch. 61.1. Luk. 4.18,21. But others, whom I rather accord with, conceive this clause to be spoken by the prophet of himself, sent by the three Persons jointly, about the delivery, as of other God's messages, so of this in special: added here more expressly, to give the greater assurance of the truth and certainty of it, and of the accomplishment thereof. So Jer. 26.12,15. See Ch. 6.8,9. The prophet does many times pass suddenly, & (as may seem, to persons not acquainted with spiritual raptures, and ecstasies.) somewhat abruptly, in the heat of delivery, from one person to another.

**V. 17.** *{Thus saith the Lord thy Redeemer, the Holy one of Israel*} See Chap. 43.14.

*{I am the Lord thy God, which teacheth thee to profit*} Heb. *teaching thee*, or, *who do teach thee* (as Chap. 44.24.) *to profit*, Who teach you such things, as for your welfare, that conduce to your peace and prosperity, ver. 18. Deut. 4.1,40. and 5.29. & 6.3. Job 22.21. Luk. 19.42.

*{which leadeth thee, by the way that thou shouldest go.*} Heb. *making thee to tread* (that is, *teaching* you, and directing you to go, as Psal. 25.5. & 43.10. as a guide does a traveler, chap. 30.21. or, as a nurse does a child, Hos. 11.12.) *in the way, thou shalt walk*; that is, wherein you should walk: the relative wanting, as ch. 47.11. and as frequently with us, and the verb taken in signification of duty: as Chap. 26.9. so Psal. 25.12,13,14.

**V. 18.** *{O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandment:*} Deut. 5.29. & 32.26. Psal. 81.13. implying, that then they had escaped many evils, and much sorrow, that *melting pot of affliction*, that in the captivity of Babylon, they had so long lain in, among the rest, ver. 10. which by their sinful excesses, willful disobedience, and obstinacy therein, they procured to themselves, Psal. 81.11,12. Jer. 7.23–28. & 26.2–6.

*{then had thy peace been as a river*} *thy peace*; that is your prosperity, as Psal. 119.165. should have abounded, as those rivers that flow with great streams; and do oft times overflow their banks. So Ch. 59.19. Jer. 12.5. and because of the article enclosed in the note of similitude, *as the river*: some of the Rabbins suppose, that Euphrates is here more specially pointed at: as Psal. 72.8. Chap. 7.20.

*{and thy righteousness, as the waves of the sea*} This is, the same in effect, though in other terms, with the former. By *righteousness*, is here meant, not any moral virtue, or gracious disposition: as the word properly, & most commonly signifies, Ps. 11.7. & 45.7. Eph. 4.24. But as some, a state well composed, & wanting nothing, that is due unto it, or requisite to its complete happiness, Ps. 72.3. Joel 2.23. Others, *prosperity*, as before: so called, because the fruit of peace, as some, Rom. 14.17. Heb. 12.11. Jam. 3.18. the reward of righteousness, as others, Gen. 30.32. as *iniquity*, for, *punishment*, the fruit and reward of it, Gen. 4.13. or, which I take to be the genuine sense of it, a confluence of all good things, which God, out of his benignity, is wont, in way of beneficence, (for that also, by the word of *righteousness*, is oft understood. Ps. 1,2,3,4,9.) 2 Cor. 9.9,10. to impart unto & confer upon a people. So is the word used, 2 Sa. 12.7. Psal. 36.5,6,10. where *benignity* and *righteousness* are twice joined together: as things very near, if not the same, as also, Ps. 75.9,10. See also, Psal. 48.9,10. compared with Prov. 3.16,17. Chap. 54.17. and 58.8. and 63.7. and this is called God's, Psal. 36.6,10. because it comes from him, Chap. 54.17. and yet theirs also, Chapter 54.17. & 58.8. because conferred upon them, Chap. 45.24. Deut. 28.1–13.

*{as the waves of the sea,*} As great plenty of all good, as of water in the sea, or, in the main ocean, where waves wallow most at large. See the like, Chap. 11.9. So the Greeks use to say, *A sea of good things*, for, great abundance thereof.

**V. 19.** *{Thy seed also had been as the sand*} Your issue should have been not numerous only, but numberless, Gen. 13.16. & 15.5. & 22.17. & 32.12. Jer. 30.22. Hos. 2.10. See the like expression, Chap. 10.22. Gen. 41.49. 1 Sam. 1.38. 2 Sam. 13.11. 1 King. 4.20,29. Job 29.18. Ps. 78.27. & 139.18. Jer. 15.8. Hab. 1.9.

*{and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof:*} *Offspring*, see Chap. 44.3. Heb. *the comings out*; as chap. 34.1. & 42.5. put for, *issue*, Job 5.25. & 21.8. & 27.14. and 31.8. Chap. 61.9. & 65.23. so called, because they are said to come out of the bowels of their parents, Gen. 15.4. & 25.23. 2 Sam. 13.11. in allusion whereunto, the gravel stones or beach, that lie on the shore, by the seaside, are in the Hebrew here styled, *the bowels thereof*, to wit, of the sea; to be supplied from Verse 28. the pronoun for the noun, as Verse 14.

*{his name should not have been cut off, nor destroyed from before me*} *His name*: that is, the memory of him, (*name*, for, *memorial*, as Ps. 83.4. Prov. 10.7.) or their posterity (in whom, men's names are continued, Num. 27.4.) should always have been acceptable with me: or as others, This your prosperous estate had continued with you, and your posterity, without interruption, Psal. 81.14,15. Zeph. 3.7. or, You had not been cast out of your land, and your *name*, that is, the glory of your state, and the renown thereof, cut off, Jer. 22.30. & 36.30. Lam. 5.16. (See Ezek. 16.13,14.) nor had you been removed out of my sight, the Temple being defaced, & destroyed wherein you were wont to appear before me, and to attend me, and have communion, as my people, with me, Psal. 42.2. and 84.7. See Jer. 35.19. Howbeit, others (the rather for that gracious promise of never cutting off, or casting off the whole seed of Israel, Jer. 31.37.) read the words, as spoken in way of commination, or intimation of what should befall them; but in way of mitigation, and of a favorable exception, with supply of a discretive particle, thus, *Yet shall not his name be cut off, nor destroyed from before me*; or, *out of my sight*, Jer. 33.18. See Chap. 49.5,16. Jer. 30.11. and 31.37. and 46.28. in which last place, God promises, that notwithstanding all the sins and abominations committed by them, yet he would not utterly either cut, or cast them off, See the like defect of the like particle, Job 14.9. Chap. 44.11. And this sense seems the more probable; because presently follows a promise of deliverance, and restitution again, Ver. 20. See the like, 2 King. 14.24,26,27. The words run in the Hebrew somewhat otherwise, than they are in our version; *He should not have been*, or, *shall not be, cut off, nor his name destroyed out of my sight*. But the difference is not much material; save that the cutting off of their persons, seems imported (whether implied, or denied,) in the one; the casting off all care of them, or special relation to them, in the other: an allusion, it may be deemed, to enrollment of servants, and retinue in some great man's family; soldiers in an army, pensioners in a state, or the like. See the like, Exod. 32.32,33. Psal. 69.28. cha. 34.26,27.

**V. 20.** *{Go ye forth of Babylon; flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing*} A promise of deliverance from the Babylonian thraldom, not by a timorous, and hazardous flight: as when servants and captives break away from their hard masters, by stealth, Gen. 31.20,27. Exod. 14.5–9. 1 Sam. 25.10. but freely and cheerfully, without fear of stay, or pursuit, as merrily as a slave, or captive, that is rescued out of thraldom and bondage, and set at full liberty. See Chap. 52.12. Howbeit some understand the words, as an admonition unto the Jews, abiding in Babylon, to get out of the city, and escape by flight, so soon as they hear tidings of Cyrus his entrance into Chaldea, or approach to the city, and not stay the surprisal of it Ch. 51.14. 52.11. Jer. 50.8. & 51.6,45. Zach. 2.6. Rev. 18.4. See the like Gen. 19.15. Jer. 46.5. & 47.3. and 48.9. Matth. 24.15–19. Luk. 17.31,32. But the *singing* here mentioned, seems rather to import their departure, with free and full liberty upon Cyrus his proclamation, Ezra 1.1. See Psal. 14.7. and 126.1,3. ch. 12.1,5. and 26.1. and 35.10.

*{declare it, tell this; utter it, even to the end of the earth:*} See the like, chap. 12.4,5.

*{declare it*} Some join the former clause, *with singing*, to this; as if it were said, *with joy tell it*, or talk of it, one to, or with, another: but the pauses annex it rather to the former; and this with what follows, seems to require the publishing of it, to other, Psal. 9.11.

*{tell*} Heb. *make it to be heard*: as ver. 3,5,6.

*{utter it*} Heb. *make it to go forth*, or *to pass*; as Psal. 19.4.

*{say ye, the Lord hath redeemed his servant Jacob*} Has rescued, and delivered him out of the Chaldean captivity, Psal. 107.2,3. as formerly out of the Egyptian bondage, Exod. 19.4–6. A type of their spiritual deliverance by Christ, Luk. 1.68. Col. 1.13. Some would have it read in the future, *The Lord will redeem*; and parallel it with that, Luke 21.28. but it seems spoken rather to the people, as telling what they should say, when they were set at large; as chap. 12.4.

*{his servant*} As chap. 41.8. 44.1.

**V. 28.** *{And they thirsted not, when he led them through the deserts; he caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them; he clave the rock also, and the waters gushed out.*} This may well be read in the future: *And they shall not thirst*, as when *he led them through the deserts*. For the prophet returns to speak in his own person, and to tell them, how it shall be with them, after their enlargement. For whereas it might be said, how shall we go with so much mirth and jollity, when we have so long and tedious a way to travel, before we can get home into our own country, and are to pass through so many wild and waste places, wherein, through want of necessaries, we may perish and miscarry by the way. The prophet, therefore tells them, that God will look to that, he will furnish them with all necessaries, one way or other: and to put them out of fear, and doubt thereof, to wit, of his power to make provision sufficient for them, he minds them of what he did in former times when he led them through the wilderness to the land of Canaan; how he furnished them with water, the greatest matter of want in those places, and most necessary for man's sustenance in travel, in those hot regions especially. Exodus 17.6. Numbers 20.11,12. Psalm 78.15. and 105.41. implying withal, that what God had then done, he could now do: yea, and would do; he would as well and sufficiently supply them, with that, and all other necessary accommodations, as if he had done the very selfsame thing again. See Chapter 41.18. and 49.10.

*{they thirsted not*} Or, *they shall not thirst*; as Chap. 49.10. not that they should not at all thirst; for hunger, and thirst, are natural affections, so far from being of themselves simply any annoyance; that they are as sauce, to give relish to our food: but that they should not, when they were athirst, want wherewith to slake and quench it. So Joh. 4.14. & 6.35. & 7.37,38.

*{when he led*} Or, as when *he led*: a defect of the adverb of time; as ver. 13. chap. 41.17. of the note of similitude, as chap. 33.4,11. See Chap. 17.5.

**V. 22.** *{There is no peace, saith the Lord, unto the wicked.*} Or, as some render it, *But*, or, *yet no peace shall be to the wicked*: *no peace*, that is, *no prosperity*: no prosperous success in aught, as ver. 18. See Psal. 1.3,4. the discretive is supplied; as Chapter 44.11. This some understand this of the profane and wicked party among the Jews, that they should have no part or share in the prosperity promised to God's people, Chap. 65.21. Others, of the Babylonians, the enemies of God's people, that all things should go cross with them, Chap. 13.11–16. Others, both of the one, and of the other; and of the unquiet and restless condition of either; yea, of all wicked ones in general, Job 15.20,21. and 20.20. See Chap. 57.20,21.

### CHAPTER 49

**V. 1.** *{Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, O people from far.*} The prophecy delivered, and recorded in this chapter, runs on in the same strain with the former, relating the restoration and enlargement, of God's church, consisting both of Jews and Gentiles, under a type of the Jews' releasement from the Babylonian deportation: and the reestablishment of them in their former estate, with much honor and increase, by accession of other nations unto them; both effected by the mighty power of the Lord Jesus the Messiah. In these first words is contained a preamble, prefixed before the delivery of the prophecy, inviting people, far and near to hear it, and inciting them to give due attention, unto the things therein delivered. See the like, chap. 41.4.

*{Listen*} Heb. *Hear*: as chap. 1.2. or, *hearken*, as chap. 51.1. a duty required as in regard of all God's prophets in general, Amos 3.1. & 4.1. Zach. 7.7. so, more specially, in regard of Christ, that principal Prophet, or Prince of Prophets, Deut. 18.18,19. Acts 3.22,23. by whom, the Father reveals himself, his mind, and his mysteries, both to his prophets, and to his people, Mat. 11.27. & 17.5. Joh. 1.18. & 3.13. Heb. 1.1,2. & 2.1–3. & 3.1,7. & 4.2,7. & 12.15,25.

*{O isles*} Or, *lands, countries*, Ch. 41.1. Some expound it simply, *islands*, being remote, say they, from the countries situate in the continent. Others, *transmarine* regions: such of them, especially, as coast upon the sea: but the word seems more general, as chap. 20.6. & Jer. 47.4. so here: and the *lands* are put for the inhabitants, or those that abide therein; as the next clause shows.

*{unto me*} The Jewish commenters understand this, as spoken in the person of the prophet Esay himself, calling upon them, to give ear to God's message, which he was to deliver, wherein also some of ours concur with them: and it is not improbable, that divers passages in these prophecies might have some reference to him, as in part verified in him, but in a more peculiar, and transcendent manner, to be accomplished in Christ, of whom, therefore principally intended; of Esay only, as what was done either by him, or about him might hold out some shadowy resemblance of such excellent graces, as were to be conferred upon Christ; and glorious works as were to be effected by him. See chap. 50.4. & 61.1. So divers of ours, understand this; though the most, of Christ alone without relation to any other: as the person, by whom was to be wrought whatsoever benefit God intended to bestow upon his people, either in those times, or in these: and who, as by the prophet he then foretold them, so was to be depended upon both now and then, for the making of them good, Chapter 11.10. Rom. 15.8–12. 2 Cor. 1.20. and 5.18,19,20. Ephes. 1.3. and 2.13–17. Col. 1.19,20. and 2.3,9.

*{and hearken*} Or, *attend*; for the word signifies a sedulous, and serious attention, to aught, either heard, or seen, chap. 21.7. & 28.24. So chap. 34.1. & 51.4.

*{O people*} Not you Jews alone, but you people also abroad; either because the Jewish people were to be dispersed among them, and to be thence again recollected, ver. 12. chap. 11.11,12. or because the salvation in this prophecy foretold, should concern the Gentiles, as well as the Jews, ver. 6. chap. 60.3. & 65.19,20.

*{from far*} Either in regard of distance of place, ver. 12. Chap. 60.4. or, of disposition, and affection, Eph. 2.13,17. Some of the Jewish writers understand it of the ensuing ages: not you alone, that now are; but those that shall be in after times, as some also expound the like, Act. 2.39. but this seems here not so fit.

*{the Lord hath called me from the womb;*} Here follows the matter, or message, unto the hearing whereof, such attention was required. And it is principally of Christ his office to be the Savior, both of Jew and Gentile, and God's calling him thereunto which in regard it was the main foundation of that work, wherein he was to be employed, Heb. 5.4–6,9,10. the prophet begins first with it.

*{called me from the womb*} God the Father, who, from eternity had foreassigned me to this office, 1 Pet. 1.20. did, both while I was yet in the womb, and so soon as I was come out of it, manifest and make known this his purpose concerning me, both to men and angels, Mat. 1.21–23. Luk. 2.10,11,13. Heb. 1.6. the like is, in respect of their office and employment, in their inferior sphere, spoken also of other the servants of God, extraordinary ones especially, Jer. 1.5. Luk. 1.15. Gal. 2.15. and may be verified also of this our prophet.

*{from the bowels of my mother*} While I was yet unborn, or so soon as I was conceived in the womb of the virgin, Mat. 1.20. Luk. 1.35. ver. 5. See Act. 13.32,33.

*{hath he made mention of my name.*} Or, *he recorded*, or, *entered upon record my name*; he made a solemn record of it, as chap. 12.4. Whence the term, that signifies *a Recorder*, or, *Remembrancer*, Chap. 36.3. or, *he mentioned* (that is, assigned me) *my name*, and called me thereby to give notice of that work and office, that he had designed me unto, Mat. 1.21. Luk. 1.31. & 2.21. The like hereunto was even before conception, birth much more, done with some special instruments, by God intended for remarkable employments; as Josias, 1 King. 13.2. Cyrus, chap. 44.28. & 45.1–3. and John the Baptist, Luk. 1.13,60,63. that which the Hebrew doctors, some of them affirm also, of this our prophet; to wit, that (as *John's* name was by God assigned him, importing that *Grace of God*, which he was to publish, Luk. 1.17. 76–79. so) the prophet Esay's name, was before his birth, imposed on him by God, thereby to import that *Salvation of God*, which he was to foretell. See chap. 1.1. But of this their assertion, we have no assurance: albeit we are not able to say, that it was not so; and leave it therefore in suspense.

**V. 2.** *{And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword*} Having avouched Christ's calling to the work of man's redemption; he proceeds, now, to a relation, of God's fitting, and furnishing of him, with abilities sufficient, for so important a work: together with his sustaining and supporting of him, in the performance of the same.

*{he*} The Father, from whom all power is derived, and communicated unto Christ, chap. 50.4. & 61.1. Mat. 11.27. & 28.18. Joh. 3.34,35. & 5.19,23. Col. 1.19. & 2.3,9. 2 Pet. 1.16,17.

*{hath made*} All, so far as concerns Christ, revealed in the flesh, 1 Tim. 3.16. runs in a prophetical strain; speaking of things future, as present, or past. So Chap. 7.14. and 45.5. & 51.16.

*{my mouth like a sharp sword*} The word of Christ is a sword of all sufficient power and efficacy, as for the subduing of men's souls, to the obedience of it: so for the cutting off, of whomsoever, or whatsoever shall oppose, or withstand it; compared therefore to *a sword*, and said to be sharper than any *two-edged sword* whatsoever, Chap. 11.4. Eph. 6.17. Heb. 4.12. Rev. 1.16. & 6.2. this also some apply to the prophet, whom God, by his Word, and Spirit, enabled, to the cutting down, & killing of sin in men's souls. See the apostle, what he says of his ministry, 2 Cor. 2.14–16. & 4.7. & 10.4–6. There is an elegant allusion in the original, which in other languages, cannot be so fully, or fitly expressed; for the word *mouth*, in the Hebrew, is ambiguous, & signifies as well the *edge* of the sword, as the *mouth* of man, or beast: hence, *a sword of mouths*, for, *a sword of divers edges*, Ps. 149.6. Pro. 5.4. and *they shall fall by the mouth*, that is, the edge of the *sword*, Luk. 21.24. and with the Greeks, as *a sharp-mouthed*, for, *a sharp-edged*; so, *a double-mouthed*, for, *a double-edged, sword*, Heb. 4.12. Revel. 1.16. that which the Latin, call, *a double-headed* one: but each language has its peculiar properties: the speech seems to be defective; for it is more fully, as if it had been said, *he hath made my mouth, like the* (mouth that is, *the edge*,) *of a sharp sword*: as Daniel 4.33. *till his hairs were grown like eagles*, (that is, *like the feathers of eagles*) *and his nails like birds*; that is, *like the claws of birds*: *mouth*, for, *word*, frequently, Genesis 45.21. Levit. 24.12. Numbers 3.16. but here more specially, in allusion to the term, no less commonly used of the *sword*, Judg. 1.8,25. & 4.15,16. & 18.27. & 20.37.

*{in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me*} *in*, or *with*, as Psal. 17.7. chap. 37.38. He has taken me into his powerful protection, chap. 51.16. *shadow*, for, *protection*; as Numb. 14.9. Psal. 17.8. and 31.20. & 91.1,2. Eccl. 7.12. *hand*, for, *power*, as chap. 10.10,13. and 11.11. & 23.11. & 26.11. verified, as of other his prophets, and servants, Jer. 1.18,19. & 15.20,21. & 20.11. so in more special manner, of his Messiah, Psal. 2.1–4. chap. 42.1. whom the Lord so protected, against all the might and malice of his capital enemies, that they neither could lay hold on him, or do aught to him, before the time, by God foredesigned, was come, Joh. 7.30,44. Luk. 22.53. nor yet keep him under, when that time was once over; though they endeavored what they could, to do it, Mat. 27.62–66. & 27.2–6. Acts 2.23,24.

*{and made me a polished shaft*} As before, *a sword* to cut; so here, *a shaft* to pierce: that, at hand, this at distance, that none may escape him: though I approve not that nicety of some Jewish writers, that would have him termed *a sword*, for the Jewish nation, near at hand, Psal. 148.14. *a shaft*, for the heathen people, to reach them further abroad, ver. 1. See chap. 41.2. as before, not a dull, but *a sharp sword*, Rev. 1.16. to cut the quicker; so here, *a shaft trimmed*, Ezek. 21.21. and so sharpened, to make it pierce the deeper. See Psal. 45.5. *a shaft polished*, respecting the head, or point of it, as *a sword furbished*, in reference to the edge of it, Ezek. 21.9. of this piercing power of the Word, (the efficacy whereof, is in both similitudes implied,) see Act. 2.37. Some render it, (and so both the old Latin, and the Greek) as *a choice arrow*; such an one, as may both fly far, and pierce deep: and the word sometime, indeed, seems to signify *choice* or, *chief*, 1 Chron. 7.40. & 16.41. Neh. 5.18. Cant. 6.10. but here rather, as elsewhere, when applied to *shafts*, or *arrows*, by whetting or polishing, made *bright*, and *sharp*. See Jer. 51.11. See also of *God's sword*, Ezek. 21.28. and the like spoken of God's people, what is here said of Christ, Zach. 9.13.

*{in his quiver hath he hid me*} The *quiver*, the place, wherein *shafts* are, both for safety and readiness at hand, wont to be disposed, Psa. 127.5. ch. 22.6. Jer. 5.16. (as the sword in the *sheath*, or *scabbard*, Jer. 47.6.) called, therefore, *the sons*, or, *children of the quiver*; because usually put up in it, and drawn out of it, as occasion is, to make use of them, Lamen. 3.13. In this resemblance therefore seems to be implied, as God's providence, so Christ's obedience; as God's protection, for the safeguard of Christ: so Christ's readiness, to do all faithful service to God his Father, Psal. 40.7,8. Heb. 10.5,7. ch. 42.1. & 50.5,7. Joh. 5.30. & 6.38. Heb. 3.2,5,6. but the former more specially. And the like protection will the Lord afford unto all his true and faithful servants, Psal. 31.19,20. For I suppose them overcurious, who by the *quiver*, would have understood, here, Christ's humanity; by the *shaft*, his deity.

**V. 3.** *{And said unto me*} Or, *And he* (the Lord, ver. 1.) *said unto me*, or, *Moreover*, (as Chap. 8.1. because it begins a new relation of a further matter) *he said unto me*. The words of God follow, who having called the Messiah, set him apart, sanctified him, and sent him into the world, for the executing of that office, whereunto he had assigned him, Chap. 61.1. 2. Joh. 6.27,29. and 10.36. does, by his speech, to him, in the words ensuing related, encourage him to set upon it, and to go on cheerfully, and constantly, in it, with assurance of success.

*{Thou art my Servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.*} Thus most read the words; or, with little variation, by way not of compellation, but of apposition, some, *Israel in whom I will be glorified*; but much divided in their expositions. Some by *Israel*, here, understand *Christ*: so called, say some because he was of the stock of Israel. Which though it cannot be doubted of, much less denied; yet they produce us no place of Scripture, where the word *Israel*, is used for an Israelite, though for the body of the people, or the better part of them, it is frequently found, Chap. 43.1,14. and 44.1,21. or, because the head of the Elect, *the Israel of God*, Gal. 6.16. who are one body with him, Joh. 17.20,21. Eph. 1.22,23. but this is also liable to the same exception with the former: for albeit, in regard of the conjunction of the faithful with Christ, by insition into him, Rom. 11.17,24. yea, of those also, in some sort, that profess the faith of Christ, by external adherence unto him, Joh. 15.2. the name of *Christ*, is sometime given as well to the one, Gal. 3.16. as to the other, 1 Cor. 12.12. Yet I no where find, that the name of *Israel*, is given unto Christ, for, as for that place, Luk. 1.54. which some popish authors produce, it looks plainly another way: or, say some again, as the true *Israel*, that should wrestle with the wrath of God, and prevail against it, as Jacob did with the Angel, and thence gained that name, Gen. 32.26,28. But this also, seems overquaint. Others therefore, who retain this reading, understand it of Esay; so called, say they, as a right Israelite: such an one, as Nathaniel, Joh. 1.47. yea, as the only Israel, in a manner, that God, in those times of general defection, had loyal to him, and constant with him, Chap. 59.15,16. and 64.6,7. Mich. 7.1,2. But this exposition labors with as many difficulties as the former. Others, again, of the whole seed of the true *Israel*, consisting jointly of the faithful, both of Jew, and Gentile, Rom. 9.6. & 11.26. and it is true, that *Israel*, is styled *God's servant*, Chap. 44.1. but, they that, after this reading, do here so understand it, consider not the coherence of this verse with the former, wherein some particular person is apparently deciphered, and so make the context very abrupt. This to salve, and make the text run the smoother, some thus render the words, *Thou art my servant, to Israel*, or, *for, Israel*; that is, for Israel's good; for my people's behoof. Which they expound, some of Esay: of whom it is questionless, true: the prophet being principally sent on God's errand, to them, Chap. 1.1. & 2.1. Others, of Christ, who as he came of them, Rom. 9.5. and had been formerly promised to them, Acts 2.30. and 13.23,32. so, was in the first place, sent unto them, Mat. 4.23,24. and 10.6. Luke 24.47. Act. 3.26. and 13.23,46. and 28.25. to which purpose it is, that Christ is said to be *a minister to the Circumcision* (that is, *to the circumcised*, the Jews, as Gal. 2.9.) Rom. 15.8. and (as some also would expound it, but that is questionable) *a servant to Israel*, Hos. 11.1. And this I should incline to, did not the Hebrew pause stay me, that makes a stop, between *servant*, and *Israel*. Those therefore I concur with, who read the words in two distinct clauses, thus; *Thou art my servant* (as having relation to his calling, mentioned, ver. 1. and pointing unto the office, whereunto he was called; of which branch, see Chap. 42.1.) *Israel* it is, *in whom I will be glorified*, (or, *will glorify myself*, as chap. 44.23.) by you. For it is *the true Israel, the Israel of God*, Rom. 9.6. Gal. 6.16. the body of the faithful in the salvation of whom, by Christ, God will glorify the riches of his grace. Rom. 9.23,33. and 11.23,26. Eph. 1.6,12,14. See Chap. 46.13. Nor does that late learned annotator's observation here, stay me from adhering to this version, who, with the Tigurine, would have, *whom in thee*, to be no more than, *in whom*, according to a good and useful rule given by him, that in Hebrew, when one speaks to another, the pronoun affixed, following the relative, & having reference thereunto, is not wont to be in the third person; but either in the first, if it relate to the person speaking, as ver. 23. or in the second, if it relate to the person spoken to, as here: for although it be granted so to be there, where the affix has reference to the relative, by an elegant redundancy, in that language very frequent: yet is there no necessity, of admitting either that reference, or that redundancy, in this place.

**V. 4.** *{Then I said, I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain*} Heb. *And I said*, which if it be rendered, *Then*, as Chap. 40.18. it should then be as an inference upon the former: as if he had said, *Then I make account that all my labor is lost, if it be Israel, by whom I must bring glory to thee.* I suppose, therefore, it should rather be rendered. *But I said*: for it seems to be in nature of a reply, or counterplea; in some sort returned to God's former speech of encouragement, ver. 4. complaining of the paucity, and small number of those, that his ministry had hitherto any gracious work upon, among his people. That which some conceive to be spoken of, and by Esay; others of, by Christ; and a third sort, to concern both: but the one is a lower degree, as a less perfect portraiture, and delineation of the other. See the like complaint, in the person of God's ministers, his prophets and apostles, Chapter 53.1. and of Christ, John 1.11. and 7.5. and 12.37–41.

*{in vain*} As Lev. 26.16. Job 29.16. Chap. 65.23. the word properly signifies *emptiness*; Whence *an empty vessel* Jeremiah 51.34.

*{I have spent my strength*} Or, *consumed it*; as Chap. 10.18.

*{for nought*} Of this word, see on chap. 40.17.

*{and in vain*} Heb. *for vanity*, Eccl. 1.2. not that his pains, with God's people, were wholly in vain, either in regard of God, that sent him, unto whom glory should accrue, as well by his justice manifested in the destruction of the obstinate: as by his mercy magnified in the salvation of sincere converts, 2 Cor. 2.15,16. Or, in regard of the persons, unto whom he was sent, as if not any at all of them were converted for a remnant of them still were reserved, ch. 6.9,10,13. & 8.16. or, in regard of himself, as if loss or prejudice should thereby accrue unto him. For his work was not the less, either regarded with God, or to be rewarded by God, as the words following import; but in regard of the slender effect, that his labors had hitherto found, for the benefit and behoof of those, about whom he had labored; and the welfare of their souls, which he principally therein aimed at, and did more earnestly affect. See Mat. 23.35. Mar. 3.5. Luk. 13.34. & 19.41,42. Phil. 4.1. 1 Thes. 2.19,20. and 3.8. Heb. 13.17.

*{yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God*} The adversative particle, *yet*, though it may seem wanting in the original, yet is not amiss supplied; as it is also elsewhere. Job 14.19. ch. 44.11. because in the words ensuing, as by way of recollection; for the better support, & reencouraging of himself, to persist in his employment, he opposes unto the want of the chiefly desired success of his labors with men, the gracious acceptance of them with God, (see 1 Cor. 15.58.) though the particle, *yet*, may as well be substituted in the room of the word, *surely*, which may here be omitted. Since, that albeit, sometime it signify *surely*, as being a note of asseveration, Genesis 28.26. 1 Samuel 15.32. yet it is oft rendered, *yet*, or, *but*, as in a notion of opposition, as Job 32.8. Ps. 82.7. yea, it may well include both, as the Latin *veruntamen* seems to do, by which some render it both here, and ch. 53.4.
