*{my judgment*} That is, as some, *mine office*: so is the word taken, 1 Sam. 10.25. 1 Chr. 6.32. and so it should have a respect to his vocation, to God's calling him to his office, ver. 1. as other rather, *my manner*, to wit, of carriage in my place (as the word is used, 1 Sam. 2.13. & 8.11.) is well known to God, and approved of by him. So Paul of himself, 1 Cor. 4.3–5. 2 Cor. 1.12. & 2.17. Or, it may well be rendered, *my cause*, as Job 23.4. & 34.6. God will justify me, and make it to appear, that it has not been through any default of mine, that my labors have had no better success. See Chapter 50.8.

*{my work*} Or, *my reward*; as Chap. 40.10. my wages for my work, which God will render unto me, not according to the issue, or success of my labors; but according to my pains therein taken, and the faithful discharge of my duty therein, 1 Cor. 3.8. See Joh. 17.4,5. 2 Tim. 4.7,8.

**V. 5.** *{And now saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him*} A further matter of encouragement is here adjoined, by a speech of God himself, either to the prophet, as the Jews, and some of ours, therein following them, or, as most of ours, unto Christ, related, partly, in this verse, in a promise not of sufficiency of support, and protection of him, only, in the work of his ministry, but of making him glorious in it, and by it; though it should not prove so successful among his own people, as he desired; and partly, in the verses following, wherein he shows, how his ministry should become so glorious, by the efficacy of it, among, and upon the Gentiles, far and near, throughout the whole world before mentioned, v. 1.

*{that formed me from the womb*} This some expound of Christ's human nature, framed in the womb of the virgin, Luk. 1.35. Gal. 4.4. Others, the Jews especially, of the molding of the prophet's body, to such an exact temperature and constitution, as might be fit to receive a prophetical spirit, as the like of Jeremy, Jer. 1.5. but this may well go among their cabalistical fancies. Others (whom I agree unto) understand it of a destination unto, and if you will also, a preparation of the person spoken of, for the work, that he had a purpose to employ him about. For the word of *forming*, or *framing*, is sometime found so used. See ch. 26.3. & 37.26. & 46.11. See also, cha. 43.21. & 44.21. v. 1,2.

*{to be his servant*} See v. 3.

*{to bring Jacob again to him*} To convert and reduce them back to God, that were strayed away from him, by the ministry of the word, the office principally of Christ the Arch-shepherd, Eze. 34.11–16,23,24. Mat. 18.11–13. Heb. 13.20. 1 Pet. 2.25. & 3.18. & 5.4. and of others also under him, in their several places, Ezek. 34.4–6.

*{Jacob*} The same with *Israel*, as ch. 44.1. v. 6. the Jewish people, unto whom he was in the first place sent, Mat. 15.24. Act. 3.26. See on v. 3.

*{Though Israel be not gathered*} There is a twofold reading in this place, as the like in divers other places, even in this prophecy, ch. 9.3. & 63.9. the one in the margin, the other in the text. The Jewish masters, for the most part, are wont to follow the margin; and so do the most of them here, though some admit both. Those that keep to the text, read the words in the negative; but so, that for the sense they concur, in effect with those, who admitting that in the margin as the genuine reading, take them in the affirmative, and read them, *Israel shall be gathered to him*: for either they conceive them, as uttered by way of interrogation, *and shall not Israel be gathered?* as if it were said, Shall God send his prophet, or messenger, to reduce a people; and shall they not first, or last be reduced? or they take the word of *gathering* in another sense, for *taking away*, or *destroying*, as it is oft used, ch. 4.1. & 16.10. & 57.1. & 60.20. Jer. 8.13. Zeph. 1.2. as if it were said, *and Israel shall not be taken away*, or *destroyed*. Our former translations have stuck to the text: our last version exhibits both; the one in the margin, the other in the body of the text, as they were found in the Hebrew: neither reading, as they render them, but carries with it very good probability, and fit consonance with the rest of the context; though the one only can be genuine. For to pass by all other interpretations, according to the textual reading, the words may well be thus rendered, *Though*, or *Albeit*, (as ch. 10.5.) *Israel be not gathered* (that is, reclaimed and brought home unto God, a metaphor from straying or straggling sheep, as Ps. 27.10. c. 11.12.) or, *will not be gathered*; (as some of our former versions, agreeable to Mat. 23.37.) *yet*, (Heb. *and*; as c. 42.25.) *shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord*, (God will have me in high esteem for the faithful discharge of my duty, and confer glory upon me, Joh. 5.22,23. & 10.15,17. & 12.28. & 17.1,5. Phil. 2.9.) *and my God shall be my strength*: he will enable me to go through with, whatsoever shall be required of me, in the place whereunto he has assigned me; and protect me against the might and malice, both of men & devils, of all opposites whomsoever. See of Christ, Joh. 10.15,18. and 16.32. of other his faithful ministers and messengers, Jer. 1.18,19. & 15.20,21. & 20.11. According to the marginal reading they run very aptly and smoothly thus, (to give you the whole entire passage together) *And now saith the Lord that formed me in the womb, to be his servant, for the reducing of Jacob to him, that Israel may be gathered to him, and I may be glorified in the eyes of the Lord, even my God that hath been my strength*. Who has hitherto supported me, for the verb substantive (as they term it) is in the time past, *and*, for *even*, as ch. 40.30. and the relative supplied, as ch. 44.2. a place parallel to this; either reading so well suits with the sequel of the context, that I can hardly resolve, whether of the twain to adhere to, only the speech running along throughout, in the person of the reporter, not as spoken to him by another, but speaking of himself, seems to speak for the latter. I shall only add what I since find in a learned annotator oft mentioned, who in this manner carries on the file of the context; but following the other reading with the negative, renders that passage, *to reduce to him Israel, who is not gathered*; that is, who is dispersed, and his shepherds look not after him. And this version seems also very probable, as rendering a reason, why there was great need of sending one to gather them. See Ezek. 34.4–6,11,12. Mat. 9.36. the defect of the relative, as v. 25. is frequent.

**V. 6.** *{And he said*} Following the latter reading, it would be rendered, *Even he* (of whom before, ver. 5.) *now saith*, or (as some render it) *He, I say* (the Lord my God, ver. 5.) *saith*. The Hebrew particle is oft so used, in returning after some other matter interposed, to the relation of what had been begun before, 2 Sam. 23.1. But according to the former, *He also*, or *He further said*, as ch. 8.5. & 39.6. because it should then usher in a second speech.

*{It is a light thing, that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel*} As if he had said, It is but a small matter, or too small a matter for you to reduce and restore this handful of people, though you should have as ample success with them, as you desire, in comparison of what further work I intend to effect by you; and for which, I have accordingly fitted and furnished you, Col. 1.19,20. Thus, according to the reading held forth in the text. Howbeit, the Jewish commenters, and not a few of our own interpreters also read them, as spoken by way of demand; *Is it a light matter for thee to be my servant* to this purpose? So the Jewish doctors expounding it of Esay; of whom God should demand, whether it were a slight matter to be put upon such an employment. And those of ours, that go this way; *Art thou lighter*, or *viler* (of less account, to wit, in the eyes of your people, as v. 7.) *than that thou shouldest be my servant*, an instrument used by me, for the raising and recovery of my people? But the former interpretation seems the more familiar, and not to need any such supply.

*{a light thing that thou shouldest be*} Or, *too light for thee to be*. Or, *a lighter thing than for thee to be*. Heb. *light from being*. See 1 Sam. 18.23. 1 King. 16.31. 2 Kin. 13.18. Eze. 8.17. and of the use of the particle thus in way of comparison, Job 11.6. ch. 41.24.

*{my servant*} As v. 6.

*{to raise up the tribes of Jacob*} The Jewish people fallen from me; my church among them decayed by their desertion of me; and their state ruined by their sin, Amos 9.11. Acts 15.16. This the Jewish writers, and divers of ours, also apply, some to Esay, as the foreteller of it, and some to Cyrus, as the effecter of the restitution of God's people, here pointed to, in the dissolution of the Babylonian captivity. But whatsoever dusky draught of it, might be descried in either, the full accomplishment of it is most clearly in Christ. See ch. 44.26.

*{to restore*} Heb. *to reduce*, or *bring back* or *cause to return*, as ver. 5. Neh. 9.26. for I find not where it is used of restitution, or reparation of decays in building.

*{the preserved of Israel*} Or, as some, *the reserved*: the elect of God among that people, whom God had from time to time protected and preserved in times of common calamity, as a remnant reserved for himself, Chap. 1.9. & 6.13. & 8.14. & 10.20,22. Ezek. 11.16,17. Mat. 24.21,24. Rom. 9.27,29. & 11.1,2,4,5,7. Jud. 1. Howbeit, our margin here affords us another reading, to wit, *desolations*, that which the rabbines also here hold forth, calling in, for the justification of it, divers places, where they suppose the word so to signify, as Chap. 1.8. & 65.4. Prov. 7.10. But these places, some of them, seem questionable; and though the restoring of wastes be oft mentioned, and promised in this prophecy, verse 19. Chap. 44.26. & 51.3. & 52.9. & 58.12. & 61.4. Yet neither is this word found in any of them; nor the verb here joined with it, used of them. Besides, that the gender of the word carry it rather unto persons, than unto places;

*{I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth*} This likewise not the Jews alone, but of ours also apply, some to Esay; from whose prophecies much light shone forth, not to the Jews alone, but to other people, when they saw them fulfilled, and were many of them, as they presume, thereby converted: some to Cyrus, by whose dissolution of the Babylonian Empire, much light of joy, accrued not to the Jews alone (as by Haman's downfall, Est. 8.16,17.) Psal. 126.1,2. ch. 9.2,3. & 12.3,6. & 35.10. but to all those people, that lived formerly, either in slavery, or in slavish fear, under it, chap. 7.16. But these things seem too much strained. Evident it is, that Christ was sent by God, to enlighten, by the saving light of the gospel, not those of his own nation alone, Chap. 9.2. Mat. 4.15,16. Luke 1.78,79. John 1.4,5. & 8.12. & 9.5. & 12.35,36,46. but people of all parts throughout the whole world, Chap. 42.6. & 51.4. Luk. 2.32. Acts 13.47. & 22.21. & 26.17,18. Rom. 10.18. 2 Cor. 4.4,6. & to effect salvation, as well for the one as the other, Ps. 98.3. chap. 45.22. Mark 16.15,16. Luke 24.47. John 10.16. & 11.51,52. & 12.32. Rom. 3.9,23–25,29,30. & 10.12,13. Gal. 3.28. Eph. 2.13–16. 1 John 2.2.

**V. 7.** *{Thus saith the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, and his holy one*} Another speech of God, unto his anointed one, follows; to give him further encouragement, against that sorry conceit, and mean estimation, that the world should have of him, with a more ample assurance of good success in his ministry, and an issue, beyond expectation, of the work to be undertaken by him, for the deliverance of his people.

*{the Redeemer of Israel, and his holy one*} See Chapter 48.17.

*{to him, whom man despiseth; to him, whom the nation abhorreth; to a servant of rulers*} A lively description of the condition of our blessed Savior in the time of his humiliation, in the days of his flesh. See the like, chap. 52.14. & 53.2,3. Howsoever the Hebrew commenters would turn it all another way, applying it all, some of them, to the prophet Esay, and some to the body of their people.

*{to him, whom man despiseth*} Heb. *to the contempt of soul*; as some, that make the word a noun: or, as others, supposing it to be a verb, *to him who is ready, for a soul to contemn*: or, as a third sort, who take it for a participle of a passive sense, *to the despised of a soul*. Herein they all agree, that by the word *soul*, is understood *man*, or *person*, as it is frequently used in either Testament, Exod. 1.5. Acts 7.14. 1 Pet. 3.20. and in a kind of generality here, *soul*, or, *a soul*, for *every one*, every *soul*, as Lev. 4.1. & 5.1. though the note of universality be not expressed. So the meaning is, one that is generally exposed to contempt, as our blessed Savior was here on earth, in the eyes and minds of the most, Psal. 22.6,7. chap. 52.14. & 53.3. Mat. 13.55,57. Mar. 6.3. John 7.48,49. Our margin renders it, *To him that is despised in soul*, that is, as some, to a contemptible creature, one whose *soul* is filled, or cloyed *with scorn and contempt*, Psalm 123.3,4. expounding it of the Jewish people, under the Babylonian bondage, Psalm 137.1,3. And thus it was indeed also both with Christ himself, when he was here on earth, Mat. 27.38–44. Mar. 15.28. and with his members and ministers after him, 1 Cor. 4.9–13. Again, some other render it, *to him that setteth light by his own soul*; as all true Christians are both admonished to do, Mat. 16.24,25. Luke 14.26. and are, said some of them to have done, Rev. 12.11. See Acts 20.24. applying it to our prophet, who exposed himself to hazard, by his freedom of speech, in opposing of Shebna, and other the great ones of the times. That which is true, also, of Christ, who exposed, and gave up his life, or soul, unto death, as an expiatory sacrifice for the sins and safety of God's people, Chap. 53.10,12. John 10.15,18. But the sense first given seems genuine, which way soever the grammar resolution, there given, go. Howbeit, a late learned annotator propounds here two other interpretations. The word, says he, is a verb infinite, which with the particle here prefixed, oft answers the Latin gerund in *dum*, as Chap. 44.14. and upon this ground he renders the text, either thus; *thy soul must be despised*, or, *set light by, for him*, or *those* (collectively taking it) *whom people abhor*, (a defect of the relative, as chap. 65.1.) *and is*, or *are, in servitude to rulers*. Or, thus, *thou must contemn*, or, *set light by, the will*, or *desire*, (so is the word *soul* used, Psalm 27.12.) *of him that abhorreth the nation, and is a servant to rulers*, that is, of Pilate, who abhorred the Jewish people, and was a servant to the Cesars. I propound them only, and leave them, as himself does, to be weighed by others.

*{to him whom the nation abhorred*} Heb. no more than, *to an abhorring nation*; which some render, *to an abominable nation*, that is, a people, say they, who in regard of their present, base, and calamitous condition, are generally abominated, Lam. 1.17. But others, and so the Jewish commenters, also, *to one abhorring a nation*; that is, who abhors the nation, either of the Jews for their wickedness; or other, for their impieties and wrongs to God's people: or, as they also, *to one, whom the nation is abhorring*, that is, whom this nation, the Jewish people, (the rather so termed, as some observe on the place, because by their wicked practices, they had made themselves no other than as other nations, and such also in God's sight, Ezek. 5.6. Hos. 1.9. See chap. 1.4.) do for the most of them even abhor. See Chapter 53.3. Matthew 11.19. and 26.65. John 5.12,18. and 7.13,20. and 8.28,52. and 10.20. Act. 3.14. The defect of the relative is not unusual. See on v. 5. nor the placing of the nominative after the verb, or participle commonly used for the verb. So Gen. 25.21. Of which place, see on ch. 21.8.

*{to a servant of rulers*} This some understand of Esay, being a subject, and so a servant to the kings of Judah, under whom he prophesied, ch. 1.1. Others of the Jewish people, in servitude under foreign governors, during the time of their captivity, ch. 26.13. But the most, and best, of Christ, used in a base sort, and in a servile manner, by the rulers in those times, when he was here upon earth, and put, by them, to such a death, as slaves among the Romans were wont to undergo, Matthew 26.27. and 27.20,22,26–38. Luke 22.63–65. and 23.11,23. John 19.1,2,5.

*{Kings shall see, and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the Lord, who is faithful, and the holy one of Israel, and he shall choose thee*} You that were sometime contemned, and scorned, both by princes, and people, shall through the faithful procurement of God, who made choice of you for this office, be advanced to that height of honor, that you shall be worshipped, and adored by the greatest potentates in the world, Eph. 1.19–21. Phil. 2.7–11. Heb. 2.9. A pregnant prophecy of the kings and princes of the earth, submitting their crowns and scepters, to the kingdom, and sovereignty of Christ, Ps. 2.8–12. & 72.10,11. & 110.3,5. Chap. 52.13,15. Rev. 11.15. Though some expound it of this prophet also, at the reading of whose prophecies, Cyrus should stand amazed: and other princes admire, when they should see them fulfilled. Others, of the church restored by Christ, of which somewhat the like, see hereafter, v. 23. Ch. 60.3,10,11,12. for she partakes also in some degree with Christ, as his spouse, in his honor, Mat. 19.18. Luk. 22.29,30. Rev. 3.21. & 12.1. & 19.7,8. but this place is principally concerning Christ himself.

*{See*} Or, *See thee*; the pronoun wanting: as v. 18. They see him, with the eye of faith, as Abraham foresaw him, Joh. 8.56. and behold the glory and dignity of Christ, now exalted, in the marvelous works, wrought by him, upon, and among his people, cha. 52.15.

*{and arise*} Or, *arise to thee*, as before: in token of reverence, as Levit. 19.32. Judg. 3.20. 2 King. 2.19. Job 29.8.

*{shall worship*} Or, *shall arise, and bow down*: as verse 22. (see Genesis 23.7. 1 Samuel 25.42.) or, *do obeisance, to thee*; in token of submission, Chap. 45.23. Phil. 2.10. ch. 60.14. Rev. 3.7. a repetition of the former verb, from the former branch: as cha. 41.25. & 43.2. and supply of the pronoun attending the latter, as ch. 58.9.

*{because of the Lord, who is faithful*} Considering God's faithfulness, which shall then appear in the performance of all his promises, made both unto you, and unto his people, by you, Rom. 15.8,9. 2 Cor. 1.20.

*{and the holy One*} Or, *for the holy one*: the preposition repeated from the former branch; as the verb before; *the holy one*, that speaks this. See before.

*{and he shall choose thee*} Or, *shall make thee a choice one*: as ch. 48.10. Zach. 1.17. or, *who hath chosen thee*: the copulative for the relative; as Chapter 44.14. Jeremiah 14.18. or, *because he shall have chosen thee*: the copulative, in a causative notion, as chapter 64.5. because he shall make it then to appear that it was he that had formerly made choice of you, and designed you unto this office, to be the Savior of his people as well Jew, as Gentile. See ch. 43.19.

**V. 8.** *{Thus saith the Lord*} God the Father speaking again unto Christ, as Psalm 2.7. and 110.1. For they strain the text unreasonably, that either restrain, or apply, all this, also, to Esay.

*{In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee*} Or, because it runs as the former did, ver. 6,7. *I will hear thee, I will help thee*: when the time appointed shall come, wherein I have determined to manifest my free favor, and gracious goodwill unto them, by working by you salvation and deliverance for them, I will then accept your suits, and intercession for them, and will be assistant unto you, in that work. See 2 Cor. 6.2.

*{an acceptable time*} Heb. *a time of goodwill*, or *acceptance*, as Psal. 69.13. See Chapter 61.2.

*{heard*} Or, *will hear*. Heb. *answer*. God is then said, as *to hear*, so *to answer*, when he grants requests, and makes it appear, that he so does, chap. 65.24. Psal. 118.5. See his solemn suit for his, John 17.

*{helped*} Or, *will help*: as Christ is with his at hand, always, to hear, and help them, Mat. 28.20. so was God the Father, ever at hand with Christ, to hear, & help him. See Joh. 11.41,42. & 16.32. Act. 10.38. 2 Cor. 5.19. See the like promises made to God's people, ch. 41.10,13,14.

*{and I will preserve thee*} Both in your person, and in the execution of your office. See ch. 42.1,6. ver. 2.

*{and give thee for a covenant to the people*} Not only make you the Mediator of the new covenant between me and my people, Heb. 7.22. & 8.6. but make good by you, all my promises made to my people, concerning their deliverance, either corporal, out of the Babylonian bondage; or spiritual, from the service of sin, and Satan, 2 Cor. 1.20. the one, being as a type and symbol; so a pledge, or pawn, also, in some sort, of the other: and the latter therefore, being usually shadowed out by the former, as well in this place, as elsewhere. See ch. 61.1,2.

*{to establish the earth*} Or, *to raise up* (as verse 6.) *the land*: as Chapter 57.13. to wit, of Judah, to restore, and settle the state of it again, after their return from the captivity: a type of the restitution, and establishment of the church by Christ, chap. 2.2.

*{to cause to inherit the desolate heritages*} That my people returning again to their possessions, out of which they had formerly been ejected, may repair, and reedify those places that had lain waste a long time, during the time of their absence from them; and being repossessed of them, enjoy them, as in former days they had done, ver. 6. ch. 51.3. & 58.12. & 61.4. Ezek. 36.3,4,34,35. a type of the restitution of the faithful; to their estate, and condition, forfeited through the fraud of Satan, and the default and defection, both of their parents, and themselves, Romans 3:23 & 5:12.

**V. 9.** *{That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that sit in darkness, Show yourselves*} That you may not only say it; but do it. For God's word is his will, and his will, is his work, Psalm 115:3 & 135:6, chapter 44:26, that you may not only proclaim, or preach, liberty to them; but procure it for them; liberty corporal, from Babel's bonds. Ezra 1:1–4, chapter 43:14 & 44:28 & 45:13 & 51:14, Psalm 107:10–14, liberty spiritual, from Satan's bonds, Luke 13:16, John 8:31,32,34, Acts 26:18, Colossians 1:13, 2 Timothy 2:26, Hebrews 2:14,15, 1 John 3:8. See chapter 42:7 & 61:1.

*{in darkness*} In *dark* dungeons, Psalm 88:6 & 107:10,14, chapter 42:7,22, a type of spiritual darkness, chapter 9:2, Matthew 4:16, Luke 1:79 & 22:53.

*{Show yourselves*} Hebrew, *Be revealed:* as 1 Samuel 14:8,11, come forth into the light.

*{They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places*} To the promise of delivery from their captivity, is adjoined a further promise of a competent supply, and provision of all necessaries for them by the way, in their traveling home to their own country, set forth in an allusion to the manner of sheep (and God's people are styled his sheep, Psalm 100:3, chapter 40:11, Ezekiel 34:31.) or other cattle, that being removed (as in Spain, and some other parts) at time of year, from one side of the country, to the other, are permitted by the way, to graze on the roads, and drift-walls, that they pass by; together with an intimation of sufficiency of food, that should, by God's procurement and providence, be found for them, even in the places most waste and barren, by which they were to pass. See chapter 35:1 and 41:18,19 and 43:19,20.

*{high places*} That are usually dry and barren, chapter 41:18, Jeremiah 12:12, albeit, a learned late writer would have it signify, not *high,* but *low* places, *valleys,* or *plans.* See chapter 13:1 & 41:18.

**V. 10.** *{They shall not hunger, nor thirst*} Having provision sufficient, of either sort, made for them, as those that travel through deserts, are compelled oft to do, Psalm 107:4,5. See Psalm 105:40,41, chapter 41:17 & 48:21, Revelation 7:16.

*{neither shall heat, nor the sun, smite them*} They shall not be troubled with such inconveniences, and annoyances, as travelers, in torrid regions, waste places especially, where no shade, or shelter is, are wont to be exposed unto, and molested with, Psalm 105:37,39, chapter 32:2 & 41:19.

*{heat, nor sun*} Hebrew, *burning,* or *scorching heat, and sun,* for, *burning,* or *scorching heat of the sun.* See chapter 5:6. Or, *scorching heat* (arising from the nature of the soil; as chapter 35:7, or other like occasions,) *or sun,* that is, sunshine: because they are also, so distinctly set down, Revelation 7:16, though the sun put first here; the copulative for the disjunctive; as chapter 44:10,14.

*{smite*} As Psalm 121:6.

*{for he that hath mercy on them, shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them*} The reason of this affluence of necessaries for them, in their way homeward; because the same God, who out of his mere mercy, had wrought their deliverance from Babylon, chapter 14:1, will go along with them, and conduct them, as he did their fathers formerly, through the wilderness, after he had brought them out of Egypt, Exodus 13:21,22, and will see that nothing be wanting unto them by the way: and because water is one of the most necessary supports of man's life, and means of his refreshment, the want whereof, whereof, unto travelers especially in hot regions, and through waste places, might most of all distress; mention is particularly made of provision for it, God promising to lead them along by such passages, where plenty of springs should be found. See chapter 41:18,19 & 43:19,20, Psalm 23:1–3, Jeremiah 31:9.

*{Springs*} As chapter 35:7.

**V. 11.** *{And I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted*} Another means of facilitating their journey for them, by making their way safe and even before them, and by removal of such impediments as might hinder them in their passage. See chapter 40:4 & 51:10.

*{I will*} A change of the person; as oft elsewhere. So chapter 41:19,20 & 42:13,14.

*{my mountains*} Those by which my people are to pass, chapter 40:4. Or, therefore, *mine,* because I am the maker of them, and can, therefore, dispose of them as I please, Psalm 95:4. See Zechariah 4:6,7. I will cause them to pass with as much ease, as if all the mountains were taken away, that stand in their way.

*{my highway shall be exalted*} Or, *my causey* (that is, such ways as shall be cast up for the more convenient passage of my people) *shall be heightened.* See chapter 35:8 & 62:10. Of the word, see chapter 19:23. Howbeit, some expound the words, *I will make my mountains a plain way,* by depressing them, *and my highways,* or roads, in the valley, *shall be raised,* to make them even with the other, and so lay all level, as chapter 40:4.

**V. 12.** *{Behold these shall come from far:*} To assure them of return to their own country again, he tells them, that no remoteness of place from their own land; nor distance of regions one from another, into which they had been dispersed, should impeach their passage, or hinder their concurrence and meeting together, in their own land again, Deuteronomy 30:3,4. See chapter 11:11,12.

*{from far*} From places most remote, chapter 43:6 & 60:4, Jeremiah 30:10. Howbeit, in regard that some special regions are in particular after related, lying towards the four quarters of the world, and the western coast, next but one to this, most interpreters here, by the *far country,* understand the east, or sunrising, the Persian land, chapter 41:2,25, as most distant from the land of Judah, that lay so far west, on the brink of the western sea.

*{and lo these from the north*} From Media, say some, chapter 41:25. From Babylon, rather, others, chapter 14:31, Jeremiah 1:14,15, for it is not probable, that the principal place of their captivity should be omitted. See Zechariah 2:6,7.

*{and from the west*} Hebrew, *from the sea,* as Joshua 16:6,8, so called, because the Midland sea lay west of them; that is, as some, from the Philistines' land, into which they had sometime fled. See chapter 9:12, as others, from the transmarine parts and western islands, Cyprus, Candy, Macedonia.

*{and these from the land of Sini*} Or, *of the Sinites;* whereby some understand such as lived in the desert of *Sin,* or about Mount *Sinai,* Exodus 16:1 & 19:1. But there seems to have been little dwelling in those deserts. Others, the *Sinites,* reckoned among the posterity of Canaan, Genesis 10:17. But these were, in likelihood, families, inhabiting among the rest of that stock in the land, where the Israelites themselves were afterward seated. Others, would carry them, as far as *China,* by Ptolomy, called *Sina:* But that country was not in those times, yet, in likelihood, known to these parts. The most probable opinion, therefore, is, that by the *Sinites* is here meant, the inhabitants of *Sin,* a chief city of Egypt, called, therefore, *Sin, the strength of Egypt,* Ezekiel 30:15,16, having its name *Sin,* from a Syriac word, that signifies, *mire,* or *dirt;* as by the Greeks also, it is therefore termed *Pelusium,* from a Greek word of the same notion, in regard of its situation, being environed with marshes and quaggy grounds; as Strabo, l. 17, put here for Egypt, because one of its head cities; which land, lying to the south of Judah, chapter 30:6, comes in to make up the fourth quarter. The return of the Jewish people, out of all these parts, into which they had been scattered, Ezekiel 5:10, being a type of those, that out of all parts of the world, should be converted, and come in unto Christ, Psalm 107:3, verse 18, chapter 43:5,6 & 66:19,20.

**V. 13.** *{Sing, O heavens, and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into crying, O mountains*} A calling upon all the creatures, both above, and below, to rejoice, upon the deliverance of God's people, chapter 44:23 & 55:12, as the whole frame of the creature is said to droop and mourn, until their deliverance be fully completed, Romans 8:19–22.

*{for the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted*} Or, *and had mercy,* chapter 14:1, verse 10, chapter 51:3 and 52:9.

**V. 14.** *{But Zion said, The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me*} Or, *Jehovah hath forsaken me; and Adonai,* or *my Lord, hath forgotten me;* as two distinct expressions of the same person, which at several times they had frequently in their mouths, the one, sometimes; and sometime the other. The laments of God's people bemoaning themselves, in the time of their long and tedious captivity, and complaining of God, through human frailty, as if he had utterly cast off all care for, and thought of them. See the like, chapter 40:27, Psalm 13:1 & 31:22 & 88:14.

*{Zion*} God's people, verse 13, who had wont to meet together at Zion, to serve God there, Psalm 84:7. So chapter 1:27 and 40:9.

*{my Lord*} That was in times past, so: my good Lord, my gracious sovereign, so forward to protect me, so ready to relieve me; whom, alone, I had wont to repair unto, and rely upon, for succor and shelter, for safety and delivery in all my distresses; he now fails me, and looks not after me; that which much aggravated their present affliction, and added much aloes thereunto, Psalm 44:9.

**V. 15.** *{Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?*} God's affectionate answer to his people's lamentable, but erroneous, and groundless, complaint.

*{Can a woman forget?*} Hebrew, *Will a woman forget?* But these enunciatives are oft used in a potential notion. So Jeremiah 2:32 & 11:12.

*{her sucking child*} That hangs on her breast. Such as mothers are wont to be most chary of, and to be most tenderly affected towards them. Or, *her young child, her youngling:* For the word seems to be somewhat larger, and to signify any young infant, or child, like a tender *branch,* or *cluster,* as the words of near affinity to it import, chapter 13:16 & 24:12, distinguished from *sucklings,* Psalm 8:2, Jeremiah 6:11. See the word itself used, chapter 65:20, Job 19:18 & 21:11, which latter places cannot well be understood of sucking babes. See chapter 40:11. A learned annotator observes, that the same word in the Ethiopic version, is used for a colt, Matthew 21:2.

*{that she should not have compassion*} Hebrew, *from having compassion,* as chapter 23:1 & 50:2 & 59:1.

*{on the son of her womb*} Hebrew, *of her belly,* an affectionate form of speech, Proverbs 31:2, and emphatical, Micah 6:7, used as well of the male, as of the female parent, Deuteronomy 28:4,18, Psalm 132:11, not unlike that, *my son which came out of my bowels,* 2 Samuel 16:11.

*{yea they may forget, yet will I not forget thee*} Though some of them should be so unnatural, Lamentations 4:3, Romans 1:31, yet I cannot prove so towards you, Psalm 103:13.

*{yea*} Or, *though,* as Nehemiah 6:1.

*{they*} Hebrew, *these;* as verse 11,21.

*{may forget*} Hebrew, *will forget,* to wit, her sucking babe, or her youngling, as the ostrich does, Job 39:14–16. But the word is taken here potentially; as chapter 39:15.

*{yet*} Hebrew, *and:* as chapter 42:25.

*{will not I forget thee*} Chapter 44:21, Jeremiah 31:20. Or, *cannot I forget thee;* that it may answer the foregoing member.

**V. 16.** *{Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands*} Or, *I have drawn thee* (portrayed you, as Ezekiel 4:1.) *on my hands,* as Psalm 119:48, Lamentations 3:41, an allusion, as some, to the manner of those, that set some mark, or tie some string upon their hand, or about some of their fingers, to mind them of some business, that they may not forget it. See Exodus 13:16, Proverbs 6:21. Or, as others, to the manner of builders, that use to draw models, of those structures, that they intend to erect, which suits well with the walls mentioned in the next clause. Or, as others again, pressing the word, *graven,* (though not indeed found there) to those, that carry about with them engraven, on some tablet, or on the stone of some ring, which they wear on their finger, the mark, name, or picture, of some person, whom they entirely affect. See Canticles 8:6, Jeremiah 22:24, whereunto some add as a probable conjecture; that the Jews, the citizens of Jerusalem especially, should usually have the figure of that city engraven on their rings; and that thereunto some allusion should be, Psalm 137:5. Of some of their coins, some such thing is reported and exhibited: of their rings, I read nothing: a defect of the pronoun possessive; as Job 13:18.

*{thy walls are continually before me*} Either my eyes are continually upon your walls now demolished and ruined. Lamentations 2:7,8, a rueful spectacle, to move me, out of pity and compassion, to be mindful of the raising and re-edifying of them, Psalm 102:14. Or, the model and frame of that goodly structure, that I intend to raise Sion unto (for he speaks of church, and people, as of a stately structure, chapter 55:11,12, Revelation 21:10–26) is continually in my thoughts, as the workman has his model, or pattern, constantly, either before his eye, or in his brain, that he is for to work by. See Exodus 25:9, Psalm 39:16, Ezekiel 40:2 & 43:11.

**V. 17.** *{Thy children shall make haste*} They shall speedily return, chapter 51:14, Jeremiah 50:8. Or, as some read it, *thy builders shall make haste:* Your walls shall be speedily built up again, chapter 44:28 and 60:10.

*{and they that made thee waste, shall go forth of thee*} They that razed your walls, and laid you waste, shall be expelled, and driven again out of your land, whereof they had formerly dispossessed you, verse 19, chapter 14:2,6 & 16:4 & 54:14 & 60:18, Zechariah 1:21.

**V. 18.** *{Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold; all these gather themselves together, and come to thee*} God speaks to Sion, by the prophet, following the former allegory; as to a mother or mother-city; and as of a present visible confluence of multitudes of people, from all parts on every side, flowing in to her; partly of her own natives; and partly, of others joined to them, and desirous to be enfranchised with them: a type of those numerous, or numberless rather numbers of persons, that should be brought home to the church of God, under Christ, by the ministry of the gospel; and have their names enrolled in God's register, as fellow citizens, with the saints, chapter 2:2,3 & 14:1 & 60:11, Psalm 87:4–6, Hosea 1:10, Acts 2:41,47 & 4:4 & 19:18–20 & 21:20, Romans 9:24,25, Ephesians 2:12,13,19, Revelation 3:12. See chapter 60:4.

*{Lift up thine eyes*} An ordinary form of speech used in Scripture, to express a serious and advised consideration, or contemplation of aught that offers itself unto view, Genesis 13:10 & 22:4 & 31:10,12.

*{gather themselves together*} Hebrew, *are gathered together:* chapter 43:9, out of several parts and places, wherein formerly they abode.

*{and come to thee*} Or, *they come to thee;* or *to come to thee:* as Judges 9:48, *make haste, do as I do,* for *make haste to do, as I do;* and so Psalm 106:13, *they made haste, they forgat;* and the like.

*{as I live, saith the Lord*} A solemn form of an oath; that God himself, upon special occasions, oft uses: as sure as I live, Ezekiel 33:11, Jeremiah 22:24.

*{thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them to thee, as a bride doth*} They shall all join themselves to you; and being joined to you, shall not be a bare burdensome multitude, hanging upon you; or as ignominious troops of base sorry people, that are no better than blots, and blemishes to a state; but they are such, as shall be as jewels, and ornaments, matter of much honor, to you, being persons endowed with such spiritual graces, as shall make them, and you by them, through those precious endowments, resplendent in them, of high esteem, in the eyes both of God, and man, 1 Corinthians 12:411, Titus 2:10, James 2:5, 1 Peter 1:7 & 3:4, 2 Peter 1:1,4, Revelation 19:8,14.

*{thou shalt surely*} So the particle seems used, chapter 5:7 & 7:9,16. Or, *that thou shalt,* etc. As sure as *I live,* so sure it is, *that thou shalt.* So 1 Samuel 20:3.

*{clothe thee with them*} Hebrew, *clothe them on,* or *put them on:* as Exodus 29:30, as one is said to be *clad,* or *clothed* with that, which makes him conspicuous in the eyes and esteem of others, Psalm 93:1 & 104:2 & 132:9,16, Romans 13:12,14, Ephesians 4:24, Colossians 3:10,12,14.

*{as with an ornament*} The word is a very general term, comprehending all rich, and gorgeous raiment, or other ornaments, that people are wont to wear about them, Exodus 33:4–6.

*{bind them to thee*} Or, *bind them on:* as jewels are wont to be for more security, Proverbs 3:3 and 7:3, it seems used more specially of head-attire, the *head-band,* or *diadem,* Jeremiah 2:32. The pronoun is not in the text: but may be supplied; as verse 7, Job 11:18.

*{as a bride doth*} As a bride is wont, of all other, in most specious and curious manner, to attire, and set out herself, chapter 61:10, Jeremiah 2:32, Revelation 21:2, *as a bride bindeth on* her ornaments, or her head-attire, which she has special care of: the verb is to be supplied, from the member before-going, as Proverbs 25:23 and 26:9,14.

**V. 19.** *{For thy waste, and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow, by reason of the inhabitants*} Or, carrying on the text in a continued tenor, (which I take to be the right,) *That thy waste, and desolate places, and thy land destroyed, shall be too strait for the inhabitant:* For so it runs word for word; as certain, as I said before, it is, that your land, formerly exhausted with destructions, and deportations, shall now be so replenished with people, that there shall hardly be room for them, to dwell one by another. See Jeremiah 31:27, Ezekiel 36:37,38, Zechariah 2:4. Or, as a learned late writer, *For in thy desolate places, and in thy wastes, and in thy land destroyed, thou shalt now surely be straitened, by reason of inhabitants:* a double *ci,* in a twofold notion, as Genesis 23:16, and a defect of the particle, *in,* very frequent; as chapter 44:12 & 48:4. And this I concur with; adding only, that according to this interpretation, the tenor of the context, may run on as before, *That in all those places thou shalt be straitened.* See verse 20.

*{thy waste, and thy desolate places*} Hebrew, *thy wastenesses, and thy desolations:* as Ezra 9:9.

*{the land of thy destruction*} Or, rather, *thy land of destruction;* that is, your destroyed land, verse 17.

*{by reason of the inhabitants*} Hebrew, *inhabitant:* as chapter 5:3.

*{and they that swallowed thee up, shall be far away*} To wit, from you: a supply of the pronoun: as verse 18. Being either driven away, or destroyed. See chapter 19:18.

*{swallowed thee up*} Or, *destroyed thee,* that wasted and spoiled you, your lands, cities and people, chapter 3:12 & 19:3 & 25:7, Jeremiah 51:34,44, a metaphor from such ravenous beasts, as devour, what they destroy, Genesis 37:33, Psalm 124:3, Jonah 1:17, chapter 42:14.

**V. 20.** *{The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me; give place to me, that I may dwell*} The great fruitfulness of the people, returned from captivity: not unlike that, wherewith God blessed them, sometime, in Egypt; Exodus 1:12,20, a type of the fertility of God's church, under the Messiah, chapter 54:1.

*{after thou hast lost the other*} Either cut off by the enemy, Jeremiah 31:15, or cast off, for their incredulity, Romans 11:15,20, which these latter shall, in number, far exceed, Revelation 7:4–9. Hebrew, *the children of thine orbity,* or *thy childless,* or *destitute, estate.* See chapter 47:9 & verse 21.

*{shall say again*} Or, *yet,* or *further.*

*{in thine ears*} Or, *in thy hearing;* as Jeremiah 48:7.

*{the place is too strait for me*} As 2 Kings 6:1, we want room, Zechariah 10:10.

*{give place for me, that I may dwell*} Or, *make room for me, that I may have where to abide;* as chapter 5:8, Jeremiah 39:14. See chapter 54:1.

**V. 21.** *{Then shalt thou say in thine heart*} Hebrew, *and:* as chapter 38:2,4, *thou shalt think with thyself;* as 1 Samuel 27:1, Psalm 14:1.

*{Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing, to and fro? and who hath brought up these? behold, I was left alone: these where had they been?*} A speech, or thought, of much wonder, upon the sight of her exceeding great, and that sudden, also, increase, with her, after her return: having been so long a time, like a lone woman, and lost so many of her children, partly, in the siege, and surprisal of the city, (for as of Sion, or Jerusalem, verse 14, he still speaks,) before the captivity; and partly, during the time of their abode therein. See chapter 66:7,8.

*{I have lost my children*} Hebrew, *I am childless;* or *have been stripped of my children:* for the word signifies *childless,* yet not at large: not so, as Mical, 2 Samuel 6:23, one that never had child; but more strictly, such an one, as has had children, but has miscarried with them, either, by abortion, before birth, Canticles 4:2 & 6:6, Hosea 9:14, or, by loss of them, afterward, 2 Samuel 17:8, Hosea 13:8.

*{and desolate*} So is the word used, in the male form, Job 15:34 & 30:3, here, in the female, it is put for a *lone* woman, (as we speak) or, *a widow,* as appears by those parallel places, where the judgments, here mentioned, are (as here) joined together, chapter 47:8,9, Jeremiah 18:21, seeing I have been a long time husbandless, not one, that never had any, (for God had been married to her, Jeremiah 3:14 & 31:32, Ezekiel 16:8.) but as one that lives severed, and divorced from her husband, as she seemed to do, during the time, of her captivity, and the intermission of her wonted solemn communion with God, in his temple ordinances, wholly for that whole time abandoned, together with the only place, thereunto appropriated, chapter 50:1. See Lamentations 1:1.

*{removing to and fro*} A *pilgrim,* or, *a vagrant;* one that goes aside, and flits from place to place; so the stock it comes from, gives it. Howbeit, not such an one here, as roves to and fro, of his own accord, like Cain, whom none, save his own guilty conscience, drove up and down, Genesis 4:14, but such an one, as is hurried from quarter to quarter, at the pleasure of those, in whose power, he, or she is; and can find rest in no place; (see Lamentations 1:3.) a just fruit of their willful wandering from God, Jeremiah 14:10. The word in this notion, is not elsewhere read; in another it is, Jeremiah 2:21, and in a third, most proper, Jeremiah 17:13.

*{brought them up*} To growth, see chapter 1:2.

*{left alone*} Lamentations 1:1.

*{these where had they been*} Or, *where were they,* or, have they been, all this while? and from whence now come they? Hebrew, *these where they;* that is, where were these? the pronoun, for the verb substantive: as Ecclesiastes 1:10, chapter 50:1.

**V. 22.** *{Thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I will lift up my hand to the Gentiles; and set up my standard to the people*} Because it might be demanded, by what means such multitudes should be brought together, and brought home, the dispersed ones of God's people, being scattered, and severed, so far asunder one from another, and by reason of their low and bare condition, destitute of all necessary means of conveyance; God tells them therefore here, that he himself would take a course for the due, and full effecting hereof: for he would, by a secret instinct, work so upon the hearts of people in all places, where any of his were, that they should not only help to bring them together, but accommodate them, also, so sufficiently, with all necessaries for their journey, that it should be with as much ease performed by them, as if they were brought home in the arms, or on the shoulders, of others, Psalm 147:2, chapter 11:11.

*{Lift up my hands to the Gentiles*} As men use to do to those, whom they call to them, or speak unto, for the doing of aught, that they desire to have done by them, chapter 13:2.

*{set up my standard*} See chapter 11:12 & 66:19.

*{and they shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders*} Or, *they shall bring thy sons in arms;* (Hebrew, as some, *bosom:* so it is rendered, Psalm 129:7, as others *lap,* Nehemiah 5:13, see chapter 40:11, *arm,* may well be retained, the rather, because little ones are wont to be so carried, Psalm 91:11, though a learned late writer, would rather have it in the plural, *arms;* not only because the term is here collectively taken, but because it signifies, properly, as he supposes, the *folding* of both arms together, *to embrace* aught, as the Ethiopic version uses it, Mark 9:36 & 10:16, Luke 2:28.) *and thy daughters shall be brought on shoulders:* with as much ease either, and with as much conveniency, as if carried in arms, or borne on shoulders; for the pronoun is in neither branch: yet may not amiss be supplied here, as it is, chapter 41:31, and may be, chapter 43:14. See the like notion in a diverse expression, chapter 66:20.

**V. 23.** *{And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and queens thy nursing mothers*} Fulfilled in those Persian potentates, Cyrus, Artaxerxes, Darius, Assuerus; with the queens also of some of them, that patronized, and protected God's people, and promoted God's work with them, Ezra 1:1–4 & 6:3–12 & 7:12,26, Nehemiah 2:6–8, Esther 8:3–8, and much more in other emperors and kings, together with their queens, as Constantine, Theodosius, and the like, who both embraced the Christian faith themselves, and maintained the profession of it. Of some whereof, see Revelation 17:12,16,17. Yet some would have it understood of Nebuchadnezzar, and his issue, under whom God's people were preserved, though not in so full liberty, Jeremiah 29:5–7, yea, divers of them liberally provided for at the royal charge, Daniel 1:3–5, and some of them advanced to places of honor, Daniel 2:48,49, and so it should be as an answer to the question, where her children had been bred, and brought up, and by whom, verse 21. And some again, would have it to imply no more, than that her children should be daintily fed and brought up, as kings and great men's children are wont to be, Genesis 49:20, Matthew 11:8, but neither of these seems to fit so well as the first, with the scope and tenor of the context. See chapter 60:6,7,16.

*{nursing fathers*} Or, *nourishers:* such as have the charge of educating great men's children, 2 Kings 10:1.

*{Queens*} Hebrew, *Princesses, Saraes,* they shall be to your children as Sarah was to Isaac, Genesis 21:7. *nursing mothers.* Hebrew, *nurses,* such as give children milk, Exodus 2:7, and so the word signifies.

*{they shall bow down to thee with their face to the earth*} Hebrew, *faces of the earth,* or, *to the earth shall bow down to thee;* which syntax; because it is not so usual, some would thus render the text; *the faces of the earth* (the entire put for the contract, as Jeremiah 10:10.) *shall bow down to thee;* that is, say they, *the honorable,* or great men of the *earth,* shall do obeisance to you: To which purpose they allege *a portion of faces,* for an *honorable portion,* as 1 Samuel 1:5, but that place is not so clear, and the phrase very frequent; though such as requires some supply here, as it does also elsewhere, carries it rather the plainer and ordinary way, *with face,* or *faces,* (for the word, though dual, because the face has two sides, the right, and the left, yet is used of any one also alone, as Genesis 19:1.) Or, *with their face,* or *faces* (for there is a want both of the preposition, and of the pronoun also, as here: So Genesis 42:6, 1 Samuel 24:8 & 28:14, 2 Chronicles 7:3, though the latter expressed, Genesis 48:12, 2 Samuel 24:20, and the former, *on,* or *upon the face,* Numbers 22:31, 1 Kings 1:23.) *to the earth,* or *to the ground:* the noun for the adverb, found fully and expressly in most of the places before recited, and 1 Samuel 20:41, 2 Samuel 14:4 & 18:28. This is, by some, supposed to be meant of such princes, of Moab, and Edom, as were in the time of the Jews' restored estate, after their return from captivity, by force of arms subdued unto them. Others, of such Christian kings and princes, as entertaining the faith of Christ, submitted themselves unto the scepter of Christ, and to his ordinances settled in the Christian church. It is an allusion to that ordinary expression of submission and reverence, usually practiced of old in those parts; as by the places above pointed to, may appear. See verse 7, Revelation 3:9, and it may have allusion to Pharao, and his followers, their bowing down, in suppliant sort, unto Moses and Aaron, and God's people, Exodus 11:8 & 12:31.

*{and lick up the dust of thy feet*} Or, stoop so low to you, as if they would even lick up the dust under your feet; an expression of the lowest submission that may be: they shall deem no office too mean, wherein they may be helpful and useful to God's church; or whereby they may testify their high estimation of God's ordinances in it, together with their free and full subjection, and entire submission thereunto. And it is an allusion, to the peculiar manner of the Persian adoration, with whom the manner was anciently in worshiping their kings, to kiss their very footsteps, or those places of the pavement on which, their feet did stand, or had stood, see Psalm 89:51 & 99:5. Howbeit, because the phrase is elsewhere used of persons subdued, and so brought under; some would have it rather meant of such princes, before spoken of, as were conquered by the Jewish armies. See Psalm 72:9 & 110:1, Malachi 4:2, but nothing hinders, but that in a spiritual sense, it may be understood as before, Psalm 45:5 and 66:3 & 110:1,2.

*{and thou shalt know that I am the Lord*} You shall, by due proof, and experience, find, that I am the true God Jehovah, able, to perform and make good all my promises to you, Ezekiel 36:38 & 37:14,28, Revelation 3:9.

*{for they shall not be ashamed, that wait for me*} Or, *and that* (as chapter 38:7.) *they shall not be ashamed, that wait on me.* Or, as some, *on whom, those that wait, shall not be ashamed of me.* Or, *shall not be ashamed:* For in the first person, sometime, such speeches run, as Genesis 45:4, chapter 37:21. See on verse 7. The meaning is, that it shall evidently be made to appear, that whosoever they be, that, through faith and patience, expect me, and salvation to be wrought by me, chapter 8:17 & 28:16 & 30:18, Luke 2:25,38, their hopes and expectations, being never frustrated, shall never shame them, Psalm 9:10 & 25:3 & 34:22, Romans 5:5 & 9:33, as the hopes and expectations of all those shall do, that rely and depend upon any other besides me, Psalm 20:7,8, chapter 20:5 & 30:5,7.

**V. 24.** *{Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?*} A twofold objection is here met with, that might be made against this promised delivery of God's people; and a twofold plea, that their adversaries might allege, for the detention of them still, with them, Jeremiah 50:33, the one, taken from their might; that they were able enough to detain them: the other, from their right, they had a due interest in them; being lawfully possessed of them by law of arms, and right of conquest, Genesis 48:22, Judges 11:21–23, unto both which, God returns answer, in the next verse, but pitching mainly upon the former.

*{prey be taken*} There is, in the Hebrew, an elegancy of sound in the words, as if it were said; *Shall from the mighty their taking be taken?* For as we use the word, *takings,* for *gain,* gotten by trade and traffic; so do the Hebrews the word of *taking,* for prey, or booty, taken in war, Numbers 31:11,12. So, *the taking of the terrible,* verse 25.

*{the lawful captive*} Hebrew, *the captivity of the just.* See Jeremiah 50:7.

**V. 25.** *{But*} Or, *yet;* as chapter 31:4.

*{thus saith the Lord*} In way of answer, or counterplea, unto the enemies' allegations; to give ground of comfort and assurance of deliverance to his people.

*{The captives of the mighty shall be taken away*} Hebrew, *captivity*, as verse 24, Psalm 126:1.

*{and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered*} Hebrew, *the taking of the terrible:* as verse 24. No power of any shall be able to detain what God will have to be re-delivered, and restored, chapter 43:6, Jeremiah 51:44.

*{and I will contend with him, that contendeth with thee*} Hebrew, *I will contend with he shall contend thee: with he shall contend,* (a defect of the relative, as chapter 47:11.) for, *with him, that shall,* or *with whoso shall contend thee,* that is, *contend with thee,* as, *dwell thee,* for, *dwell with thee,* Psalm 5:4, so also, chapter 7:8. Howbeit, the word may be (as some make it) not a verb, but a verbal, and then it is word for word, *with thy contender:* as the plural, from such a form, is used, Psalm 35:1, Jeremiah 18:19. Whether way we take it, (and this latter seems the more expedite) it is delivered in the singular number, to assure them of protection against any whosoever, that should offer to be meddling, or quarreling with them. So Genesis 12:3, Psalm 35:1, chapter 41:11 & 50:8,9, and this seems to have some reference to the latter part of the enemies' plea, concerning their pretended right, verse 24, as undertaking also, to clear that against them, in behalf of his people, though there were no other to do it for them, chapter 51:22, Micah 7:9, as if he had said; I will debate with them, in your behalf, and put them beside their groundless claim, Jeremiah 50:34 & 51:36. See God himself so doing, chapter 52:3–5.

*{and I will save thy children*} Jeremiah 30:10.

**V. 26.** *{And I will feed them, that oppress thee, with their own flesh; and they they shall be drunk with their own blood, as with sweet wine*} I will cause them to destroy one another, and shed the blood of each other, as eagerly, and greedily, as if it were meat and drink to them; yea, the most delightful drink to them, that could be, to be making havoc of, and spilling the blood, either of other. Thus God had, at divers times, formerly done, Judges 7:23, 1 Samuel 14:20, 2 Chronicles 20:23, and the like he threatens, as to the Egyptians, chapter 19:2, so here, to other the enemies, and oppressors of his people, those nations, that had served under the Chaldeans, against them, one by another, 2 Kings 24:2, and the Chaldeans also, by factions, and divisions amongst themselves. For Xenophon reports, that many of the Chaldeans fell off from the Babylonian king, and joined themselves to Cyrus, and were of the forwardest, both in the surprisal of the city, and of the king's palace especially, where they slew him themselves, and all that were about him. For that which some would have to be hereby intimated, of the Babylonians feeding one upon another for famine, during the siege of their city, is of no probability; since that, as Herodotus reports, they had laid in abundance of victual before, as expecting a far longer siege than it proved; and on that very day, wherein the city was taken, they had a great general feasting, both in public, and private, throughout the whole city, as those two writers both record. See on Jeremiah 51:39,57. See also the like judgment, to that here mentioned, chapter 9:20.

*{them that oppress thee*} So most render it, *thine oppressors;* as coming from a verb, that signifies to oppress, Ezekiel 18:10 & 22:7. See chapter 51:23, yet some of the Jewish critics, and others after them, render it, *thy numberers,* or *those that numbered thee;* as coming of a word, that signifies *to number, reckon,* or keep account: as it is used, Psalm 147:4, those that *numbered thee out to the sword,* as God himself speaks, chapter 65:11, and they suppose it to have some reference, either unto such officers, as are appointed to take tale of captives, or prisoners; such as the *field-marshal,* chapter 33:18. Or, as some of them to those that take tale of sheep, or other cattle, Jeremiah 33:13, (where the word also is read) & Ezekiel 20:37, and this way they turn it the rather, because God's people are called his *sheep.* See on verse 11. But the numbering of cattle looks another way; and the former sense seems the plainer, and better.

*{drunk with blood*} A phrase used of blood in great abundance shed, chapter 34:5–7, by such especially, as much desire it, and take delight in it, Revelation 14:10 & 16:6.

*{as with sweet wine*} Such, as with the pleasantness of it, entices men to drink much: the word seems to signify, in the first place, *new wine,* or *must,* as newly *trodden out,* coming of a word that so signifies, Malachi 4:2, and in the next place, *sweet wine,* because the new is usually such, Jeremiah 1:5 & 3:18, Amos 9:13. See chapter 62:6.

*{and all flesh shall know, that I the Lord am thy Savior, thy Redeemer, the mighty one of Jacob*} So remarkable shall your deliverance be and the destruction of your enemies so strange that all people shall take notice of a special hand of your God in it. See chapter 60:16.

*{all flesh*} As chapter 40:5.

*{the mighty one*} So called here, in opposition to the mighty ones, before mentioned, verse 24.
